Title: b'Feature Request: Break up Paragraphs in the way that they appear in a document instead of fixed split_length'
Body:
b'### Discussed in https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/discussions/3464

@ZanSara 

Summary: Add in a feature to the Haystack PreProcessor that will be able to split paragraphs in the way that they appear in the document, potentially by the`\n` or `\f` special characters or both. This  way, a document will get split not by a fixed split_length but rather by the length of the paragraph in the document itself.

Use Case: In many cases, one may need to preserve the structure of a paragraph as it appears in the document. If you split a document by a fixed size, the paragraph y that appears after paragraph x may be included in x and it may not make any sense at all as x and y may be talking about two different things.'

Title: b'anakin87'
Body:
b'While thinking about #3447, I decided to revamp this issue.

## Document store and retrievers
From what I understood, in Haystack:
- document stores: should store documents and their representations (such as embeddings)
- retrievers: should be used to query the document stores, in order to provide the most relevant documents
(currently, in some cases, they also build document representations that are then saved to a document store. See #2403)

This holds true for most of the cases, with some exceptions:
- graphs: in the current implementations, they combine the features of a document store and a retriever
- TF-IDF retriever: it uses a document store as a source, but it builds an internal representation for documents (based on a `DataFrame` and a `TfidfVectorizer`)

## How to make the TF-IDF retriever to support different indexes (accept the `index` parameter)?
I see two alternative options:
- find a way to store the representation in the document store
clean from a logical point of view, but hard to implement since this retriever support several different document stores
- modify the current implementation of TF-IDF to create a representation for every index
simpler but dirtier

## Support for BM25Retriever in `InMemoryDocumentStore` (#3447)
It seems related to the same topics.
However, unlike TF-IDF, in Haystack BM25 is a pure retriever (it completely relies on document stores to save document representations).
Based on the proposals made to use external libraries (rank-bm25, gensim) it would seem that even in that case, we want to create a specific implementation of BM25 that builds its own internal representation of the documents...

Sorry if I misunderstood something...

@ZanSara @Timoeller WDYT?
'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b"Hey @anakin87! Great analysis, as usual! This is going to be useful even for me to explain the situation to others :rocket:

## Mandatory premise

So, first things first: I believe the current abstraction of Retrievers is fundamentally wrong. As you noticed, some Retriever rely fully on the docstore for the retrieval steps, others have their own internal representation stored (usually) in memory. The whole thing at some point will need to be re-evaluated and clarified (a topic already raised, as you noticed, in https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/2403) by assigning to document store, retrievers and embedders consistent and distinct responsibilities.

However, we need to get stuff done with the current architecture for now :sweat_smile: 

## How to make the TF-IDF retriever to support different indexes (accept the index parameter)?

>    - find a way to store the representation in the document store
>      clean from a logical point of view, but hard to implement since this retriever support several different document stores

Technically all docstores should support indices already, so this should not pose too many challenges. However, I have not verified this in practice.

>    - modify the current implementation of TF-IDF to create a representation for every index
>      simpler but dirtier

In case the first solution proves too tough, this is a viable alternative. it might make TFIDFRetriever slow as a snail on large collections, but honestly it's already slow in such conditions, so I don't see it as a big issue :sweat_smile: 

## Support for BM25Retriever in InMemoryDocumentStore (https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/3447)

> It seems related to the same topics.
> However, unlike TF-IDF, in Haystack BM25 is a pure retriever (it completely relies on document stores to save document representations).
> Based on the proposals made to use external libraries (rank-bm25, gensim) it would seem that even in that case, we want to create a specific implementation of BM25 that builds its own internal representation of the documents...

For as odd as it sounds, I think the main challenge of adding BM25 support to `InMemoryDocumentStore` is to figure out where to put the BM25 retrieval step. Currently I tend to believe it should be added as a method of `InMemoryDocumentStore`, which can then store the representation alongside the documents. `BM25Retriever` might remain almost unaffected. Please tag me early on in the PR if you decide to go for this, so we can review together how the implementation will look like.

I hope this is helpful, let me know if I forgot to address something!"

```python

The .fit() call in turn calls the document_store.get_all_documents() method [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/main/haystack/nodes/retriever/sparse.py#L429) which if not given an index will default to the document store's self.index, which is not correct in this case."

Title: b'FHardow'
Body:
b"Hey all
let me elaborate a little bit on 
```
@FHardow suspects that the stream request returns a 200 and an empty list before the documents are actually being fetched (@FHardow correct me if I didn't get this right).
```

I've issued the same call through postman ([document-stream](https://api.cloud.deepset.ai/docs#/document_store/get_all_documents_stream_api_v1_workspaces__workspace_name__indexes__index_name__documents_stream_post)), the call immediately returned a 200, but the stream data was loaded after ~15s. 
My guess is that the request is getting a 200 as response status code, but the json body at this point is empty. 
`document_store.get_all_documents()` gets a generator on the request data internally and will try to create a list out of it. This generator is probably exhausted and closed as there is no data at first. With that the function returns an empty list. 

"

Title: b"Move `document_store` argument to `retrieve` method instead of the Retriever's constructor"
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Retrievers' constructors require the `document_store` parameter to be created. While this may be ok for sparse retrievers, DPR, for example, requires loading models. And then, when I want to use the same retriever, but with a different document store, I have to create a new instance of it making all the models load again, which doesn't make any sense. 

At the same time constructors mostly just emit some warnings connected with the document store, and no other significant operations are executed.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

The best and most intuitive would be to move the `document_store` argument to the methods, which are directly operating on it (`retrieve`, `retrieve_batch`, etc). This way model operates on the data and does not depend on them.

To preserve the backward compatibility `document_store` argument can stay in the `__init__`, but each method will have then the `document_store=None` argument so that we can fall back to the constructor's object if no other is passed.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Another way would be to add the method to substitute the `DocumentStore` object. It can be done by substituting the attribute value, but the self-preserving instinct would tell any programmer not to change any object's internal values.

**Additional Context**

I have asked about the intentions of putting the `document_store` argument in the `__init__` on Haystack's Discord. And @masci  advised me to address this idea here as an issue."

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b'Hi @Goader thank you for making this suggestion and for describing it in so much detail.  We thought about improving the current coupling of retriever and document store in our team too. What do you think about the suggestion here @ZanSara @masci ?'

Title: b'masci'
Body: b'@julian-risch I think the solution proposed here could be implemented right ahead: users would get immediate benefit but the overall logic would stay the same, without affecting the long-term plan of revisiting the retriever/docstore design'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b"I agree that the current design doesn't make much sense and I'd really like to see this change... but I'm afraid it will break `Pipeline`. Unfortunately, the document store object right now is not passed along: `Pipeline` assumes that nodes that require access to the docstore will have their own internal way to access it, that's why Retrievers take it in their `__init__`. Making `retrieve()` take a `document_store` param would simply make Pipeline crash right now.

If we want to start from this angle, then we need also to make Pipeline aware that some nodes might require a document store and, if their `run` method asks for it, where to find it. It would mean that is no more Retrievers that takes a document store in their init, but `Pipeline`.

This is a _big_ shift unfortunately, but a very welcome one if you're up for the challenge. @masci do you have opinions here? Is it something we can target or does it sound too big? It is surely a delicate change. I'm of course open to other ideas if you have any. This is a tangled problem that can be approached from several angles right now."

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body: b"Ok, after a review of the code I realized that this is doable if we don't want to affect Pipelines at all. I'll go ahead and give it a try to see if my idea is correct. I'll link a PR soon."

Title: b'Add support for BM25Retriever in InMemoryDocumentStore'
Body:
b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Many of our tutorials are using the ElasticsearchDocumentStore. While this is a good choice for a production system, it can be quite cumbersome to set up and run during your "first minutes with haystack". It would be awesome to use the `InMemoryDocumentStore` instead for the first steps of users (Tutorial 1, Quick Start ...).  The only thing that I see holding us back here: `InMemoryDocumentStore` doesn't support our `BM25Retriever` which is a fast and easy retriever to get started with (and therefore a good choice in tutorials). Switching to another retriever might complicate tutorials, slow them down or reduce the quality of answers users get.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Supporting the usage of the `BM25Retriever` in combination with the `InMemoryDocumentStore`

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using TFIDFRetriever but I am concerned about the quality of results and leading our users into a wrong direction here.

**Priority**
I don't think this feature is urgent but it might be a helpful step when we want to improve the early user experience'

Title: b'Extract headings from Markdown files'
Body:
b"
**Describe the solution you'd like**
Markdown files tag headlines with the `#` character. Different levels of headings are marked by the number of `#` characters. We should use this information and add headline information to the documents metadata. This information might be used to improve retrieval, for example.

When adding this, we need to make sure in the PreProcessor's split method to keep only those headings that are relevant for each split."

```python
if self.answer is not None:

        # Set default before validation 
        no_answer = self.answer.answer == "" or self.answer.answer is None
        
    if no_answer == True:
        if self.answer.answer != "" or self.answer.context:

    elif no_answer == False:

from haystack.schema import Label, Answer, Document

# doesn't raise
label = Label(answer=Answer(answer="", context="some value"), query="test", document=Document("dasd"), is_correct_answer=True, is_correct_document=True, origin="user-feedback")

# raises but shouldn't
Label.from_dict(label.to_dict())

Title: b'`EmbeddingRetriever` assumes the title of the document is in a field of `meta` called `name`'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
- In `embed_documents`, `EmbeddingRetriever` assumes the title of the document is in a field of `meta` called `name`: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/7e79a4854085fc8fd5875266ec4ce466b8313197/haystack/nodes/retriever/_embedding_encoder.py#L189

**Expected behavior**
- The name of the field containing the title should be configurable.
- We should be able to configure which meta fields are embedded through the `embed_meta_fields` parameter.

**Additional context**
- https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/3252#discussion_r976248153

'

Title: b'anakin87'
Body:
b'Hey @ZanSara!

I think that this line is **superfluous** and indeed is probably wrong:
https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/6cb4e939653719698764b2e0ad379b0859f862be/haystack/nodes/retriever/_embedding_encoder.py#L214


In fact, before calling that method, in the `embed_documents` method (of the `EmbeddingRetriever`), `_preprocess_documents` is called and the meta fields indicated by `embed_meta_fields` are **concatenated there**.
https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/6cb4e939653719698764b2e0ad379b0859f862be/haystack/nodes/retriever/dense.py#L1838-L1868

So for now, if you have such a document:
```json
{"content": "mycontent",
"meta": {"name": "myname"}}
```
and you try to embed it with an `EmbeddingRetriever`, by specifying `embed_meta_fields=['name']`,
under the hood these are the passages to encode (sum of `_preprocess_documents` and `embed_documents`).
```python
[['myname', 'myname\ncontent']]
```
I verified that with some experiments.

### Possible solution
We can simply remove that line from `embed_documents` if you agree that the meta fields have already been concatenated in `_preprocess_documents`.
Do we want to provide some default value for `EmbeddingRetriever`'s `embed_meta_fields` attribute? Currently, it is an empty list.'

Body:
b"Hey @anakin87, wow, thank you for digging into this one.

So, although I don't believe this duplication benefits anyone, there might be parts of the code deep into the retriever that either assume the name will be in the first position of the list, and others that assume the name is already concatenated. My recommendation would be to proceed, remove the line, and then thoroughly test the resulting code. By this, I mean that we should make sure all tutorials run on it. If you can, running all tests locally would be also fantastic.

Title: b'anakin87'
Body:
b"While working on this, I noticed that currently there is a `generate_single_summary` parameter (default value is False).

Based on my experiments and the [docs](https://docs.haystack.deepset.ai/docs/pipelines#example-creating-a-retriever-ranker-summarizer-pipeline), I can say that if `generate_single_summary` is True, the result is only one document.
Its text is the summary, while the context is the sum of all the documents' texts.

It can make sense in querying pipelines.

**But now we want to leave the text unchanged and add the summary in a meta field**.
This seems appropriate both for querying and indexing pipelines.

An option could be:
if `generate_single_summary` is True, we leave the document texts unchanged
and add the same single summary to every single document.

@ZanSara @brandenchan WDYT? Any better ideas?

"

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b"Wow... Good point. You make a nice proposal, but I think we can do better :grin: 

I propose to remove the `generate_single_summary` feature altogether.

If users wants a single summary from all the retrieved documents, fine, I'd rather give them a node that merges small documents into bigger ones. We have the `PreProcessor` for splitting, let's make a small `DocumentMerger` for merging. It might come handy for other usecases as well. This makes `Summarizer` simpler and smaller, and gives us a new node with a simple and clear task that we can reuse.

You might need to update the documentation to clarify this change. I'm not sure there are tutorials involving this node, have a look."

Title: b'anakin87'

In any case, if you think it is the best thing, I proceed to the simplification proposed by you.
No tutorials involved, but several docs.'

If that's too much work to remove `generate_single_summary`, your original plan works too! Have a look and feel free to choose your way. Either is good for me :slightly_smiling_face: "

Title: b'brandenchan'
Body: b'So funnily enough I raised this issue in the first place because we wanted the docs to have real world use cases that are more realistic! The use case that we are aiming for is one where summaries are attached to all documents at index time so that after retrieval, documents can be displayed with their text or their summary.'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body: b"Ah cool, so this is more about the docs than the Summarizer itself! \r\n\r\nNow that we're at it, what do you think about the `generate_single_summary` removal? Title: b'Trouble with retriever filtering in dC'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
I had a standard retriever-reader pipeline on deepset Cloud with an embedding retriever (`top_k` = 10) and `roberta-large` reader model. The use case was standard QA, so lots of repeated queries filtering by various file IDs. When doing this we noticed that for many filtered queries the retriever wasn't returning any documents at all. After talking with @tstadel about this, here's my (somewhat limited) understanding of the problem - @tstadel please feel free to step in and correct any mistakes/gaps on my end.

For some reason, for the document stores used by dC (`OpenSearchDocumentStore`?) the filter is applied to the documents **returned by the retriever**, rather than the documents **fed into the retriever**. As a result, the retriever pulls the 10 top-scoring documents in the whole document store, and only then restricts these to those that meet the filter requirements. Hence, if none of those 10 meet the filter requirements (which will happen often) then the filtered retriever won't return anything. From what I gather, this is connected to a Haystack issue with OpenSearch, rather than some dC-specific bug.

@tstadel came up with a clever work-around for this: set the retriever to a very high `top_k` (e.g., 10000), and then insert a `JoinDocuments` node between the retriever and reader with `top_k_join` set to whatever the "real" `top_k` should be (e.g., 10). While this largely solves the problem in this particular case, it does lead to a slowdown (rough estimate: 2-3x) and is not ideal.


**Expected behavior**
Filtering happens before retrieval.


**To Reproduce**
Deploy a dC reader-retriever pipeline (or a retriever-reader pipeline with the same type of document store, parameters, etc.) and perform filtered queries. Haven't tested this, but presumably the more documents are in the document store the more likely it is that the bug will pop up.


**FAQ Check**
- [X] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?
'

Title: b'id_hash_keys is ignored'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
Passing `id_hash_keys` to an ingestion pipeline or individual nodes has no effect. For example given `id_hash_keys = ["meta"]` and two documents with different meta data, both will share the same id if the content is the same.

**Error message**
No error

**Expected behavior**
Generated document ids should be formed using a hash of the fields passed through the `id_hash_keys` parameter

**Additional context**
During debugging I've noticed that the Document constructor ignores the `id_hash_keys` parameter that is passed by the node e.g. a TextConverter node. This is possibly due to the issue with [mutable default parameters](https://stackoverflow.com/a/1145781/11571339) in Python.

For example try this code:

```python
# Different metadata

doc1 = Document(content="hello world", meta={'doc_id': '1'}, id_hash_keys=['meta'])
print(doc1.id)

doc2 = Document(content="hello world", meta={'doc_id': '2'}, id_hash_keys=['meta'])
print(doc2.id)
```

```
Output:
# Same generated ids
ab97467d60eb63b1533f6046eb7f610e
ab97467d60eb63b1533f6046eb7f610e
```

However if we explicitly pass all constructor arguments:

```Python
doc3 = Document("hello world", "text", None, None, {'doc_id': '3'}, None, ['meta'])
print(doc3.id)

doc4 = Document("hello world", "text", None, None, {'doc_id': '4'}, None, ['meta'])
print(doc4.id)
```
```
Output:
# Different generated ids
ee6af6c5a7999fae9b46a6c257fd957e
324d51b0738f74b683f7d69cbf2a58ef
```

Different ids are generated

**To Reproduce**
See above or try this code

```python
def ingest(meta_id):
    doc_store = InMemoryDocumentStore()
    
    # Pass id_hash_keys to the TextConverter
    text_converter = TextConverter(valid_languages=['en'], progress_bar=False, id_hash_keys=["meta", "content"])

    # Pass id_hash_keys to the PreProcessor
    pre_processor = PreProcessor(progress_bar=False, id_hash_keys=["meta", "content"])
    
    p = Pipeline()
    p.add_node(component=text_converter, name="TextConverter", inputs=["File"])
    p.add_node(component=pre_processor, name="PreProcessor", inputs=["TextConverter"])
    p.add_node(component=doc_store, name="DocumentStore", inputs=["PreProcessor"])
    
    # Pass id_hash_keys to the pipeline
    params = {
        "debug": True,
        "id_hash_keys": ["meta", "content"]
    }
    
    meta = {
        "meta_id": meta_id
    }
    
    result = p.run(file_paths=["./test_doc.txt"], meta=meta, params=params)
    # Final generated id
    doc = result['documents'][0]
    # TextConverter generated id
    debug = result["_debug"]['TextConverter']
    text_converter_id = debug['output']['documents'][0].id

    print("Meta id".ljust(20), meta_id)
    print("TextConverter id".ljust(20), text_converter_id)
    print("Generated id".ljust(20), doc.id)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    ingest("1")
    print("")
    ingest("2")
```

```
Output:

TextConverter id     3eddb872a053055e226cb754159e098e
Generated id           3eddb872a053055e226cb754159e098e

Meta id                    2

Title: b'Preprocessing: Warning when max doc length significantly exceeds preprocessor split length'
Body:
b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When running a retriever-reader pipeline, we noticed that certain inference times were much longer than others, and were even running into timeout problems. We thought this was odd, since we had a preprocessor splitting files into 250-word docs in order to avoid this. However, since `split_respect_sentence_boundary` was set to `True` by default, and since there were large passages in our files without a period (hence were parsed as a single sentence and not split by the preprocessor), this meant that some of the documents were much, much longer than 250 words (e.g., 62,000 words), hence the slowdown. It took us quite some time to figure this out, which admittedly falls partly on our shoulders, but it would have saved us considerable time and effort if we had received some sort of warning indicating that the max doc length in our document store was many multiples greater than the preprocessor's split length.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be helpful to receive some kind of warning whenever the max document length after preprocessing is significantly greater than the preprocessor's split length. (I don't have an exact definition of "significantly greater" pinned down; apologies for the imprecision.)
'

Title: b'ElasticSearch Document Store add Bulk parallel write method'
Body:
b'I have been playing with the library today and I need to insert around 1Millions documents in elastic search. 

I found that we have a `write_document` method that supports bulk writing and it takes around 25 minutes to insert my document in elastic search.

By searching, I found that elastic search has a `bluk_parrallel`  method which does bulk insert but in parallel, I was thinking it can be a good idea to have it implemented. 


The function is similar to the`write_document` but with some `bulk parallel

Here is what I am using.

```
def write_documents_parallel(
        self,
        documents: Union[List[dict], List[Document]],
        index: Optional[str] = None,
        batch_size: int = 10_000,
        duplicate_documents: Optional[str] = None,
        headers: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
    ):
        """
        Indexes documents for later queries in Elasticsearch./ an update for the index that use parallel bluk

        Behaviour if a document with the same ID already exists in ElasticSearch:
        a) (Default) Throw Elastic's standard error message for duplicate IDs.
        b) If `self.update_existing_documents=True` for DocumentStore: Overwrite existing documents.
        (This is only relevant if you pass your own ID when initializing a `Document`.
        If don't set custom IDs for your Documents or just pass a list of dictionaries here,
        they will automatically get UUIDs assigned. See the `Document` class for details)

        :param documents: a list of Python dictionaries or a list of Haystack Document objects.
                          For documents as dictionaries, the format is {"content": "<the-actual-text>"}.
                          Optionally: Include meta data via {"content": "<the-actual-text>",
                          "meta":{"name": "<some-document-name>, "author": "somebody", ...}}
                          It can be used for filtering and is accessible in the responses of the Finder.
                          Advanced: If you are using your own Elasticsearch mapping, the key names in the dictionary
                          should be changed to what you have set for self.content_field and self.name_field.
        :param index: Elasticsearch index where the documents should be indexed. If not supplied, self.index will be used.
        :param batch_size: Number of documents that are passed to Elasticsearch's bulk function at a time.
        :param duplicate_documents: Handle duplicates document based on parameter options.
                                    Parameter options : ( 'skip','overwrite','fail')
                                    skip: Ignore the duplicates documents
                                    overwrite: Update any existing documents with the same ID when adding documents.
                                    fail: an error is raised if the document ID of the document being added already
                                    exists.
        :param headers: Custom HTTP headers to pass to elasticsearch client (e.g. {'Authorization': 'Basic YWRtaW46cm9vdA=='})
                Check out https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/http-clients.html for more information.
        :raises DuplicateDocumentError: Exception trigger on duplicate document
        :return: None
        """

        if index and not self.client.indices.exists(index=index, headers=headers):
            self._create_document_index(index, headers=headers)

        if index is None:
            index = self.index
        duplicate_documents = duplicate_documents or self.duplicate_documents
        assert (
            duplicate_documents in self.duplicate_documents_options
        ), f"duplicate_documents parameter must be {', '.join(self.duplicate_documents_options)}"

        field_map = self._create_document_field_map()
        document_objects = [Document.from_dict(d, field_map=field_map) if isinstance(d, dict) else d for d in documents]
        document_objects = self._handle_duplicate_documents(
            documents=document_objects, index=index, duplicate_documents=duplicate_documents, headers=headers
        )
        documents_to_index = []
        for doc in tqdm(document_objects):
            _doc = {
                "_op_type": "index" if duplicate_documents == "overwrite" else "create",
                "_index": index,
                **doc.to_dict(field_map=self._create_document_field_map()),
            }  # type: Dict[str, Any]

            # cast embedding type as ES cannot deal with np.array
            if _doc[self.embedding_field] is not None:
                if type(_doc[self.embedding_field]) == np.ndarray:
                    _doc[self.embedding_field] = _doc[self.embedding_field].tolist()

            # rename id for elastic
            _doc["_id"] = str(_doc.pop("id"))

            # don't index query score and empty fields
            _ = _doc.pop("score", None)
            _doc = {k: v for k, v in _doc.items() if v is not None}

            # In order to have a flat structure in elastic + similar behaviour to the other DocumentStores,
            # we "unnest" all value within "meta"
            if "meta" in _doc.keys():
                for k, v in _doc["meta"].items():
                    _doc[k] = v
                _doc.pop("meta")
            documents_to_index.append(_doc)

            # Pass batch_size number of documents to bulk
            if len(documents_to_index) % batch_size == 0:
                pb_ = parallel_bulk(self.client, 
                              documents_to_index, 
                              chunk_size=10000, 
                              thread_count=8, 
                              queue_size=8,
                              refresh=self.refresh_type, 
                              headers=headers)
                deque(pb_, maxlen=0)
                documents_to_index = []

        if documents_to_index:
            pb_= parallel_bulk(self.client, 
                          documents_to_index, 
                          chunk_size=10000, 
                          thread_count=8, 
                          queue_size=8,
                          refresh=self.refresh_type, 
                          headers=headers)
            deque(pb_, maxlen=0)
```

Let me know what you guys think. 

If it seems okay, I can find some time over the weekend to submit a PR and support the hard work you are doing. But I may need someone to help in testing this.'

Title: b'Squishy-33'

> refresh_type: Type of ES refresh used to control when changes made by a request (e.g. bulk) are made visible to search.
                             If set to 'wait_for', continue only after changes are visible (slow, but safe).
                             If set to 'false', continue directly (fast, but sometimes unintuitive behavior when docs are not immediately available after ingestion).

However, on the elastic website, the default value is `false` and they say:

> Unless you have a good reason to wait for the change to become visible always use refresh=false, or, because that is the default, just leave the refresh parameter out of the URL. That is the simplest and fastest choice.`

Title: b'sjrl'

Title: b'Change BaseElasticsearchDocumentStore.query_batch() to allow for a full, flexible _msearch '
Body:
b'## **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
My existing application makes use of the [_msearch api](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/search-multi-search.html#search-multi-search-api-request-body) from Elasticsearch. This allows me to run multiple different queries, each on different indices, in one request. The results then get processed on the application side. 

I'd like to augment the searching with Haystack, whose `BaseElasticsearchDocumentStore.query_batch()` [function](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/main/haystack/document_stores/elasticsearch.py#L898) uses `msearch` and can receive multiple queries and filters, however you can only pass it one index as a string. If you omit the index, it gets set to `self.index`, which appears to default to `document`. This presumably prevents you from sending nothing/a blank string as the index parameter, which would then allow the ES request to look something like `GET _msearch`.

`query_batch()` then loops through the filters and queries that were passed in and appends them to the ES query body along with the header - this is almost sufficient for what I'd like to acheive, given that the headers parameter is a Dict. However, the headers parameter doesn't get looped through - the same value simply gets appended to each body.

Likewise, the `custom_query` parameter is just a string as well, meaning that I can't pass in different ES DSL queries for each index - instead I would have to create new Queries and Filters in Haystack's format, which is unnecessary work. 

## **Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like for `query_batch` to have the following characteristics/functionalities

1. be able to receive and pass along a blank `index` parameter
2. `custom_query` should be a List/Dict, which can be looped through just like the query and filters parameters
3. the `headers` Dict should be looped through and appended along with the corresponding body

This would ultimately allow for a singular query such as 

```
GET _msearch
{}
{"query" : {"match_all" : {}}, "from" : 0, "size" : 10}
{"index" : "my-index-000001"}
{"query" : {"match_all" : {}}}
{"index" : "my-index-000002"}
{"query" : {"match_all" : {}}}
```

I don't expect that this would have any impact on the rest of Haystack - ultimately it is just returning a list of `all_documents` which are to be processed elsewhere, presumably by custom application code. 

Given that you are already [planning to overhaul `run` and `run_batch`](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/2807) (and perhaps also `run_query` and `run_query_batch` while you're at it?), I hope that you'll consider doing the same for `query` and `query_batch`, ultimately streamlining it all with fewer but more flexible functions.

## **Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using a loop in my application to send each query individually and store the results in an array which can then be processed further outside of the loop. This would clearly be less performant - `msearch `exists for a reason.'

Title: b'Bad Semaphore initialization in RequestLimiter'
Body:
b"**Describe the bug**
RequestLimiter takes a number as parameter and use it to set up a Semaphore. The issue is that the environment variable indicates the concurrent allowed requests per worker. When the semaphore is created (https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/6790eaf7d8be05c5674d97a75cc5783e00a66875/rest_api/rest_api/controller/utils.py#L13), this value is set down by 1. This is clearly not what the project tried to achieve (at least per naming). 

**Error message**
REST API will always return it's busy, error 503 when CONCURRENT_REQUEST_PER_WORKER is equal to CONCURRENT_REQUEST_PER_WORKER -1. When user set the concurrency to 1, it will never be able to call the API, since the Semaphore declaration will be Semaphore(0)

Title: b"`FilterRetriever` doesn't have an `__init__()` function"
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
`FilterRetriever` inherits from `BM25Retriever`, just like his predecessor and deprecated `ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever` did. But `FilterRetriever` doesn't have an `__init__()` function and that messes up the config of the node when doing `node.get_config()` when the node it's within a pipeline.

**To Reproduce**

In order for this script to work, you need to have an Elasticsearch instance running.

```python
from haystack.nodes.retriever import ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever, FilterRetriever
from haystack import Pipeline
from haystack.document_stores.elasticsearch import ElasticsearchDocumentStore
es_endpoint="127.0.0.1"
es_port=9200
index = "test_documents"
document_store = ElasticsearchDocumentStore(
    host=es_endpoint, port=es_port, similarity="dot_product", index=index
)
filter_retriever = FilterRetriever(document_store=document_store)
es_retriever = ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever(document_store=document_store)
p = Pipeline()
p.add_node(filter_retriever, name="FilterRetriever", inputs=["Query"])
print(p.get_config())
# {'document_store': <class 'inspect._empty'>, 'top_k': 10, 'all_terms_must_match': False, 'custom_query': None, 'scale_score': True}
# {'components': [{'name': 'FilterRetriever', 'type': 'FilterRetriever', 'params': {}}], 'pipelines': [{'name': 'query', 'nodes': [{'name': 'FilterRetriever', 'inputs': ['Query']}]}], 'version': '1.9.0'}

p_2 = Pipeline()
p_2.add_node(es_retriever, name="es_retriever", inputs=["Query"])
print(p_2.get_config())
# {'components': [{'name': 'ElasticsearchDocumentStore', 'type': 'ElasticsearchDocumentStore', 'params': {'host': '127.0.0.1', 'index': 'test_documents'}}, {'name': 'es_retriever', 'type': 'ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever', 'params': {'document_store': 'ElasticsearchDocumentStore'}}], 'pipelines': [{'name': 'query', 'nodes': [{'name': 'es_retriever', 'inputs': ['Query']}]}], 'version': '1.6.0'}
```

As you can see, `FilterRetriever` doesn't have any `params` but `ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever` has the `document_store` as param.
'

Title: b'BaseRetriever checks `query` is passed using `not query` instead of `query is not None`'
Body:
b'I am using the [FilterRetriever](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/9582a423a2f4826a4a15529b72fea45da611b81c/haystack/nodes/retriever/sparse.py#L344) node which doesn't use the query that the user has to pass at all, just the filters to get filtered documents from the document store.

So I was following the advice in the [docstring of the class](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/9582a423a2f4826a4a15529b72fea45da611b81c/haystack/nodes/retriever/sparse.py#L363) where it says: `:param query: Has no effect, can pass in empty string`.

So I passed an empty string and I got the following error:

```shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test.py", line 44, in <module>
    docs = retriever.run(
  File ".../python3.8/site-packages/haystack/nodes/retriever/base.py", line 274, in run
    raise HaystackError(
haystack.errors.HaystackError: Must provide a 'query' parameter for retrievers in pipelines where Query is the root node.
``` 

This error happens because, in the [BaseRetriever](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/9582a423a2f4826a4a15529b72fea45da611b81c/haystack/nodes/retriever/base.py#L49) class, the parameter `query` is checked with the following statement:

https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/9582a423a2f4826a4a15529b72fea45da611b81c/haystack/nodes/retriever/base.py#L271

That is a bad way of checking if a parameter is passed because **that statement will also be true for an empty string**. The default value is None, so if the parameter is not passed then it should be checked with:

```python
if query is None:
```

As a **workaround**, a string with a space in it could be added:

```python
query = " "
```

### This happens in other classes with other variables too (as far as I know), so I would strongly recommend checking other classes as well'

Title: b'Update the PineconeDocumentStore'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Pinecone recently [released a new update](https://www.pinecone.io/docs/release-notes/#june-7-2022) that changes a few things for the better when integrating with Haystack.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
There are two important features:
1. **Selective metadata filtering** - using this we no longer need to host a local SQL instance to hold larger metadata (like document content). This is perfect because it simplifies the integration and makes everything easier for the user.
2. **Unary queries** - Pinecone always accepted batch queries, this feature isn't being deprecated and replaced with unary queries. I believe Haystack only supports unary queries, so this is better aligned. Additionally, the response from the Pinecone client has changed, so anyone using the latest version of the `pinecone-client` will see:

Title: b'Using multiple indices in FAISS seems broken'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
I'm trying to use FAISS document store and want to store multiple use cases in the same document store, i.e. specify different "index" during writing and querying. Everything works as expected for the first index I create, but for the subsequent ones, the query results are unexpectedly limited. 

I looked into it, and I think what's happening is: 

in the FAISS db, documents in each new index are keyed by vector_id, and this gets reset to 0 in each index. However, in the SQL db, the "vector_id" key isn't reset to 0 for each index. So when `get_documents_by_vector_ids` gets called with the vector_id's from the FAISS lookup, you get the wrong results, and most likely no results at all, when querying any of the subsequently created indices.

**Error message**
No error

**Expected behavior**
The vector ids in the SQL db should match those in the FAISS db for a given index.

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here, like document types / preprocessing steps / settings of reader etc.

**To Reproduce**

```python
from haystack.document_stores import FAISSDocumentStore
from haystack.nodes import EmbeddingRetriever
from haystack.pipelines import DocumentSearchPipeline
document_store = FAISSDocumentStore(sql_url="sqlite://", similarity='cosine', embedding_dim=384)
retriever = EmbeddingRetriever(document_store=document_store, embedding_model='sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2')
pipeline = DocumentSearchPipeline(retriever)                   

#vector_id's in the SQL db vs FAISS db (maybe not exact order)
document_store.write_documents([{"content":"dogs are great"},  #vector_id:0 vs 0
                                {"content":"dogs are OK"},      #vector_id:1 vs 1
                                {"content":"cats are awful"}],    #vector_id:2 vs 2
                                    index="index1")
document_store.write_documents([{"content":"I love cake"},       #vector_id:3 vs 0
                                {"content":"I like cake"},     #vector_id:4 vs 1
                                {"content":"I hate cake"}],    #vector_id:5 vs 2
                                index="index2")

document_store.update_embeddings(retriever, index="index1")
document_store.update_embeddings(retriever, index="index2")

print(len(pipeline.run("I love dogs", params={"Retriever": {"index": "index1", "top_k":1}})['documents']))
# => 1 
print(len(pipeline.run("I like cake", params={"Retriever": {"index": "index2", "top_k":1}})['documents']))
# => 0
```

**System:**

 - GPU/CPU: CPU
 - Haystack version (commit or version number): 1.9.0

 - Reader: None
 - Retriever: EmbeddingRetriever

### Current bug
It is caused by `vector_id = sum(index.ntotal for index in self.faiss_indexes.values()) `.
In fact, in `update_embeddings`, `index2` is reset, but `vector_id` starts from 3, making the retrieval ineffective.

### Possible solutions
If you agree that `vector_id` may not be unique, a quite easy solution is to revert #1961.

In any case, I am eager to hear your opinion and I am ready for the challenge of opening a PR :smile:
@ZanSara any thoughts? 


"

Title: b'julian-risch'

b'Hi @Akshayextreme thank you for reporting this bug. When the YAML file is loaded, Haystack tries to validate the content of the file against a schema. I assume that this validation fails because the content of the `custom_query` field contains special characters that usually do not occur in other parts of a YAML file, such as {,",$,*,]. 
If you are on the latest version of the main branch, I think only the $ and * are causing the problem. If you use Haystack v1.9.0 or older than also the other characters are problematic. 
@bogdankostic @mathislucka We worked on a similar issue recently but I am afraid that our fix in https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/3345 doesn't work for the `custom_query` field as in the example here:
```

  params:

      "AUTO"}}}, "highlight": {"fields": {"content": {}}, "pre_tags": ["**"], "post_tags":

    document_store: ElasticsearchDocumentStore
  type: BM25Retriever
```'

Title: b'bogdankostic'

Title: b'Additional metrics: MRR, nDCG and ROUGE for Pipeline evaluation'
Body:
b'Hi everyone!

In a meeting with @Timoeller , I had proposed to add more evaluation metrics commonly used in Information Retrieval *(IR)* (MRR, nDCG) and in Query Rewriting *(QR)* (ROUGE-1). This would make Haystack more suitable for researchers researching *QR* in Question Answering pipelines like in this publication by [Vakulenko](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2101.07382v1.pdf).

**Proposed solution**
Instead of implementing MRR, nDCG ourselves, we could use [metric-eval](https://pypi.org/project/metrics-eval/#description) or [pytrec-eval](https://github.com/cvangysel/pytrec_eval). The former claims to have a performance increase over the latter. However, pytrec-eval is created/published by researchers of University of Amsterdam [paper](http://128.84.4.18/pdf/1805.01597).
For ROUGE, we could use an implementation by Google [rouge-score](https://pypi.org/project/rouge-score/)

I was wondering on what would be the best way/place to implement the metrics giving #904 . 

Looking forward to your feedback,
'

Title: b'Timoeller'
Body:
b'Hey @giguru thanks for creating this detailed concept about adding eval metrics. 

About metrics for ranking: [metric-eval](https://github.com/AmenRa/metrics_eval) seems cool, Im unsure if it is battle tested enough. I really like your suggestion for pytrec-eval. It is based on the metrics used at TREC conference IR workshops, so I would assume those metrics are correct.

The ROUGE project by google seems good. Also HFs rouge metric use this repo under the hood.

For the best way to implement the metrics with our refactoring we should ask @brandenchan for guidance - he is working on the refactor.

'

Title: b'brandenchan'
b'giguru'
Body:
b"Hi Branden, thank you for your reponse. My focus is on Conversational QA (ConvQA) and Conversational Search, but very often working with open-domain datasets (e.g. Wikipedia dump).

Do you mean replacing  [`Label`](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/32050fdce3cc6d55ed744e2475b8c2dcee2edd4b/haystack/schema.py#L80) properties 'answer' and 'document_id' with `reader` and `retriever` respectively?

Since we have the JoinNode, I was thinking about the support of long/complex pipeline like this:
Query --> `Some Retriever` --> `EvalRetriever` (1)
Query --> `Other Retriever` --> `EvalRetriever` (2)
`JoinResults (1) and (2)` -> `EvalRetriever` -> `Reader `--> `EvalReader`.

If EvalRetriever can support this, users can debug their complex pipelines more easily, because every retriever can be evaluated independently.

**Alternative solution**
I think `Label.answer` can function as the label.reader from the dictionary in your post. And if we expand `document_id = Optional[str]` to `document_id = Optional[Union[str, List[str]]]` it can function as the label.retriever property from the dictionary in your post. This would be more backwards compatible, I think.

Do you think this is a good solution? Or am I misunderstanding your proposal?"

Title: b'brandenchan'
Body:
b'Hey @giguru, I have a working draft of the evaluation pipeline in #904. It might be a bit easier to explain what I mean by referring to this. The starting point is the `haystack/pipeline_eval.py` file. As previously mentioned, the pipeline looks like this
 ```
 Query --> Retriever --> EvalRetriever --> Reader --> EvalReader
```
`EvalRetriever` expects 2 arguments when its `run()` method is called: `documents` and `labels`. Sorry if I confused you a little earlier because I wasn't very clear, but I am proposing that this `labels` argument should be a dictionary, and not a `haystack.Label` object. 

In the above pipeline, if we want to evaluate both `Retriever` and `Reader` in the same run, the same `labels` object needs to contain gold labels for both the Retriever and the Reader. So my proposal here is that it has something like this structure.

```
labels = {
    'reader': 'text answer to the question',
    'retriever': {
        'doc_2': 1,
        'doc_3': 1,
    }
}
```
I have no strong requirements about the format of `labels["reader"]` and `labels["retriever"]` and so I'm happy to leave it flexible for now. With this I think we should be able to do the 4 different stages of evaluation that you propose! `labels["reader"]` will be consumed by the one instance of `EvalReader` and `labels["retriever"]` will be consumed by the 3 instances of `EvalRetriever`. Here you can use the other metric libraries to calculate what's needed. 

I hope this makes sense and I haven't misunderstood you. Let me know if there's anything that should be clarified!'

Title: b'giguru'
Body: b"Sorry for misunderstanding. It is clear now. Your proposed solution is perfect then! Your `labels` argument will give the flexibility   to expand it later. I'm working on a QueryRewriter in #929, which would require another key in that dict."

Title: b'QA inferencer very slow because of bad default multiprocessing settings'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
When doing pipeline.eval I realized that it is very slow and also outputs way too many lines of tqdm.
That is why I tested it with and without multiprocessing. My results are incredible:

MP on 
Elapsed: 22.35

MP off
Elapsed: **6.079**


**To Reproduce**
I benchmarked the pipeline.eval function on a V100 with only 10 labels + retriever topk 10
with FARMReaders num_processes parameter set to 0 (disable MP) or None (use all available processes)

**additional insights**
I think the problematic part is in the FARMReader.predict methods that calls:
```       
        predictions = self.inferencer.inference_from_objects(
            objects=inputs, return_json=False, multiprocessing_chunksize=1
        )
```
Since the multiprocessing_chunksize is hard coded to 1 it will split up all data, even when it is very few data, and feed this one by one to the GPU. This results in tiny batches and therefore bad GPU utilization for basically all retriever + reader usage... 
'

Title: b'Support FAISS in OpenSearch'
Body:
b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
FAISS comes with very efficient and reliable ANN algorithms that would allow scaling up the number of docs for dense retrieval.

Approximate KNN search can be configured via index mappings and settings:
https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/search-plugins/knn/knn-index/

We can split it into the following sub issues:
- [x] support HNSW for dot product and l2 (S)
    - add param `knn_engine` with default "nmslib" to construtor
    - use the same hnsw params as for nmslib
- [x] check whether existing index supports the requested method (S)
    - throw or fallback to exact knn
- [x] support HNSW for cosine (M)
    - normalize vectors manually
    - use dot_product space under the hood
    - https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/3217
- [ ] support product quantization (S)
    - add param `product_quantization_subvectors` with default value None
    - if not None `pq` is activated with `m=product_quantization_subvectors`
    - omit `code_size` for now as it is only supported with IVF
- [ ] support IVF (S)
    - add `ivf` option to `index_type` constructor param
    - use default values
    - support product quantization'

Title: b'FARMReader parallelism issues'
Body:
b"**Describe the bug**
When running FARMReader, without a GPU, it spawns the inferencers, start processing, but suddenly all process goes to 0% CPU usage, and it never returns any results. I noticed that despise it spawning 7 inferencers, it's using just 1 CPU core. 

This has been tested on a notebook, and on 3 Azure instances.

When using TransformersReader, the same setup (models, instances, document stores), the Reader spawns 7 inferencers, but 7 CPU cores get fully used. Results appears under 11m5s.

**Error message**
FARMReader get in a deadlock state

**Expected behavior**
Reader should use all CPU cores (it's not limited by any command), like TransformersReader, and should return results

**Additional context**


**To Reproduce**
Create a DocumentStore, create a BM25Retriever, crete a FARMReader, use ExtractiveQA pipeline to run the prediction query.

**FAQ Check**
- [x] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?

**System:**
 - OS: Ubuntu
 - GPU/CPU: i7 and Xeon
 - Haystack version (commit or version number): 1.9.0
 - DocumentStore: OpenSearchDocumentStore
 - Reader: FARMReader
 - Retriever: BM25Retriever
"

Title: b'Benchmark Haystack components'
Body:
b'We want to measure the performance of each "family" of Haystack components: Document Stores, Retrievers and Reader with different models, both standalone (when possible) and within pipelines. The goal is twofold:
- allow users to take informed decisions when they design Haystack pipelines
- identify bottlenecks and performance regressions

A possible solution might be hosting multiple real-world production setups using meaningful pipeline and models.

## Desired Outcomes

- [ ] Define a reference environment (CPU and memory size, GPU, disk)
- [ ] Automatically deploy a QA pipeline on a reference environment every day, using the unstable version of Haystack
- [ ] Run several queries and measure the time spent overall and on each step of the pipeline
- [ ] Make the results available so that they can be published on the internet (e.g. docs website)

As a next step, we could measure more and different pipelines grouping them as solutions, to allow user to easily access the ideal setup for each use case along with performance considerations.'

Title: b'Simpler deployment'
Body:
b"### What?
Guide / template to deploy on AWS / Kubernetes

### Why?
Road to production from an experimental environment should be simplified.

### How?
- create a simple helm chart for AWS EKS that anybody can deploy via AWS console
- this helm start works as a starting point to make more complex deployments happen (e.g. scaling, different k8s flavour, different ingress)
- find a way to deliver helm chart (registry is just a http server)
- write a guide in our documentation how to use it

### To be refined
- MVP is AWS/Kubernetes deployment? Yes, we use Helm Charts. There are various advantages compared to docker-compose like k8s' scaling, resilience and deployment capabilities. Additionally, K8s has become defacto-standard for deployment.
- Is ray too complex here? Yes, might be another Epic.
- Do we want to support other environments (like Azure, Google Cloud)? Yes, Helm Chart should be compatible with other Kubernetes flavours
- Are there more things to be considered if pipelines get more complex than say a basic Retriever-Reader-Pipeline? 
  - GPU allocation
- Can we generate Helm charts from docker-compose.yaml? No, helm is more specific. Helm charts created by kompose are too basic (e.g. pods instead of deployments, no ingress)

### Misc

pipeline.add_node(component=retriever_3, name="Retriever3", inputs=["Query"])
pipeline.add_node(component=retriever_4, name="Retriever4", inputs=["Query"])

Title: b'EmbeddingRetriever does not account for longer documents'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
The EmbeddingRetriever does not account for long sequences. More precisely, it passes on the documents to the underlying encoder model (sentence-transformer) which truncates the sequence before embedding. 

As such, 
i) The embedding isn't based on the full document and 
ii) Multiple documents can have the same embedding if they have the same starting sequence up to the max-len of the model.

Note: Also the case for tableQA 

**Expected behavior**
- Short-term: a relevant warning message. 
- Long-term: some way to natively handle long documents. 

From: @sjrl 
> I believe as @ju-gu mentioned it would be helpful to add a warning message when passing documents to the embedding retriever that are longer than the max_seq_length supported by the loaded Embedding model. This would be very similar to the warning that is thrown by the FARMReader (I think just during training) which warns the user that the texts being passed to the reader are being truncated.
>
> We also discussed offline in Slack alternatives to using truncation. For example, for each long documents we could split into smaller text chunks, pass each chunk into the EmbeddingRetriever, and then pool (e.g. mean or max) the embeddings together. This post [here](https://towardsdatascience.com/how-to-do-average-and-max-word-embedding-for-long-sentences-f3531e99d998) explains the concept well but falls short in actually evaluating how well the new embedding vectors perform.

> This would allow us to create a single embedding that "represents" the whole document. However, as @mathislucka pointed out this is not how the embedding retriever models were trained and does not seem to have good benchmarks for testing this in NLP communities.
> 
> Additional resources:
> 
> - Discussion in Sentence Transformers about this topic where they mention that they also use something like mean pooling for larger texts: https://github.com/UKPLab/sentence-transformers/issues/364#issuecomment-706632145
> - [Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer ](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.05150)Another potential alternative could be to support the Longformer which was built to embed longer documents. This model type is supported in HuggingFace and the docs page can be found for it here: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/longformer
> - BigBird was also developed to handle longer texts. HuggingFace link here: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/big_bird

**To Reproduce**
[This Colab Notebook](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/13DS_Dd50nHuEuBhXYmgBMEyIszZMD0fI?usp=sharing).

'

Title: b'Replace multiprocessing tokenization with batched fast tokenization'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Tokenization based on multiprocessing (DataSilo) dates back to an era of pure Python tokenizers that were significantly slower than modern, fast Rust-based tokenizers. The current use of multiprocessing in Haystack originates from a goal to tokenize the text content faster. However, with the onset of fast tokenizers and batched text processing, these multiprocessing remnants create more issues than benefits. There were user reports on how using certain recent torch releases multiprocessing tokenization causes blockages in tokenization. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We should replace all multiprocessing code related to text tokenization with fast tokenizers using large batches of text. For more background and the rationale for use of fast tokenizers with large batches see https://huggingface.co/course/chapter6/3

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatives are limited


**Todo**
I propose that we simply remove multiprocessing code in datasilo and rely on multi-threading in Rust based fast tokenizers instead of multiprocessing. In order to utilize Rust multi-threading, the passages we pass to tokenizers should be longer lists of text batches. Of course, as we already used fast tokenizers, single process, multi-threaded fast tokenization will not be as fast but we'll make sure that it is not unnecessarily slow.   We'll also remove all deprecated `batch_encode_plus`, `encode_plus` with tokenizer ` __call__` method. 
"

Title: b'tstadel'
Body:
b"Hey @Taekyoon,
FAISSDocumentStore is a little special here. Under the hood it contains a sql database and a FAISS index. The sql database needs to be backed by file storage all the time, so it is stored automatically. The FAISS index on the other hand lives entirely in-memory and there is no automatic saving to disk taking place. That's why FAISSDocumentStore has the `save()` method. This will write the FAISS index to disk. Furthermore you also have to load the previously stored FAISS index explicitly again. This works by calling the `load()` class method or passing `faiss_index_path` to the constructor. So you would basically first have to check whether there is a stored FAISS index on disk and decide if you want to create a new FAISSDocumentStore or use an existing one like:

```
if os.path.exists(configs.faiss_index_path):
    document_store = FAISSDocumentStore.load(configs.faiss_index_path)
else:
    document_store = FAISSDocumentStore(vector_dim=configs.hidden_dims, faiss_index_factory_str=configs.faiss_index)
```"

Title: b'Add MultipleNegativesRankingLoss for EmbeddingRetriever training with sentence-transformers'
Body:
b'Currently training `EmbeddingRetriever` with sentence-transformer uses the `MarginMSE` loss. We want to also support `MultipleNegativesRankingLoss` which can work with a simpler data requirement, particularly it doesn't necessitate a "score" for the data pairs/tuples.

Related discussion: deepset-ai/haystack-tutorials#35 

## Background and Related work

deepset-ai/haystack#2388 added the ability to train `EmbeddingRetriever` (sentence-transformer variant) with Generative Pseudo Labeling (GPL). It uses `MarginMSE` loss with labels coming from a soft pseudo-labeling process. [Example Colab notebook](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1Tz9GSzre7JfvXDDKe7sCnO0FMuDViMnN?usp=sharing).

Input data is then of the format:

```
[
{question: , pos_doc: , neg_doc: , score: }, 
... 
]
```

It works well. However, there can be cases where users want to directly move onto the retriever training from their data without the pseudo-labeling or some other intermediate process to come up with the scores. 

Supporting the use of [MultipleNegativesRankingLoss](https://www.sbert.net/docs/package_reference/losses.html#multiplenegativesrankingloss)(MNRL) can provide such an option.

## Proposal

Provide an argument (maybe a string or directly the loss class from `sentence-transformers`) to the `EmbeddingRetriever#train` method to allow for selection between the two losses. Data checks could be added to make sure the loss choice and data formats are compatible. 

For MNRL, the format would be as below (with the `neg_doc` also being optional).

```
[
{question: , pos_doc: , neg_doc: }, 
... 
]
```

## Next up

I'll open a draft PR and start working on this. Fine implementation details can be worked out there. In the meantime, if there are any thoughts, please drop them here. 
cc: @mkkuemmel @mathislucka @vblagoje '

Title: b'tanaysoni'

In the next weeks, we plan to improve the confidence scores/probabilities for answers in Haystack. With the improved scores, a possible approach could be to set a large default page size and filter out answers below a threshold score.

Title: b'brandenchan'
Body: b'Hi, the `score` is the raw logit output of the model, and this value is essentially unbounded. The `probability` is a pseudo probability that is generated by scaling `logit` to a value between 0 and 1. This will be improved upon in future to better reflect real model confidence. I hope this helps!'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'As @brandenchan mentioned, the `score` is just the raw logit coming from the model. This allows meaningful comparisons of answers across different documents (not possible with softmax probabilities). 

However, those are not scaled between 0-1. That's why we have an additional value called `probability`, which is scaling the score into this range. The scaling from "logits" / "scores" to a pseudo probability happens here with a very simple function: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/3a95fe2006ec708a44ec227be1993acf77789844/haystack/finder.py#L108
We have some ideas to change this calculation to a more meaningful "probability" that reflects model confidence, but this is not our highest priority on the roadmap right now.  '

Title: b"Refactor pipeline's design"
Body:
b'From https://www.notion.so/deepsetai/Re-base-4-Pipeline-Type-Fundamentals-88d305b5edec4bdb923ba7c3d63a8d5c

## Current Status and Issues

- We distinguish between **query pipelines** and **indexing pipelines**
    - Query pipelines:
        - Use `"Query"` as root node
        - Ouput: `List[Document]` or `List[Answer]`
        - Access of `DocumentStore` through `Retriever`
    - Indexing pipelines:
        - Use `"File"` as root node
        - Dont have an output, but index `Documents` to `DocumentStore`
        - Currently not very prominent
            - not really used in Tutorials
            - `convert_file_to_docs` utility function takes currently the role of indexing pipelines
        - Explicit access of `DocumentStore`
- You can theoretically have more than one `DocumentStore` per Pipeline, but right now this possibility is not contemplated
- `Pipeline`'s `run` method takes basically anything - `query`, `documents`, `file_paths`, `labels`, ...
- Next to the generic `Pipeline`, we have a collection of "standard pipelines"
    - Currently, these are only query pipelines
    - Purpose: Easing the use for people who arent aware of how Pipelines should look like for specific tasks, like a recipe
    - Syntactic sugar: they don't add anything to a simple Pipeline made of the same nodes.
- Due to the `"Query"` and `"File"` root nodes, Pipelines can only be query or indexing: other approaches are really hard to implement
    - For example, quite complicated to build a summarization pipeline

## Core ideas

- Clarify the status of `DocumentStore` in Pipelines
  - Decision point: are **Document stores nodes or not**
  - If they are, they need to behave like normal nodes
  - If they are not, we need to clarify their API with respect to Pipelines. 
  - Direct access of DocumentStores by nodes should be made harder to avoid the DocStore-Retriever issue. Pipelines should mediate it.

- Pipelines should always produce an output
    - Currently indexing pipelines do not produce an output, while query pipelines do.
    - In case of indexing pipelines, the output could be a list of `Document` objects that can be indexed - to clarify

- Get rid of `convert_file_to_docs` utility function
    - Used in a lot of tutorials and should be exchanged by indexing pipelines

- Get rid of `"File"` and `"Query"` root node
  - We should stop classifying pipelines as indexing or query, but allow a more flexible structure. 
  - This would then be a generic `Pipeline` which should work easily with any use case
  - Additionally, we might have the subclasses `QueryPipeline(Pipeline)` and `IndexingPipeline(Pipeline)` which would help users understand what's required for querying and for indexing respectively.

- Nodes should declare their input
  - Right now nodes use the `run` method to declare their input. Mypy doesn't like that, for a good reason
  - Nodes should be free to take the input they need, so either with **kwargs or with an object/dictionary,
  - They need to declare a list of expected parameters to allow validation.

- Distinction between `run` and `run_batch` is unnecessary
  - There should be only `run_batch`, as the current `run` is simply a corner case where batch_size=1
    
- Marginally related: 
   - https://www.notion.so/deepsetai/Ray-graph-api-49b8d35a4cd544caaa7ae396790b2926 
   - https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/2403 **Separate concepts of "Retriever" and "Embedder"**

## Action Plan

- [ ] Create a new `Pipeline` and `BaseComponent` objects with basic features
  - Aims: 
    - Remove `Query` and `Indexing` root nodes
    - Refactor the `run` method to always take generic, batched input
    - Implement input validation through class attributes
    - Tackle dynamic outgoing edges management (#2850)
    - Add support for circular pipeline graphs?
    - Add support for `async`? https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/2968
    - Add support for nodes to output on several nodes at once: see https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/discussions/2972
- [ ] Migrate split/join nodes
   - Related: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/2599
 - [ ] Ensure loading from YAML and validation before loading are still possible
   - Name the content of YAML files is a bonus (A pipeline "schema"/"group"/"blueprint"? A "configuration"? An "architecture"? A "manifest"?) 
 - [ ] Implement a new `RayPipeline` taking https://www.notion.so/deepsetai/Ray-graph-api-49b8d35a4cd544caaa7ae396790b2926 and https://github.com/ArzelaAscoIi/ray-graph-api into account
- [ ] Introduce `QueryPipeline` and `IndexingPipeline`
- [ ] Phase out standard pipelines
- [ ] Replace the original `Pipeline` and migrate nodes
   - Heavy breaking change
   - Cobble together some support for Docstores and Retrievers
- [ ] Define Docstores' position in the pipeline by making the either normal nodes, or not nodes at all.
- [ ] Decouple Docstores and Retrievers
- [ ] Phase out `convert_file_to_docs` and replace with indexing pipelines wherever used

Each step comes with its own test refactoring.

## Notes:

- Splitting the execution of a pipeline from the graph and the nodes themselves (see below and https://deepset-ai.slack.com/archives/C02HA67P97Y/p1659605858455789)
- We can take inspiration from the Rasa approach to Pipelines https://github.com/RasaHQ/rasa/blob/main/rasa/engine/graph.py
'

Title: b'wochinge'

The `PipelineRunner` can then either run the pipeline locally or could e.g. also distribute its execution. For that it shouldn't be required to inspect the individual pipeline nodes (pipeline nodes should be abstract components with a `run` and `index` method + some initializer). Title: b'`TransformersDocumentClassifier`: inconsistent output between ordinary and zero-shot classification'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
When using `TransformersDocumentClassifier`, the output structure is different between ordinary and zero-shot classification.
For example, for the same document, we have these different outputs for `doc.meta['classification']`

*Classification*:
`{'label': 'joy', 'score': 0.9433773756027222}`

*Zero-shot classification*:
```
{'sequence': "The soundtrack album for the second season of HBO series ''Game of Thrones'', titled '''''Game of Thrones: Season 2''''', was published on June 19, 2012. The instrumental music by Ramin Djawadi was performed by the Czech Film Orchestra and Choir and recorded at the Rudolfinum concert hall in Prague.",
 'labels': ['music', 'history', 'natural language processing'],
 'scores': [0.953018069267273, 0.023982945829629898, 0.02299901656806469],
 'label': 'music'}
```

**Expected behavior**
I think that the output structure should always be the same.

**To Reproduce**

```python
from haystack import Document
from haystack.nodes import TransformersDocumentClassifier

doc = Document.from_dict(
    {'content': "The soundtrack album for the second season of HBO series ''Game of Thrones'', titled '''''Game of Thrones: Season 2''''', was published on June 19, 2012. The instrumental music by Ramin Djawadi was performed by the Czech Film Orchestra and Choir and recorded at the Rudolfinum concert hall in Prague.",
 'content_type': 'text',
 'meta': {'name': '25_Game_of_Thrones__Season_2__soundtrack_.txt'
  }})

doc_classifier = TransformersDocumentClassifier(model_name_or_path="bhadresh-savani/distilbert-base-uncased-emotion")
doc_classifier_zero_shot = TransformersDocumentClassifier(
    model_name_or_path="cross-encoder/nli-distilroberta-base",
    task="zero-shot-classification",
    labels=["music", "natural language processing", "history"]
)

print(doc_classifier.predict([doc])[0].meta['classification'])
print(doc_classifier_zero_shot.predict([doc])[0].meta['classification'])
```

**FAQ Check**
- [X] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?

**System:**

**How do we want to tackle this issue?

Title: b'Report separate QA metrics in eval for "no answer" labels '
Body:
b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We don't have any mechanism yet in pipeline.eval() for users to distinguish the performance of Reader models on "no answer" labels vs. regular labels. This makes it hard to compare performance between generative and extractive models - and is also quite useful just for extractive cases to understand the weak spots of the model. For example, if the model is just performing bad on no answer labels, you would typically calibrate the `no_ans_boost` or `confidence_threshold` in the [Reader](https://haystack.deepset.ai/reference/reader#farmreader).  It is also quite common to report these metrics separately (e.g. [Official SQuAD eval script](https://github.com/white127/SQUAD-2.0-bidaf), [results](https://huggingface.co/deepset/roberta-base-squad2) in our own model cards or our old eval in FARM)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Adjust `EvaluationResult.calculate_metrics()` to return the additional QA metrics:
- "f1_has_answer"
- "exact_match_has_answer"
- "sas_has_answer"
- "exact_match_no_answer"

(we can probably leave out "f1_no_answer" and "sas_no_answer", as they would be the same as "exact_match_no_answer")

Wording of the variables could of course be different. Could be a quick win, as we already have all data for this in the dataframe + the logic of calculating those metrics. We probably just need to filter the dataframe differently before calculating these metrics.'

Title: b'Pipeline uses too much memory when indexing a large amount of files'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
When using a pipeline with an `EmbeddingRetriever` to index a large amount of files, the process gets killed after generating all the embeddings but before indexing all of them in the `DocumentStore`. Using all pipeline components in isolation works just fine.

**Error message**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16985509/178289646-60d7fdda-9ae2-4731-9fc4-a551da983103.png)


**Expected behavior**
The indexing does not fail.

**To Reproduce**

Here is the pipeline yaml that was used:

```yaml
version: '1.5.0'

components:
  - name: DocumentStore
    type: ElasticsearchDocumentStore
    params:
      host: "localhost"
      port: 9200
      similarity: cosine
      refresh_type: "false"
      recreate_index: True
  - name: Retriever
    type: EmbeddingRetriever
    params:
      document_store: DocumentStore
      embedding_model: deepset/gbert-base
      model_format: sentence_transformers
      use_auth_token: False
      top_k: 25
  - name: TextFileConverter
    type: TextConverter
  - name: Preprocessor
    type: PreProcessor
    params:
      split_by: passage
      split_length: 1
      split_respect_sentence_boundary: False

pipelines:
  - name: query
    nodes:
      - name: Retriever
        inputs: [Query]

  - name: indexing
    nodes:
      - name: TextFileConverter
        inputs: [File]
      - name: Preprocessor
        inputs: [TextFileConverter]
      - name: Retriever
        inputs: [Preprocessor]
      - name: DocumentStore
        inputs: [Retriever]
```


This code was used to do the indexing:

```python
def create_single_files(batch_file_path):
    file_paths = []
    with open(batch_file_path, 'r') as f:
        for line in f:
            file = json.loads(line.strip())
            file_path = '/'.join(batch_file_path.split('/')[:-1])
            file_path = os.path.join(file_path, file['doc_id'])
            with open(file_path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(file['doc'])
            file_paths.append(file_path)

    return file_paths


def load_pipeline(pipeline_yaml_path):
    return Pipeline.load_from_yaml(pipeline_yaml_path, 'indexing')


def index_files(batch_file_path, pipeline_yaml_path):
    file_paths = create_single_files(batch_file_path)
    with open(pipeline_yaml_path, 'r') as f:
        yaml_object = yaml.safe_load(f.read())

    timings = {
        'num_docs': len(file_paths),
        'pipeline': yaml_object,
        'benchmark_data': str(datetime.now())
    }
    start_pipeline_load = time.process_time()
    pipeline = load_pipeline(pipeline_yaml_path)
    end_pipeline_load = time.process_time()
    timings['pipeline_load'] = end_pipeline_load - start_pipeline_load

    start_indexing = time.process_time()
    pipeline.run(file_paths=file_paths)
    end_indexing = time.process_time()
    timings['indexing'] = end_indexing - start_indexing
    timings['docs/s'] = len(file_paths) / (end_indexing - start_indexing)

    print(timings)
    with open('logs/benchmark_w_pipeline.json', 'a') as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(timings) + '\n')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    batch_file_path = './data/corpus_1M.jsonl'
