Title: b'Trying to load a YAML pipeline with a Retreiver using custom_query fails validation'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**

I have a use-case where I need to apply a filter query for access control purposes. 
I found that I could use the `custom_query` field on the `Retriever` implementation to do exactly what I wanted.

Unfortunately, when I converted the project to use a YAML pipeline definition instead of hard coded values, I encountered validation issues .

Here's the problematic portion of the `pipeline.yaml` file: 

```yaml
- name: CustomRetriever
    type: BM25Retriever
    params:
      document_store: CustomElasticsearchStore
      top_k: 20
      custom_query: '{
                        "size": 10,
                        "query": {
                          "bool": {
                            "should": [
                              {
                                "multi_match": {
                                  "query": ${query},
                                  "type": "most_fields",
                                  "fields": ["content"]
                                }
                              }
                            ],
                            "filter": [
                              {
                                "term": {"source": ${source}}
                              }
                            ]
                          }
                        }
                      }'
```

**Error message**

`
haystack.errors.PipelineConfigError: '{ "size": 10, "query": { "bool": { "should": [ { "multi_match": { "query": ${query}, "type": "most_fields", "fields": ["content"] } } ], "filter": [ { "term": {"source": ${source}} } ] } } }' is not a valid variable name or value. Use alphanumeric characters or dash, underscore and colon only.
`

By running a search on the error string, it led me to the `config.py` file where it uses a regex to validate the input strings.

`
VALID_INPUT_REGEX = re.compile(r"^[-a-zA-Z0-9_/\\.:]+$")
`
https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/pipelines/config.py 


I'm not sure how I can pass a JSON query from YAML with such restrictions.

On the other hand, I do have a way out that is less elegant by using an environment property:

`
CUSTOMRETRIEVER_PARAMS_CUSTOM_QUERY='{ "size": 10, "query": { "bool": { "should": [ { "multi_match": { "query": ${query}, "type": "most_fields", "fields": ["content"] } } ], "filter": [ { "term": {"source": ${source}} } ] } } }'
`


**Expected behavior**

The `custom_query` field should be accepted if it contains valid JSON  and is of type `str`.
The internal usage of the field works just fine if using the ENV variable substitution or code configurations.

**Additional context**

It's a simple retriever with an Elasticsearch document store. 

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a pipeline with non-trivial `custom_query`.

```yaml
version: '1.5.0'

components:

    type: ElasticsearchDocumentStore
    params:
      host: localhost
      index: test
      port: 9200

                              {
                                "multi_match": {
                                  "query": ${query},
                                  "type": "most_fields",
                                  "fields": ["content"]
                                }
                              }
                            ],
                            "filter": [
                              {
                                "term": {"source": ${source}}
                              }
                            ]
                          }
                        }
                      }'

  - name: Reader
    type: FARMReader
    params:
      model_name_or_path: deepset/roberta-base-squad2
      context_window_size: 500
      return_no_answer: true

pipelines:
  - name: query
    nodes:
      - name: CustomRetriever
        inputs: [Query]
      - name: Reader
        inputs: [CustomRetriever]
```

2. Attempt to load it from YAML.
`
pipeline = Pipeline.load_from_yaml(Path(PIPELINE_PATH), pipeline_name="query")
`

**FAQ Check**
- [x] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?

Yes.

Title: b'danielbichuetti'
Body:
b'Hi @masci 

I'm sorry for not sending all into one message. It's just that I got the error and investigated further after sometime. Using Selenium the only options would be implicit wait using (driver.implicitly_wait(x) # x second), or explicit wait. The latest would need the user to send an EC (expected_condition), ready-made or custom one.

There is a framework - Playwright - from the same authors of Puppeteer that is currently under development by Microsoft. Disney, ING and Adobe uses it for web testing. We use it at the company for some web scraping. It's simple to install, allowing to use a pre-installed browser or let it download it. It has a pretty clear design and there are some wait conditions in the navigation classes, like:

`page.goto("https://www.migalhas.com.br", wait_until="networkidle")` or
`page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle"); # This waits for the "networkidle"` or even the most sofisticated one:
`page.wait_for_function("() => window.amILoadedYet()")`

A lot of the web scraping companies uses Playwright now.

'

Title: b'danielbichuetti'
Body:
b"I've tested a lot more and implicitly wait is not a good choice. It's pretty unstable, and sometimes it just doesn't wait correct time (I didn't look at the source code to understand). Also, it's suitable to wait in elements being ready, and in some cases elements are removed from the DOM. A better solution would be waiting (time.sleep) or a custom WebDriver function. Another option would be to implement a Playwright port of the Crawler.

Using a new variable page_wait_time using your patterns, init, crawl and run with the time in seconds to wait makes it a plausible solution for the time. And maybe another to receive the WebDriverWait function (page_wait_function), if user want to wait specific EC.

Are you open to contributors ? May I code this fix and start then a Playwright class (PlaywrightCrawler) ?"

Title: b'`Pipeline` does not forward empty parameters'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
- An indexing pipeline receiving an empty list of files will throw a confusing `TypeError`

**Expected behavior**
- The pipeline should either be no-op, raise a warning and then no-op, or throw a helpful error message explaining what's really wrong.

**To Reproduce**
```python
from haystack import Pipeline
from haystack.nodes import FileTypeClassifier

pipeline = Pipeline()
classifier = FileTypeClassifier()
pipeline.add_node(classifier, name="classifier", inputs=["File"])

pipeline.run(file_paths=[])
```

**Error message**
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/sara/work/haystack/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/haystack/pipelines/base.py", line 509, in run
    node_output, stream_id = self.graph.nodes[node_id]["component"]._dispatch_run(**node_input)
  File "/home/sara/work/haystack/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/haystack/nodes/base.py", line 172, in _dispatch_run
    return self._dispatch_run_general(self.run, **kwargs)
  File "/home/sara/work/haystack/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/haystack/nodes/base.py", line 216, in _dispatch_run_general
    output, stream = run_method(**run_inputs, **run_params)
TypeError: run() missing 1 required positional argument: 'file_paths'

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/sara/work/haystack/examples/example.py", line 9, in <module>
    pipeline.run(file_paths=[])
  File "/home/sara/work/haystack/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/haystack/pipelines/base.py", line 512, in run
    raise Exception(
Exception: Exception while running node `classifier` with input `{'root_node': 'File', 'params': {}, 'node_id': 'classifier'}`: run() missing 1 required positional argument: 'file_paths', full stack trace: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/sara/work/haystack/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/haystack/pipelines/base.py", line 509, in run
    node_output, stream_id = self.graph.nodes[node_id]["component"]._dispatch_run(**node_input)
  File "/home/sara/work/haystack/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/haystack/nodes/base.py", line 172, in _dispatch_run
    return self._dispatch_run_general(self.run, **kwargs)
  File "/home/sara/work/haystack/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/haystack/nodes/base.py", line 216, in _dispatch_run_general
    output, stream = run_method(**run_inputs, **run_params)
TypeError: run() missing 1 required positional argument: 'file_paths'
```

Note how in the snippet above `file_paths` is clearly given, even if it's an empty list.

**Additional context**
Pipelines currently work in a very odd way. The `run()` method expects different inputs for each node, but Pipeline does not use proper signature matching and rather forwards to the nodes only parameters that are not empty. So if a required parameter is, like in this case, an empty list, `Pipeline` will assume that the node does not require that argument, thrown it out, and cause the exception above.
'

Title: b'Add support for Multi-Hop Dense Retrieval'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
`haystack` supports a couple of great retrieval methods. However, as far as I have seen, none of them is designed for multi-hop retrieval, i.e., use cases where it is necessary to look at multiple connected documents (see [here](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2009.06401#S1.F1) for a better description). Amongst others, this can be useful for multi-hop fact-checking or QA.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
There are a couple of methods out there that tackle this issue. A relatively straightforward one to add to `haystack` might be _Multi-Hop Dense Retrieval (MDR)_ introduced by Facebook last year: [Answering Complex Open-Domain Questions with Multi-Hop Dense Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.12756). 

In principle, it's DPR ([`DensePassageRetriever`](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/a2a99f79b141d1bbecc15d0d45ebacae2fc348e8/haystack/nodes/retriever/dense.py#L35)) applied iteratively. In the first iteration, a set of documents is retrieved. Then, the query and the top-ranked document from the first iteration are concatenated and embedded in order to give context to the query. This embedding is then used to search the document vector space in the second iteration. And so forth. One important difference between DPR and MDR is that MDR uses a shared encoder for queries and documents.

A reference implementation from Facebook is available here: https://github.com/facebookresearch/multihop_dense_retrieval

**Additional context**
I'd like to give an implementation a try if you think it's a valuable addition to `haystack`  Any tips/suggestions/comments?
"

When you call 

```
document_store = FAISSDocumentStore.load(index_path = 'my_faiss_docstore.faiss', config_path = 'my_faiss_docstore.json')

document_store.save('hello.faiss')

Object of type IndexFlat is not JSON serializable

Docstore gets saved

When a docstore is initialized from a load statement, or initialized while giving it an existing faiss index, that index is passed into config, and when you call save, it throws an error because the index is not json serializable.

TO FIX:

I feel that that config should not contain the index, since it isn't really a part of the config, and also the index gets saved in a separate file anyways.

Another way to fix this is to do something like 

```
temp = dict(self.pipeline_config["params"])
temp.pop('faiss_index')
with open(config_path, 'w') as ipp:
            json.dump(temp, ipp)
```
[here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/document_stores/faiss.py#L531) but this seems very hacky.

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b'Hey @ugm2, I had a quick look at your report here, so forgive me if I misunderstood what you're trying to do.

I agree it's not always easy to understand what the `params` dictionary can take, but something that I can say with certainty is that it does *not* correspond to the list of parameters taken by the `__init__` method of your target node. So the parameters you give in the YAML (`host`, `port`, `query_embedding_model`, etc...) can't be passed again in the `.run()` method.

The idea behind this is that the parameters given in the YAML are the ones you use to _create_ the nodes (so `host` and `port` for Elasticsearch, the models for Retriever, etc), while the params passed in `.run()` are the ones the node needs while _running_ (so for example `top_k`, `split_by`, etc...).

Sometimes there is some overlap. For example PreProcessor can also take `split_by` in its `__init__` and use that value as a default if you don't pass another value to the `.run()` method. But you can't pass another model name to Retriever, because the model is already initialized when the node is created, and can't be re-created at runtime.

I hope this explanation makes some sense to you. I am going to look for a better explanation in the docs and link it here :slightly_smiling_face: 

----

For the question "What can I put into the params dictionary": the quick answer is "Whatever the `.run()` method accepts". For example, DensePassageRetriever has no `.run()` method: it uses `BaseRetriever`s, which looks like: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/4ca331c0a77165f622af11b6180c959c991d03be/haystack/nodes/retriever/base.py#L260-L269

These are the keys you can have in `params`. Notice `top_k`, `filters`, `index`, `headers`, `scale_score`, etc...

For PreProcessor instead: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/4ca331c0a77165f622af11b6180c959c991d03be/haystack/nodes/preprocessor/base.py#L52-L62
 
So you can pass `clean_whitespace`, `split_by`, etc... 

I hope this helps :slightly_smiling_face: '

Title: b'Suppress tokenizers parallelism warning'
Body:
b'The following warning is triggered for every reader inference step if using CPU for inference with `num_threads` not set to 1:
```
huggingface/tokenizers: The current process just got forked, after parallelism has already been used. Disabling parallelism to avoid deadlocks...
To disable this warning, you can either:
	- Avoid using `tokenizers` before the fork if possible
	- Explicitly set the environment variable TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=(true | false)
```

We should show this warning at most once.

Unfortunately, the warning is not a proper python warning that we could easily filter out after the first occurrence but a simple print statement here in rust: https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers/blob/943b5421aa8031f1c6b87ce726b594dcf31f4045/bindings/python/src/lib.rs#L30

What I have in mind as a workaround is turning off TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM via the environment variable from within Haystack in case we notice that the warning would be triggered otherwise. Something like the following in `modeling/infer.py` https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/ffb7e4e4bd900616f3e9154755847c91b23fb340/haystack/modeling/infer.py#L340:

```
# TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM env variable needs to be set to false to prevent a warning in huggingface tokenizers.
# To this end, we store the env variables value if it is not already set to false,
# then set it to false before the method call,
# and finally set it back to its previous value afterward.
env_variable = "TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM"
tokenizers_parallelism = os.getenv(env_variable)
if tokenizers_parallelism in ["", "off", "false", "f", "no", "n", "0"]:
    predictions = self._inference_with_multiprocessing(
        dicts, return_json, aggregate_preds, multiprocessing_chunksize
    )
else:
    try:
        os.environ[env_variable] = "false"
        predictions = self._inference_with_multiprocessing(
            dicts, return_json, aggregate_preds, multiprocessing_chunksize
        )
    finally:
        if tokenizers_parallelism is not None:
            os.environ[env_variable] = tokenizers_parallelism
        else:
            os.unsetenv(env_variable)
```
'

Title: b'Incompatibility of python 3.10 and elasticsearch 7.10 with Haystack 1.5'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
The new Haystack v1.5.0 release supports python 3.10. However, I came across an incompatibility issue/a small bug in the elasticsearch client 7.10 and python 3.10. 

The error message is as follows when running `python tutorials/Tutorial1_Basic_QA_Pipeline.py`:
```
INFO - haystack.document_stores.base -  Numba not found, replacing njit() with no-op implementation. Enable it with 'pip install numba'.
Traceback (most recent call last):

    from collections.abs import Mapping
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'collections.abs'
```

So there is a typo `collections.abs` instead of `collections.abc` in the elasticsearch client, which lets the import fail.

It was fixed here:
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch-py/commit/cf39af344c26b58b5f0ab8d9bb992879fdf71ac6

Downgrading the elasticsearch client to 7.9 worked for me. Maybe we should upgrade the client in the setup config (7.10 is currently the upper limit)? Another option would be to exclude version 7.10 for now but so far not many people seem to be using Haystack with python 3.10. What are your thoughts?'

Title: b"Ranker scores shouldn't be discarded"
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The reason for using a ranker is that the scores should be more accurate than the retriever scores. For this reason, in that use case you would also want to use the ranker scores later on instead of the retriever score (e.g. when defining a threshold). You currently cannot do that as the ranker scores aren't saved anywhere (see [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/b87c0c950b2243f47fb249aa3865d4c46edb16df/haystack/nodes/ranker/sentence_transformers.py)) as the reader only updates the order and not the score. Having the order of documents not dependent on the scores is also unintuitive.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Replace retriever scores with ranker scores.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Having an additional field to save ranker scores."

Title: b'id_hash_keys does not use the passed fields to calculate the document id'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
Running an indexing pipeline with `params={"id_hash_keys": ["content", "meta"]}` does not use the `meta` field of the document to calculate the hash. Therefore two doucments with the same content end up with the same `id` even if they have different metadata.

**Expected behavior**
Adding the argument `{"id_hash_keys": ["content", "meta"]}` should use the meta values to compute the hash and therefore these documents should be written twice to the database instead of replacing each other.

**To Reproduce**
```py
from haystack.document_stores import DeepsetCloudDocumentStore
from haystack.nodes import ElasticsearchRetriever, FARMReader, FileTypeClassifier, PDFToTextConverter, PreProcessor, TextConverter
from haystack.pipelines import Pipeline
from pathlib import Path

document_store = DeepsetCloudDocumentStore(index="your-index-in-deepset-cloud") # can be replaced by any docstore
file_type_classifier = FileTypeClassifier()
text_converter = TextConverter()
preprocessor = PreProcessor(split_by="word", split_length=250, split_overlap=50, split_respect_sentence_boundary=True)
retriever = ElasticsearchRetriever(document_store=document_store, top_k=20)

indexing_pipeline = Pipeline()
indexing_pipeline.add_node(component=text_converter, name="TextConverter", inputs=["File"])
indexing_pipeline.add_node(component=preprocessor, name="Preprocessor", inputs=["TextConverter"])
indexing_pipeline.add_node(component=retriever, name="Retriever", inputs=["Preprocessor"])
indexing_pipeline.add_node(component=document_store, name="DocumentStore", inputs=["Retriever"])

meta_1 = {"key": "a"}
meta_2 = {"key": "b"}
meta = [meta_1, meta_2]

file = Path("textfile.txt")
file_paths = [file,file]

params={"id_hash_keys": ["content", "meta"]}

batch_indexing = indexing_pipeline.run(file_paths=[file,file],meta=meta,params=params)
print(batch_indexing.get("documents")[0].id) 
print(batch_indexing.get("documents")[1].id)
assert batch_indexing.get("documents")[0].id == batch_indexing.get("documents")[1].id # <- true 

single_1_indexing = indexing_pipeline.run(file_paths=file,meta=meta_1,params=params)
print(single_1_indexing.get("documents")[0].id)
single_2_indexing = indexing_pipeline.run(file_paths=file,meta=meta_1,params=params)
print(single_2_indexing.get("documents")[0].id)

assert single_1_indexing.get("documents")[0].id == single_2_indexing.get("documents")[0].id # <- true 
```


'

Body: b'Code looks good so far: `id_hash_keys` is used in `TextConverter`, `Preprocessore` and `DocumentStore` appropriately. Needs some debugging...'

Title: b'Restructure the tests'
Body:
b'The current tests suite has a number of issues which is slowly growing. Some notable ones are:
- GitHub runners often run out of resources during the execution of the tests
- Large test suites are flaky and Windows tests are even more flaky, sometimes outright not runnable
- The CI takes a very long time to complete (around 10-20 minutes)
- The setup is not optimized (sometimes document stores are started even if not used)
- Most unit tests are actually integration tests in disguise

We have a lot of margin of improvement on our test suite. The main goals are:

- Separate unit tests from integration tests
- Use mocks heavily in the unit tests
- Increase test speed, coverage and readability

To achieve these goals, I propose to:

- [x] Separate `unit_tests` and `integration_tests`.
    - Unit tests should test only Haystack code and mock all dependencies.
       - If the test loses its utility in the process, then it was probably not needed to begin with and should stay as part of a larger integration test instead.
       - Unit tests should be really fast and always able to run locally on any reasonable laptop without GPU.
       - Unit tests should run in matrices of all supported Python versions and possibly all supported dependency versions, as much as possible.
       - https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2562

   - Integration tests should be very few and do few asserts,
       - Corner cases should be rather covered by unit tests
       - Stuff can still be mocked in shorted integration tests.
       - We might want to further distinguish between integration and end-to-end tests, but this decision can be taken in a later stage.
       - https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2557
    
- [ ] Create some easy-to-reuse mocks for the most used and most resource intensive components of Haystack: 
   - MockReader
   - MockRetriever (a MockDPRetriever might be needed too)
   - MockDocumentStore (maybe a simplified version of InMemoryDocumentStore) 
   - Other components if needed will be added progressively in later PRs

- [x] Refactor the fixtures and move them in the relevant suites if needed
    - Some fixtures are very specific for some test suites, sharing them only makes them more complex.
    - **In tests only**, we prefer code duplication over code reusability. Tests should be first of all very easy to read.
    - https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2577
    - https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2554

Additional, more specific tasks include:

- [ ] Each document store will have its own tests. 
    - Reusing tests across document stores is probably the source of their really complex setup, and the differences among them are often too large for this process to bring many benefits. 
    - We might still have some shared tests, but they should be the minority and possibly they should be only integration tests.
    - https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2573

- [x] Review the GitHub workflows
    - There is probably some improvements on the way the tests are executed on the CI for example about the document store containers.
    - https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2576
    - https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2547
    - https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2556'

b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
 The Preprocessor class is an amazing tool and it is very useful to use when we are processing data.  But it may be useful if we can add a custom cleaning function to call on top of it , if we want to  add more cleaning . For example, I am working on French data, I would like to remove accents or dialetrics to my text before applying the preprocessor.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It is not that it is not possible to achieve that , I can do this by cleaning my text first and then pass it to the preprocessor , I have tried to extent the class and let it do what I want , here is what I come up with.

```

class CustomPreProcessor(PreProcessor):
    def __init__(self, custom_preprocessor: callable=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.custom_preprocessor = custom_preprocessor
    def clean(
        self,
        document: Union[dict, Document],
        clean_whitespace: bool,
        clean_header_footer: bool,
        clean_empty_lines: bool,
        remove_substrings: List[str],
        id_hash_keys: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    ) -> Document:
        """
        Perform document cleaning on a single document and return a single document. This method will deal with whitespaces, headers, footers
        and empty lines. Its exact functionality is defined by the parameters passed into PreProcessor.__init__().
        """
        if id_hash_keys is None:
            id_hash_keys = self.id_hash_keys

        if isinstance(document, dict):
            document = Document.from_dict(document, id_hash_keys=id_hash_keys)

        # Mainly needed for type checking
        if not isinstance(document, Document):
            raise HaystackError("Document must not be of type 'dict' but of type 'Document'.")
        text = document.content
        if custom_preprocessor:
              text = self.custom_preprocessor(text)
        if clean_header_footer:
            text = self._find_and_remove_header_footer(
                text, n_chars=300, n_first_pages_to_ignore=1, n_last_pages_to_ignore=1
            )

        if clean_whitespace:
            lines = text.splitlines()

            cleaned_lines = []
            for line in lines:
                line = line.strip()
                cleaned_lines.append(line)
            text = "\n".join(cleaned_lines)

        if clean_empty_lines:
            text = re.sub(r"\n\n+", "\n\n", text)

        for substring in remove_substrings:
            text = text.replace(substring, "")

        if text != document.content:
            document = deepcopy(document)
            document.content = text

        return document
```
Here is my solution and, how I am calling it, I don't know what you guys think if we can integrate It into the code.

Title: b'MichelBartels'
Body:
b"Hi @sbhttchryy, thanks for your interest in TableQA.

1. For training the model, we've used the dataset that we have introduced in [this paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.04049). We trained for one epoch and used the `MultipleNegativesRankingLoss` implemented in the sentence transformers library.
2. The paper mentioned above describes that specific table encodings do not seem to result in better model performance. We also tried more recently newer table retrieval models and their table-specific encodings also didn't seem to result in any improvements. These findings were also confirmed by [a paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.09843.pdf) that was released a few weeks ago.
For this reason, we decided just to fine-tune an existing sentence embedding model on tables in csv format and we found all-mpnet-base-v2 to work best in that case. The reason we used csv was just that it uses just very few tokens. In general, most ways of encoding the table seemed not to perform significantly different.
3. Currently, haystack does not support training an EmbeddingRetriever for tables. You could, however, use a library like sentence-transformers and do the table to csv conversion yourself.
4. I am afraid there's also no way to train a TableReader in haystack. I would recommend using the transformers library for this. They have quite an [extensive tutorial](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/tapas#usage-finetuning) on it and afterwards you should be able to easily load it into haystack."

Title: b'Yes/No question QA model'
Body: b'Do you have example/pretrained model to support Yes/No boolean questions?\r\n\r\n'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b"Hey @vladgets , 

Interesting question and definitely a valuable feature in QA pipelines - especially for conversational use cases!

We don't have a pre-trained model for yes/no questions yet. We added some basic functionality in FARM a while ago to train such models on the natural questions dataset. You can find an example script [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/FARM/blob/master/examples/natural_questions.py). The idea there was to have two prediction heads  - one for extractive QA and one for classifying yes/no. If you are interested in training such a model yourself, maybe give this a try.

We also have the support for yes/no on the roadmap of Haystack. What's missing? Well, we were not 100% happy with the inference part and answer format of the existing FARM implementation. Our plan is to refactor this in FARM before we make it available in Haystack (and publish models). 

In general, we are also following the research activities for this feature quite closely. If you are considering training your own model, maybe this dataset could also be interesting as NQ doesn't contain too many yes/no samples: https://www.aclweb.org/anthology/N18-1074/

Happy to hear also your thoughts on this feature and any modeling/experiments you maybe already did yourself!
"

Title: b'tholor'

This is rather a complex issue and to manage expectations: the main work here is to figure out a very clean, lean implementation and modeling approach. We won't have the time to guide you here closely in the next weeks. 

A simpler alternative might be to train a generator (like RAG) on a dataset that includes more "yes/no" answers. This is probably less dependent on deep FARM/Haystack integrations but can also easily take a couple of weeks work.

Whoever is going to kick-off work here: We should also do a quick literature review about other recent approaches here. Papers addressing the binary questions in Natural Questions might be a good starting point.

Title: b'Is it possible to implement pipeline for "question answering on a Knowledge Graph"'
Body:
b'**Question**
We want to use pipeline for a question answering based on knowlege graph, but right now there aren't nodes implementation to retrieve, for example, triples from a web services or insert them on a GraphDB instance.

We know that knowledge graph functionalities are still in a very early stage, but we think that with some hints we can implement (and share of course) some classes to:
- retrieve triples from web services (like crawler?)
- store them in graphdb instance (which kind of node implement the "store" phase?)
- convert query into sparql (retriever or trasformer?)
- execute sparql query (retriever?)
- return results

Is there some points in the documentation that we can check? 
Could you give use some hints?
Thanks in advance

**FAQ Check**
- [X] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?
'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b'Hello @ilseva! Great to hear you're interested in the knowledge graph feature :slightly_smiling_face:  I can try to help you with this one.

The current Haystack nodes related to KGs are:
- `GraphDBKnowledgeGraph` https://haystack.deepset.ai/reference/document-store#module-graphdb , the equivalent of a "document store"
- `Text2SparqlRetriever` https://haystack.deepset.ai/reference/retriever#module-text2sparql which translates natural language queries into SPARQL queries.

To my knowledge that's all. Regarding your points specifically:

- **retrieve triples from web services**: Yes, that would definitely be a sort of Crawler. No constraints here: feel free to implement it as you wish, as long as it produces a TTL file as a result. This is the only format that can be processed by `GraphDBKnowledgeGraph` ATM, 
    - If you feel like implementing a method of `GraphDBKnowledgeGraph` that can process some other type of input, then this limitation doesn't apply anymore.

- **store them in graphdb instance**: see above

- **convert query into sparql**: `Text2SparqlRetriever` can do it :slightly_smiling_face:

- **execute sparql query**, **return results**: `GraphDBKnowledgeGraph` has a `query` method which should do the trick. In addition, I believe that `Text2SparqlRetriever` performs the query to the KG too, so given a natural language question, will return the results of the SPARQL query against your KG.

I haven't tried, but I think query pipelines with `GraphDBKnowledgeGraph` and `Text2SparqlRetriever` should work nicely. The indexing side is more fuzzy instead, and I think it can't be made in a pipeline right now: you'll have to run the crawler "manually" (call its `run` method explicitly), then give the file to `GraphDBKnowledgeGraph.import_from_ttl_file()`.

I hope this helps! Let me know if you have any other questions. If you open a PR, please tag me so I can keep track of them more easily.'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b"Hey @DJokes , 

Ok as we are just forwarding the params from Haystack to the elasticsearch client to establish the connection let's try to understand what might be a solution on the elasticsearch client level. If we have something working there, we can adjust the haystack params. 
Does the workaround with the ssl_context mentioned [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch-py/issues/712#issuecomment-357750570) work for you (just using the elasticsearch client directly without any haystack)?"

Title: b'amena-koi'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b"Ok, then I'd suggest that we create the `ssl_context` object within the `ElasticsearchDocumentStore` and pass it down to the elasticsearch client for the connection.

For context, this is the example for them elastic thread: 
```
ssl_context = create_ssl_context(<use `cafile`, or `cadata` or `capath` to set your CA or CAs)
context.check_hostname = False
context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
es = Elasticsearch('localhost', ssl_context=context, timeout=60 ...)
```

So we could probably pass the path in `ca_certs` to `create_ssl_context` and set the context attributes. 

The alternative would be to just add a `ssl_context` parameter to the init of `ElasticsearchDocumentStore`. However, I see that this might cause problems with saving / loading pipelines to YAML as this param would not be easily serializable.

@Djokes Are you interested in opening a pull request here? If not we can also tackle this with our team, but it might take a few weeks."

Title: b'masci'
Body:

I would argue we can keep using the ssl-related kwargs, which seems safer than migrating all the connections in Haystack to use `ssl_context`.

I am also keen to rule out the linked issue on elasticsearch-py altogether: that happened in 6.x and claimed to be fixed there, and a snippet running `elasticsearch==7.10.0` with `verify_certs=False` is working for me.

I suspect the problem happens at a lower level, for example depending on wether you're using `Urllib3HttpConnection` or `RequestsHttpConnection`, the latter would be affected by certain environment variables set.

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body:
b'Hi @yuanwu2017, thanks for sharing the additional information, this helps me to identify the problem. Looking at your config files, I am not quite sure what you are trying to achieve, maybe you can elaborate a bit more on your case?

The first problem I see is that you are using an `EmbddingRetriever` with the model `"deepset/sentence_bert"` bur you are using the `"deepset/elasticsearch-countries-and-capitals"` image with pre-indexed Documents as your DocumentStore. There are two issues with this:
1) The Documents inside the DocumentStore you're using do not contain embeddings. Therefore, you are not able to retrieve them using the `EmbeddingRetriever`. You would need to either add embedding to those Documents or use the `BM25Retriever` instead.
2) The Documents inside the DocumentStore are not in the format that we would expect for FAQPipelines. Title: b'Differences in DocumentStores'
Body:
b"We currently support 10 different DocumentStores in Haystack. In the following overview, I try to list the public methods that are available in only some of the DocumentStores.

 

#### `get_metadata_values_by_key`
- Supported in: `ElasticsearchDocumentStore`, `OpenDistroElasticsearchDocumentStore`, `OpenSearchDocumentStore`
- Missing in: `InMemoryDocumentStore`, `MilvusDocumentStore`, `PineconeDocumentStore`, `SQLDocumentStore`, `WeaviateDocumentStore`

This method allows the user to get the distinct values + their counts of a specific metadata field inside a DocumentStore. Currently, this is only available for DocumentStore inheriting from `ElasticsearchDocumentStore`. I'd guess that this is not a highly used method and, therefore, would not give this a high priority to add this to the other DocumentStores.

#### `update_document_meta`
- Supported in: `ElasticsearchDocumentStore`, `OpenDistroElasticsearchDocumentStore`, `OpenSearchDocumentStore`, `MilvusDocumentStore`, `PineconeDocumentStore`, `SQLDocumentStore`, `WeaviateDocumentStore`
- Missing in: `InMemoryDocumentStore`

This method allows the user to update the meta fields of a Document by providing the Document ID and a meta dictionary. It is available in almost each DocumentStore, only `InMemoryDocumentStore` does not support it. However, the implementation in the different DocumentStores seems to differ: While for most of the DocumentStores only the specified fields seem to be overwritten and the unspecified ones remain unchanged, for `PineconeDocumentStore` it seems that all of the Document's meta data will be replaced by the specified meta dictionary.

#### `query` / `query_batch`
- Supported in: `ElasticsearchDocumentStore`, `OpenDistroElasticsearchDocumentStore`, `OpenSearchDocumentStore`, `WeaviateDocumentStore`

This method is supported in DocumentStores inheriting from `KeywordDocumentStore`. Those are DocumentStores that inherently support a keyword-based search. It probably would not make sense to add those methods to the other DocumentStores, as they only support querying by embedding.
Also, I think we should remove this method from `WeaviateDocumentStore`. There, the `query` param is not even supported and it rather has the functionality of `get_all_documents` with using filters.

#### `query_by_embedding` / `update_embeddings`
- Missing in: `SQLDocumentStore`

This method allows querying the DocumentStores using dense methods and is currently supported in all DocumentStores except for `SQLDocumentStore`. Maybe it might make sense to implement this functionality using something like [pgvector](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector-python)?

Also, filtering support for `FAISSDocumentStore` and `Milvus2DocumentStore` seems to be missing here. While FAISS still does not support filtering, filtering should be possible with Milvus2.

#### `train_index`
- Supported in: `FAISSDocumentStore`

This method is needed for some of the supported index types in FAISS. I had a quick look at Milvus, Weaviate and Pinecone documentation and it seems that with these DocumentStores, training is not required.

#### `save` / `load`
- Supported in: `FAISSDocumentStore`
- Missing in: `InMemoryDocumentStore`

Saving and loading a saved a DocumentStore is currently only supported in `FAISSDocumentStore`. For the other DocumentStores, this method might not be needed, as they already use persistent storage, i.e. indexed Documents don't get lost. Only `InMemoryDocumentStore` would need such functionality, but here we (or even the user) might simply use `pickle`.

#### `get_documents_by_vector_ids` / `update_vector_ids` / `reset_vector_ids`
- Supported in: `SQLDocumentStore`, `FAISSDocumentStore`, `PineconeDocumentStore`, `MilvusDocumentStore`

This method is used to map the vectors that are indexed in the different vector databases to the Documents that are indexed in the SQL database and is supported by document stores inheriting from `SQLDocumentStore`. I don't think that these methods need to be public, I would rather make them private.

#### `get_scores` / `get_scores_numpy` / `get_scores_torch` 
- Supported in: `InMemoryDocumentStore`

Theses methods are used to calculate the scores for dense retrieval in `InMemoryDocumentStore`. IMO, these methods don't need to be public either. 

"

Title: b'tstadel'
Body: b"I think there are additional differences regarding labels. They are a bit hidden however. E.g. `SQLDocumentStore` and thus `Pinecone`, `Milvus` and `FAISS` too don't support metadata and filters in labels, and others (I think it's just Weaviate) don't support labels at all."

Title: b'Separate concepts of "Retriever" and "Embedder"'
Body:
b'**Problem**
Right now, dense Retrievers take responsibility for two separate operations: creating the embeddings and using them. This causes several unintuitive situations, like:
- Indexing pipelines need Retrievers right before the document store in order for the embeddings to be generated at indexing time
- We classify retriever as dense and sparse, putting in the same basket classes with substantially different API
- Dense retrievers have a sort of weak circular dependency with the docstore (see https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2311) that sparse retrievers don't have

**Solution**
I propose to extract the creation of embeddings into a separate node, which could be called "Embedder" or something similar, with the sole task of generating the embeddings. Such node would fit neatly into an indexing pipeline. 

Retrievers would lose the ability of creating embeddings and would just fail if they don't find them in the docstore. In this way, they would be mostly fit for query pipelines only, would get smaller and easier to understand. Also the distinction between sparse and dense ones would become smaller and more understandable ("A dense Retriever needs an Embedder to generate embeddings for the documents at indexing time", rather than the current"A dense Retriever needs to be placed before the docstore at indexing time and after it at query time").

Of course different Retrievers will require embeddings created by their own Embedder, but this is a simple check that could be added.

This is still a rough idea, so refinement and alternative ideas welcome :slightly_smiling_face: 

@oryx1729 '

Title: b'lalitpagaria'
Body: b'Adding a related historical ticket https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1004 '

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body: b"Really interesting idea you had there! Thank you for linking, when we will manage to tackle docstores I'll try to make this possible :+1: After all, Retrievers, Docstores and Pipelines are all tangled together. Once we start refactoring one soon it will be time for the others :slightly_smiling_face: \r\n"

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body: b'@julian-risch and I discussed this idea of splitting the functionality of dense retrievers into two separate nodes (`Embedder` and `Retriever`) and decided for now against this approach. The main reason for this is that training/adapting dense retrieval models would get less intuitive. It would not be clear which node should be responsible for this (Embedder or Retriever), and how this could be designed intuitively for DPR or TableTextRetriever which consist of more than one embedding models, while the potential Embedder node only consists of one embedding model.\r\n\r\n'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'Another remark regarding the solution proposed in the issue description

> to extract the creation of embeddings into a separate node, which could be called "Embedder" or something similar, with the sole task of generating the embeddings. Such node would fit neatly into an indexing pipeline.

We need the creation of embeddings also in the query pipeline to embed an incoming query. Therefore an "Embedder" would then need to be present in both indexing pipeline and query pipeline. So it doesn't really simplify the current situation.'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b'I admit I didn't follow the conversation from the start,  but I might have an idea to contribute. How about extracting the creation of the embeddings in a class that is not a Node?

All functionality related to the creation of embeddings could go in this class, and Retriever could simply instantiate its own instance at creation time. On the other hand, the second node (choose if to call it "embedder" or something different) that also owns its own instance of that class and uses their methods.

So if you need to do training and distilling (which is not done in pipelines) you can use the class directly. In pipelines instead, you have nodes that leverage that class.

What do you think? Can it help in our current situation?'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b"The main downside of having a separate Retriever and Embedder is that we can't easily enforce that the same model is used in both nodes ( -> both pipelines, indexing and querying). If the two nodes use different models, the pipeline will give bad results and users might find it difficult to understand what's causing the issue. Right now, we enforce that the same model is used by re-using the same retriever node in the indexing pipeline and the querying pipeline."

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b'But then I'd rather add an additional field in the document store to allow for this check to be performed: something on the lines of "if this document has an embedding, we also record the name of the model that generated it.".  So at the end this potential mismatch doesn't sound like a blocking issue to me, especially considering the benefits for the codebase and usability.

In a way, such mismatch could happen also now! The fact that we never observed any user doing it is a good sign. I don't see this as being such a large risk.

Happy to take the discussion offline if you think there's more to the matter!'

Title: b'Implementing Generative Pseudo Labeling (GPL)'
Body:
b'UKPLab has recently released a paper and the codebase on Generative Pseudo Labeling. It seems like this could be a useful feature for haystack.

It allows to fine-tune a dense retrieval model on unlabeled data by 1) generating synthetic questions using T5, 2) mining hard negatives using an existing dense retrieval pipeline and 3) creating soft labels using a cross encoder. Step 3) is important because it is making up for errors introduced in step 1) and 2).

Step 1) could be implemented easily by using existing `QuestionGenerator`.
Step 2) could also be implemented easily by using existing `DocumentSearchPipeline`.
Step 3) is a bit more difficult as the existing `SentenceTransformersRanker` only outputs documents so we could either add an argument for outputting the scores or we could just load transformers cross-encoder without using a specific haystack class.

Additionally, we would need to create subclasses of `Trainer` and `DataSilo`, but these should be quite easy as it would just be necessary to override `__init__` and `compute_loss`/`_dataset_from_chunk`.

The training method should probably be a method of `DensePassageReader` similar to the existing `train` method.

The dataset input for this method could either be a file path like the `train` method or a `DocumentStore`.
An advantage of also using a file would be consistency, but using a `DocumentStore` would probably be easier for the user as they would have it in a `DocumentStore` in most use cases anyway.

The results from the different steps could also optionally be saved into a text file (eg. csv file) for caching/debugging. They could also be stored as `Label` objects, but that would probably require too many modifications of the `Label` class.'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b"@vblagoje Here is the issue on adding GPL to Haystack. I'll assign it to you now already but we know that you won't start working on it in the next days. @bogdankostic can support if you would like to discuss ideas or like to get feedback on a draft PR."

Title: b'vblagoje'
Body:
b"Hi @julian-risch, @bogdankostic and @MichelBartels - I'll be implementing GPL this week. From the outset, I wanted to run four design questions/approaches by you. 

1) Document input format. As @MichelBartels suggested - it makes a lot of sense to have DocumentStore as input, but I would also add BEIR format. So we'll support those two formats as input. If users require more input formats, we can add them later. 

2) GPL dependency-free implementation. I am leaning toward an implementation that doesn't require GPL dependency. Yes, GPL has this nice one-liner for training, but it writes the intermediate files to disk, so I'd instead implement GPL directly using only sentence_transformers. Like Nils implemented it in this [collab](https://colab.research.google.com/gist/jamescalam/d2c888775c87f9882bb7c379a96adbc8/gpl-domain-adaptation.ipynb#scrollTo=c2d10c07).  We might reuse some internal components as @MichelBartels  suggested, we don't have to manage yet another dependency and be at the mercy of potential changes in GPL that we might not like. 

3) Is GPL domain adaptation a single atomic transaction? As you know, there are several distinct steps in GPL (@MichelBartels outlined them above). However, two significant steps emerge, as I see it. 
**The first step** involves all three steps outlined above (question generation, negative mining and pseudo labelling). I would treat these three steps as a single transaction. 
**The second step** involves training/adapting retriever on the training data generated in step one.  
My main reason for this delineation is that the first step produces the training data for the second step - an excellent natural border. It seems like an overengineering to checkpoint and restart any of the (question generation, negative mining and pseudo labelling) of the first step. This way, one could restart the second step having the training data saved from the first step, fine-tune the training hyperparameters etc. In addition, one could simply execute these two separate transactions in series and have GPL adaptation done in one shot. 

4) Are we aiming to GPL optimize SBert Bi-encoders and/or DPRs as well? Note that GPL example adaptations are run on SBert Bi-Encoders which are different architecturally to DensePassageRetrievers. Should we support just Bi-encoders or both?"

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body:
b"Hi @vblagoje, looking very much forward to your implementation! Regarding your questions:

1. I like the idea of being able to provide data in BEIR format, this goes well with #2333 where we integrated BEIR to evaluate a certain pipeline.
2. I agree that it would be better to add GPL to haystack without adding another dependency.
3. I think that splitting GPL into **Label Generation** (including question generation, negative mining and pseudo labelling) and **Training** makes sense. This would allow to use the generated training data on different retriever models without having to regenerate them.
4. It would be great to support both SBert Bi-encoders and DPRs. Adding GPL to sentence-transformers models (which are used in our `EmbeddingRetriever`) in Haystack might require a bit more work than adding it to DPR, as we currently don't have any training procedures for models used in `EmbeddingRetriever`.

Happy to answer any further questions and help! :)"

Title: b'Simplify loading of `EmbeddingRetriever`'

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body:
b'I just had an in-depth look into the `EmbeddingRetriever` and came to the conclusion that it might be possible to drop the `model_format` entirely. Currently, we support the following formats: `"farm"`, `"transformers"`, `"sentence_transformers"` and `"retribert"`.

- Both `"farm"` and `"transformers"` use the `_DefaultEmbeddingEncoder` -> these two cases can be merged
- As pointed out in the [SentenceTransformers documentation](https://www.sbert.net/docs/pretrained_models.html#pretrained-models), all `"sentence_transformers"` models are hosted on the HF model hub. Therefore, these models can also be used by `_DefaultEmbeddingEncoder`. To be able to load local sentence transformers models, we would need to make sure [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/5a1e98e3ff6f30faba06c8d7dc337158ab6fc4a0/haystack/modeling/infer.py#L184) that we either use `InferenceProcessor.load_from_dir` (if the model is in farm format) or `Processor.convert_from_transformers` (if the model is in HF transformers format)
- `"retribert"` format can be inferred either from the model name or from `model_type` in `config.json`

As a result, we would just need `_DefaultEmbeddingEncoder` (for `"farm"`, `"transformers"` and `"sentence_transformers"` format) and `_RetribertEmbeddingEncoder` (for `"retribert"` format, which can be inferred from model name or `model_type` in `config.json`).

One concern I still have with this approach is that apparently, as noted in #2301, `_SentenceTransformersEmbeddingEncoder` is a lot faster than `_DefaultEmbeddingEncoder`. I think the reason for this is that the default setting for `max_seq_len` of the `EmbeddingRetriever` is 512. In `_DefaultEmbeddingEncoder`, each input is always padded to `max_seq_len` (512 for the default case), while in `_SentenceTransformersEmbeddingEncoder`, the input texts are sorted by length and each input is only padded to the length of the longest sequence in the same batch.'

Title: b'mathislucka'
Body: b"One concern that I would have is that there might be a future mismatch in sentence transformers and our `_DefaultEmbeddingEncoder` in terms of features. This would mean that we'd have to implement additional features if sentence transformers adds any. I also would not want to miss out on the speed advantage."

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body: b'Another reason why not to remove `_SentenceTransformersEmbeddingEncoder`: In #2388, we are currently implementing GPL, but only for the `_SentenceTransformersEmbeddingEncoder`.'

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body:
b'We decided to keep all `_DefaultEmbeddingEncoder`, `_SentenceTransformersEmbeddingEncoder` and `_RetribertEmbeddingEncoder`.

We also decided to infer the `model_format` parameter automatically like this:

1. If `config_sentence_transformers.json` in model path or in model hub repo, use `_SentenceTransformersEmbeddingEncoder`.

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b"Hello @HighDeFing you can find the hyperparameter settings that we used for training a German DPR model in this paper: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2104.12741.pdf

> ...For the training, queries are clipped after 32 tokens and passages after 300 tokens. The learning
rate is 106 using Adam, linear scheduling with
warm-up, and dropout rate 0.1. With a batch size
of 40, the model achieves an average in-batch rank
of 0.50 after training for 20 epochs and the average
rank does not further improve after more epochs...

We also found that the difficulty of the in-batch negatives have a strong influence on the training process. These in-batch negatives shouldn't be neither too simple (too dissimilar to the relevant document) nor too difficult (too similar to the relevant document). Make sure your dataset is shuffled and not ordered by topic or something like that.

The `evaluate_every` parameter doesn't have an effect on the accuracy of the trained model. It's just for monitoring the progress during the training. If you set it too low, the training will be interrupted with an evaluation and thus it will slow down the training process.

I would recommend to keep `grad_acc_steps` at 1. I am not 100% sure that the gradient accumulation implementation works correctly. It might well be correct but I am not sure.

`batch_size` shouldn't be too small. I wouldn't recommend to use a `batch_size` smaller than 10. With a larger `batch_size` the training will be more stable. As you can see in the paper, we used 40, which requires a lot of GPU memory. 10 to 20 should also be fine if your GPU doesn't allow more. 

Please let us know if you have more questions or whether we can close this issue.

Good luck with your training!  "

Title: b'Rethink inputs to `run_batch`'
Body: b"In #1239, we decided that the `run_batch` method should be able to handle both `str` and `List[str]` as argument to `queries`.  In the corresponding PR #2481 the [question](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2481#discussion_r862880048) came up whether it might make sense to only allow `List[str]` as argument `queries`.\r\n\r\nLet's use this issue to come up with advantages and disadvantages of both options and make a decision."

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body:
b"So far, I can think of the following advantages for changing the type of `queries` in `run_batch` from `Union[str, List[str]]` to `List[str]`:
- Required input to `run_batch` gets more intuitive 
      -> `run_batch` **always** runs a batch (= list) of queries
- Code will become less complex
     -> In most batch methods (for example [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/a2a99f79b141d1bbecc15d0d45ebacae2fc348e8/haystack/nodes/reader/farm.py#L1087)), we check whether the user passed a single string or a list of strings as argument for `queries`. This case distinction can be dropped.
- Return type of a lot of methods can be simplified
      -> In a lot of methods, we return `Union[List[Document], List[List[Document]]]` depending on whether a single query or a list of queries is supplied. This will be simplified to `List[List[Document]]`, for example [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/a2a99f79b141d1bbecc15d0d45ebacae2fc348e8/haystack/nodes/retriever/sparse.py#L216).

Disadvantages that I can think of are that one functionality gets lost: Currently, it is possible, to use a retriever-reader pipeline in the following way:

1. Supply a single query string to the pipeline's `run_batch` method
2. Retriever retrieves top-k relevant documents.
3. Reader applies the single query to each retrieved document individually and returns top-k answers for each of the documents.

I think, though, that this is not really a common use case.
     "

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body:
b'We decided to only allow `List[str]` as type for `queries` argument in `run_batch`

The lost functionality can be achieved without `run_batch` in the following way:
```python
answers = []
relevant_docs = retriever.retrieve(query=QUERY_STR)
for doc in relevant_docs:
    cur_answers = reader.predict(query=QUERY_STR, documents=[doc])
    answers.append(cur_answers)
```'

Title: b'WeaviateDocumentStore bug - weaviate has an internal query limit, so `.update_embeddings()` will loop forever if hits that'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
FYI - @ZanSara @bogdankostic 
The latest version of the `WeaviateDocumentStore` has a bug, which comes up when calling `.update_embedddings()` on a collection with more than 10k documents.
The bug was introduced by recent commit https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/commit/ae712fe6bf087c717f3e38e4e87d2347165fc12b#diff-d4e4f2566db6c2fbe852debffcf7830447ecb969d4cdcce6d796fd773eba379bR682

**Error message**
No error, it gets into a forever loop never completing - due to a `while` loop never turning false.

**Expected behavior**
The `WeaviateDocumentStore` should be able to update the embeddings of ALL documents and should not be limited by the Weaviate query limit (`QUERY_MAXIMUM_RESULTS`, which is 10k by default). Or if it is limited, then at minimum it should throw an error explaining that it cannot update all documents only up to the `QUERY_MAXIMUM_RESULTS`, instead of getting into a forever loop when hitting the 10k records and not being able to go further.

**Additional context**"
Unfortunately fixing it is not as simple as just increasing the `QUERY_MAXIMUM_RESULTS` to infinity.
Quoting the Weaviate documentation, it is NOT recommended to increase the `QUERY_MAXIMUM_RESULTS` to too high. See:
_"Due to the increasing cost of each page outlined above, there is a limit to how many objects can be retrieved using pagination. By default setting the sum of offset and limit to higher than 10,000 objects, will lead to an error. If you must retrieve more than 10,000 objects, you can increase this limit by setting the environment variable QUERY_MAXIMUM_RESULTS=<desired-value>. Warning: **Setting this to arbitrarily high values can make the memory consumption of a single query explode and single queries can slow down the entire cluster.** We recommend setting this value to the lowest possible value that does not interfere with your users expectations."_
https://weaviate.io/developers/weaviate/current/graphql-references/filters.html

**To Reproduce**
Try to run the Haystack-Weaviate example published by Laura Ham: 
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BkozaOnZpJI
GitHub: https://github.com/semi-technologies/weaviate-examples/tree/main/harrypotter-qa-haystack-weaviate

This example dataset has 13k records and uses default Weaviate settings, which has `QUERY_MAXIMUM_RESULTS` set to 10k, so it will hang forever when calling `.update_embeddings(), which will hit that forever loop at https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/caf13364243807b873d74b9f4f2448ce2cec60f0/haystack/document_stores/weaviate.py#L693 (as the query can only return 10k records, but it is expecting to receive 13k, so it will keep querying forever).

**FAQ Check**
- [ X ] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?

**System:**
 - OS: Ubuntu
 - GPU/CPU: GPU
 - Haystack version (commit or version number): 1.4.0
 - DocumentStore: Weaviate
 - Reader: deepset/tinyroberta-squad2
 - Retriever: sentence-transformers/multi-qa-mpnet-base-dot-v1
'

Title: b'Validation of Ray pipelines'
Body:
b'**Problem**
Ray pipelines do not conform fully to the JSON schema we defined for regular Pipelines. Therefore they will often fail validation, even though they are completely valid.

**Solution**
Define a new schema for Ray pipelines and validate them against it. We could heavily leverage the existing JSON schema generation code to do so.

**Alternatives**
Relaxing the schema to allow bot regular and Ray pipelines could lead to a lot of confusion about which attributes are valid where. Also, given that the pipeline type was an attribute value, selecting different structures based on it would have been quite convoluted in the schema. I believe separate schemas are much more clear.
'

b"I decided to separate the validation of Ray pipelines when I noticed that they have an extra parameter in the pipelines attributes: `replicas` https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/6fb58d09a9ac0f6895bbbb9e617d459b5f27f155/test/samples/pipeline/test_ray_pipeline.yaml#L38-L44

The fact is that I am not sure how many of these additional params there are, whether they are mandatory, etc. So I thought taking this specific topic out of the main PR was wiser. 

I think all answers are in the code of `RayPipeline` so I don't expect to have trouble with it, but I'll surely reach out to @oryx1729 in case of doubts."

Title: b'`QuestionGenerator` causes CUDA-out-of-memory-error for large Documents'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
For very large Documents, the `QuestionGenerator` will run into a CUDA out of memory error. The reason for this is that  at [this line of code](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/89bb1ca1399f8b76a7a23f4f8b8d5a46b619533f/haystack/nodes/question_generator/question_generator.py#L102), we are splitting the input text into smaller chunks based on the provided split_length parameter.  If the input text is very large, we will have a loooot of smaller text chunks. [Here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/89bb1ca1399f8b76a7a23f4f8b8d5a46b619533f/haystack/nodes/question_generator/question_generator.py#L117) we are giving all of the text chunks as input to the model at the same time, resulting in the out-of-memory error (there are to many text chunks to fit into memory simultaneously).

To prevent this, we should add the possibility to set a `batch_size` parameter. Like this, the user can control how many smaller text chunks are fed to the model at the same time.

**Error message**
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 474.00 MiB (GPU 0; 15.78 GiB total capacity; 13.27 GiB already allocated; 272.00 MiB free; 14.16 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
```

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here, like document types / preprocessing steps / settings of reader etc.

**To Reproduce**
```python
from datasets import load_dataset
from haystack.nodes import QuestionGenerator


# Get data
dataset = load_dataset('nreimers/trec-covid', split='train')

corpus = []
for row in dataset:
    if len(row['title']) > 20 and len(row['text']) > 100:
        text = row['title'] + " " + row['text']

        text_lower = text.lower()

        if 'covid' in text_lower or 'corona' in text_lower or 'sars-cov-2' in text_lower:
            corpus.append(text)

        if len(corpus) >= 17:
            break

print("Len Corpus:", len(corpus))

qg = QuestionGenerator(model_name_or_path="doc2query/msmarco-t5-base-v1", max_length=64, split_length=128)
questions = []
for doc in corpus:
    cur_questions = qg.generate(doc)
    questions.append(cur_questions)
```


**System:**
 - OS: Ubuntu 20
 - GPU/CPU: GPU
 - Haystack version (commit or version number): current master

'

Title: b'Improve warnings for write operations of `DeepsetCloudDocumentStore`'
Body:
b'Currently the `DeepsetCloudDocumentStore` raises an exception if you want to write files. To allow users to test their pipelines without having to create an other documentstore first (e.g. elasticsearch) we want to "allow" these write operations by logging the results and logging a warning instead of writing the actual results to a database. 

Implementation: 
- log results of the indexing run `indexing_pipeline.run(path=...)` 
- add a warning like: `This is only a preview of the documents that would be generated by running an indexing pipeline in  deepset cloud. To add these documents to the index, pleas upload your files and deploy the indexing pipeline.`

Since this workflow is the prioritized workflow (connecting to empty index) instead of creating a different docstore first (#2402) we should implement this first. We would still need this warning if users want to `migrate a pipeline to DC` that previously used  a different document store during local development (#2402)'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body: b"Hello @FabianHertwig, unfortunately the YAML definition can't contain function calls, only static values, so you won't be able to authenticate properly with it. On the other hand, I believe it's not a big deal to modify `setup_pipelines` to use code instead of a YAML: the two options are not designed to have the same expressive power, and in this case you're clearly better off with code. I'd recommend you to stay on your current solution.\r\n\r\nIf you really need to use YAML for any reason though, there is a workaround: you can use a simple docstore (for example `InMemoryDocumentStore`) in the YAML, and then, once the pipeline is loaded, swap out the docstore with OpenSearch. Although possible, this is way uglier than simply initializing the pipeline in code, so I hope you don't really need YAML so desperately :smile: "

Title: b'baregawi'
Body: b'PyMilvus updated to version 2.0.0 on January 25th and that is now what gets installed from PyPI by default so recent recent farm-haystack installations have been breaking. I fixed this issue by installing `pymilvus==1.1.2`. I am certain that the error comes from trying to use `pymilvus==2.0.0`. It is easy to confirm by reading the code, doing the imports and checking versions yourself. So my guess is that you are did not install `pymilvus==1.1.2` in a way that haystack is accessing that pymilvus version.'

Title: b'baregawi'
Body:
b"For those who have tried `pip install pymilvus==1.1.2` and have not found success you can try uninstalling haystack and reinstalling it again with a constraints file:
`pip install -c constraints.txt farm-haystack` 
With the contents of constraints.txt as:
`pymilvus==1.1.2`

Or for short:
```
pip uninstall farm-haystack
echo 'pymilvus==1.1.2' > /tmp/constraints.txt
pip install -c constraints.txt farm-haystack
```"

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b"Hi @ShabRa1365 sorry to hear that you are still having problems with getting Haystack to run. I'm happy to help. I think there was a misunderstanding. There is no need to create a new virtual machine. I meant a virtual environment for python. How you can create such a virtual environment depends on your own setup and is different from user to user. For example, what I use is is [conda](https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/user-guide/install/index.html):
`conda create --name py39v130 python=3.9 -y` and then afterwards `conda activate py39v130` to activate the virtual environment. The steps required to install Haystack are then really just:
```
git clone https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack.git
cd haystack
pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -e '.[all-gpu]'
```

I can only guess what's causing the problem on you side. Either it's a python version that is not compatible with Haystack or some dependencies that are already installed but incompatible with Haystack. You can check what python you are using with `which python`, similarly you can check with `which pip` and `which pip3` what pip you are using. For example, on my system `pip` and `pip3` point to the same installation of pip.
With `pip list` you can check what dependencies are already installed (before running `pip install -e '.[all-gpu]'`). `torch` must be lower than 1.11 so if you already have torch 1.11 installed that will cause problems. You can see the limitations on dependencies compatible with Haystack here: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/setup.cfg#L56"

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b"Hi @HighDeFing we have [benchmarks](https://haystack.deepset.ai/benchmarks/latest) with the section _Retriever Performance_ showing also the _indexing speed_ (in docs/sec). You're right that updating the model requires to re-calculate the embeddings of all indexed documents. Uploading a few new documents though requires only to calculate embeddings for those. Does that answer your question?

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b"You could try to set a larger `batch_size` (default is 32 in EmbeddingRetriever) up until you are using all the memory of your GPU. Title: b'Version check is too restrictive'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
Currently when trying to load a saved pipeline YAML in older or newer versions of haystack it fails because the version is incompatible (i.e. a schema change occured). In most cases the YAML would be perfectly fine if just the version had been updated. From a usage point of view this is no good behavior given the fast pace of haystack releases. The user would always when there's a schema change update her YAML manually or at some point set it to "unstable" because they got frustrated. In addition the user needs to know the current haystack version to update the version. Currently the appropriate message that points the user to the compatible haystack versions is not shown because schema validation fails upfront.

**Error message**
`Validation failed. '1.1.0' is not valid under any of the given schemas. The error is in 'version'. See the stacktrace for more information.`

**Expected behavior**
Version check should show which versions are compatible and at least we should provide an option to not check the version string. We technically provide this by having the "unstable" one. But this implies that something is not right given the bad connotation of "unstable". Additionally the user would have to set the YAML to unstable manually as we always save YAMLs with the current haystack version. 

**Additional context**
We cannot upload YAMLs from older or newer versions of haystack to Deepset Cloud because of this. E.g. uploading from haystack 1.1.0 fails with error message `Failed to validate pipeline.yaml, with error Validation failed. '1.1.0' is not valid under any of the given schemas. The error is in 'version'. See the stacktrace for more information.`

**To Reproduce**
Try to load YAML with version "1.1.0" within haystack 1.3.0.'

Title: b'Allow for batch querying when using Pipelines'
Body:
b"Same larger goal as #1168 but for querying instead of indexing.

As discussed with @oryx1729 and @tholor, we'd like to design the node and Pipeline APIs so that batches of queries can be processed together. This will allow for a better user experience but also allows in future for batch optimizations to speed up querying. Note that we're here focusing first on designing the interfaces. The optimization can be handled separately for each node in different issues.

One design choice we decided upon is have explicit separation of the _single_ and _batch_ functions. This will make for a clear user experience, and avoid any ambiguity for developers looking into the code. More specifically we want to avoid any uncertainty in the input and output formats of nodes.

The following methods should be implemented:
```
Pipeline.run(query)
Pipeline.run_batch(queries)

Node.run()
Node.run_batch()
```
If we call `Pipeline.run_batch()` every node should be executed using their `Node.run_batch()` method, not `Node.run()`.
In particular, @bogdankostic and @julian-risch agreed in the refinement of this issue that `Pipeline.run_batch()` should be implemented with the following signature and should return a list of the elements usually returned by `run()`:
```
def run_batch(
        self,
        queries: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None,
        file_paths: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        labels: Optional[Union[MultiLabel, List[MultiLabel]]] = None,
        documents: Optional[Union[List[Document], List[List[Document]]]] = None,
        meta: Optional[Union[Dict[str, Any], List[Dict[str, Any]]]] = None,
        params: Optional[dict] = None
        debug: Optional[bool] = None
```
There might be use cases when the same query is executed separately on different sets of documents. Therefore queries is still allowed to be a single query.
Note that every query in the batch needs to use the same `params` for now. Otherwise, optimization will be hardly possible. We could change that limitation in future if necessary.

`file_paths` and `meta` are so far only used in indexing pipelines. If they are set, we should call `run()` instead of `run_batch` or trigger an error message if that is impossible.
Note that we should allow for flexibility in the format of the metadata passed into `Pipeline.run_batch()`. If it is a single meta dictionary, it should be applied to all queries. If it is a list, it should be one meta dict for each query.


Further, every node's `predict_batch()` should have a `batch_size` param that can be passed via `params`.

For now, a `Node.run_batch()` can be implemented in a naive, non-optimized way by simply calling `Node.run()` multiple times in a loop and split queries, labels, documents and meta if necessary so that the run() method is called with a single query/list of document. The individual results need to be collected in a list of results.
As an alternative, BaseComponent could implement `run_batch()` by calling the node's `run()` method.

The FARMReader already has a `predict_batch()` method that can be use: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/f33c2b987a461dbc07bdc1a6b3eb94f99ef75f68/haystack/nodes/reader/farm.py#L528
For the transformer based models, we could make use of transformer's pipeline batching mechanism: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main_classes/pipelines#pipeline-batching
However, docs say 

> All pipelines (except zero-shot-classification and question-answering currently) can use batching."

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b'Hey @aruroyc, I'm not too familiar with the `--preload` flag either, but reading the documentation I think I have a clue of what's going on.

 `--preload` "load application code before the worker processes are forked."(https://docs.gunicorn.org/en/stable/settings.html#preload-app). The fact is that our REST API for Haystack 1.0.0 used to do a lot of operations at import time: namely, they were loading all the nodes and setting up the pipeline.

I have the impression that:
- You're using a dense retriever, and as such modified the REST API to compute the embeddings.
- The code calculating the embeddings is executed at import time

Is any of this true? If you modified the REST API, could you share your changes?

A possible solution would be to upgrade Haystack and the REST API to 1.3.0. Plenty of improvements there, including a refactoring of the REST API that now do not load the pipeline at import time anymore. However, from 1.0.0 you might have to migrate a few things: proceed with care and skim through the changelog before jumping on the next version. As an alternative, I believe you have to find a way to defer the creation of embeddings at any point after import time: this is likely to allow the workers to boot and fork without meeting with any timeout.
