Title: b'Generalize <sep> token of QuestionGenerator node'
Body:
b'**Issue**
Right now the docstring of the QuestionGenerator says the class supports [any Seq2SeqLM model](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/cb881b6fa9c73639440c86f2645ba778d0a93b81/haystack/nodes/question_generator/question_generator.py#L38-L39). However, it [assumes](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/cb881b6fa9c73639440c86f2645ba778d0a93b81/haystack/nodes/question_generator/question_generator.py#L109) the generated questions are separeted by a "<sep>" string.

From my understanding this is the case right now for most Question Generation models on the hub. However, the separator between questions could in general be any string (e.g. ["[SEP]"](https://github.com/patil-suraj/question_generation/blob/bffa0a51e3ecba3922cafd13f424521135677303/prepare_data.py#L65)).

**Proposed changes**
To generalize this class to models with different sep tokens I propose to first look whether `tokenizer.sep_token` is set. If so, this string representation should be used to split the questions. If not, a default "<sep>" string is used. The token should also be in the init parameters, since [sometimes the question separator is not explicitly set as "sep_token"](https://github.com/patil-suraj/question_generation/blob/bffa0a51e3ecba3922cafd13f424521135677303/prepare_data.py#L153). In this case, the user of the QuestionGenerator class would need to explicitly provide the separator.

I know right now it is kind of a theoretical issue, since there are only a few Question Generation models out there, and they work with the current code. But hopefully we'll have some more QG models in the future:) If you think this change makes sense, I'd be happy to contribute it.


'

Title: b'Is it possible to add a code for Visual QA on Bar Charts, Pie Charts and Visualizations ?'
Body: b'Chart question answering (CQA) is a newly proposed visual question answering (VQA) task where an algorithm must answer questions about data visualizations, e.g. bar charts, pie charts, and line graphs. CQA requires capabilities that natural-image VQA algorithms lack: fine-grained measurements, optical character recognition, and handling out-of-vocabulary words in both questions and answers. Without modifications, state-of-the-art VQA algorithms perform poorly on this task. Here, we propose a novel CQA algorithm called parallel recurrent fusion of image and language (PReFIL). PReFIL first learns bimodal embeddings by fusing question and image features and then intelligently aggregates these learned embeddings to answer the given question. Despite its simplicity, PReFIL greatly surpasses state-of-the art systems and human baselines on both the FigureQA and DVQA datasets. Additionally, we demonstrate that PReFIL can be used to reconstruct tables by asking a series of questions about a chart.'

Title: b'ArzelaAscoIi'
Body:
b'Hi @ZanSara , sorry for confusion. The yaml is indeed valid. The case I am talking about can be tested with this script: 

```py

            - name: TextFileConverter
              inputs: [File]
            - name: Preprocessor
              inputs: [ TextFileConverter]
            - name: Retriever
              inputs: [Preprocessor]
            - name: DocumentStore
              inputs: [Retriever]
"""
config = yaml.safe_load(PIPELINE_YAML)
validate_config(config)  # this wont throw an exception
generate_code(config, pipeline_name="query")  # this will throw the exception "KeyError: 'Reader'"

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b'Ok actually a very quick inspection made me realize the issue here.

This one is in between a naming issue and an unintuitive API design. The fact is that `validate_config` **does not validate the graph**: that step happens only in `load_from_config`. `validate_config` just checks that all the config abides the schema, not that the graph defined by the nodes is actually valid.

However, your issue has no solution at the moment. `load_from_config` check the graph while building it, so if you want to check that the YAML is valid without loading any node, there's no clean way in the current API. You're cleverly using `generate_code` here, which simply _assumes_ the graph is valid: so when it is not, it fails, providing you the "validation" step you were looking for.

I will definitely proceed to extract the graph validation step in a separate API that can be invoked stand-alone on any YAML. Being able to fully validate YAML files before loading the pipelines is indeed quite important.'

Title: b'MLFlowLogging always disabled for training `FARMReader` models'
Body:
b"**Describe the bug**
When training a Reader model, a user might want to log training statistics and metrics to MLFlow. However, when initializing a `FARMReader`, we initialize an `Inferencer`. There, we call `MLFlowLogger.disable()` on [this line](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/15c70bdb9f8cd16511d1eb9ed9b2e9466de65cbf/haystack/modeling/infer.py#L77), which disables all logging to MLFlow. Therefore, when a user is calling the Reader's `train` method after initializing the Reader, no tranining statistics wil be logged.

As a workaround, the user can manually set `MLFlowLogger.disable_logging = False` before calling the `train` method."

Title: b'Rename `pipeline_config`'
Body:
b'I believe this concept needs renaming.

The issues with `pipeline_config` can be summarized as:
- is not very descriptive, quite vague for such a specific concept.
- it should point out the plurality, so at least it could become `pipelineS_config`

One fundamental issue brought to light by this name is that in many part of the stack we address an object containing the definition of several nodes and several pipeline graphs using those nodes. This object has currently no name and is usually referred to with some mix of `config`, `definition`, `yaml` according to where it's fetched from and how it's sliced. Worst of all, in some cases it's just called `pipeline`, which is actively misleading as this object might contain several the graphs of several pipelines.

We should agree on a name for this object, document it and refactor the codebase to use it consistently and clearly. Some "sane" options for the name of this object might be:
- Bundle
- Stack
- Pipeline Group (quite long)

so that  `pipeline_config` would become `bundle_config` or `stack_config`.

Some other, a bit more exotic, could be:
- Set (a bit vague)
- App (quite vague too)
- Chart (Chart of Pipelines?)
- Cohort (usually refers to people)
- Network (sounds like an alternative to a Pipeline, not a group of them)
- Plumbing :smile: 
- Manifest (although `manifest_config` sounds a tad odd).

Any other idea is welcome.

@oryx1729 @julian-risch @tstadel @bogdankostic '

Title: b'Improve Document Relevance Scores in ElasticSearch'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Out of the box, document relevance scores returned by ElasticSearch are unbound. However, we would like to convert these scores to probabilities in a meaningful way. The score should estimate how likely the document satisfies the information need of the user given the query.

The current implementation is here: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/document_stores/elasticsearch.py#L1306 
It scales the scores but this scaling does not always work and is not flexible enough, e.g., with varying length of documents/queries, tfidf scores, etc.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
An alternative to what we currently have could be the following: Given a query, let's estimate the max (raw) score that a document could have that satisfies the information need. Given this max (raw) score and the raw scores of each document when can calculate: `(raw score of returned document)/(max raw score)`. This converted score then estimates how close the returned document is to an ideal document.
The difficulty here is the calculation of the max score, which need to take into account the internal formula of Elasticsearch, something like:
`score(q,d)  =  queryNorm(q)   coord(q,d)   (tf(t in d) idf(t)   t.getBoost()  norm(t,d)) (t in q)`

@Timoeller let's discuss some other ideas as well. For example, users could calibrate the magic number that we have in the current formula."

Title: b'Timoeller'
Body: b'I like the idea of normalizing with a max score but are unsure about your suggestion. So you are saying that the score varies (a lot) depending on query length? This means we would need to normalize the score for each query separately. Is this computationally fast?\r\n\r\n@mathislucka also proposed a min-max scaling based on a couple of QA/IR datasets out there to see what are good default values. Wouldnt that be a valid quick fix? '

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b"The suggestion by Mathis is what I would call calibration and that could be a good quick fix. Essential is that the raw scores on the datasets that you use for calibration are similar to the data that you would like to use in production. That includes similar tf-idf values and doc/query length, etc. Only experiments could tell us what the impact of the different terms is.\r\n\r\nThe other approach that I suggested above indeed needs to calculate a different max score for every query. I don't think this calculation will have a noticeable effect on query speed. Maybe a topic for a hacky friday. "

Title: b'mathislucka'
Body: b'I think a calibration dataset or multiple calibration datasets could also be useful for other scoring systems like dot product based scores in EmbeddingRetrievers or Scores that come from a CrossEncoder/Ranker. We could even give the user an option to calibrate the scores themselves by passing in a custom dataset that can be used for calibration.\r\n\r\nI like the idea proposed by @julian-risch but one issue with the approach might be that it produces weird results when dealing with queries of different length. A longer query might produce a low score in terms of how high is this score compared to the theoretical max score, but it can still be a very relevant result. Also, it does not work for dot product or Ranker scores.'

Title: b'`top_k` in `ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever` has no effect when using `ElasticsearchDocumentStore`'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
Using `top_k` with `ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever` has no effect because `ElasticsearchDocumentStore.query` does not consider `top_k` if `query is None`. It seems the default number returned is `10`, which happens to be the default `top_k`.

**Expected behavior**
If there are more than `top_k` documents after applying filters, then `ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever.retrieve` should return `top_k` documents.
If there are less than `top_k` documents after applying filters, then `ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever.retrieve` should return all documents.

**Cause**
The `if query is None` branch does not apply `body["size"] = str(top_k)`, hence why `top_k` has no effect.
https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/692cde11e736884cbd1a5f99416cee94c4f0921b/haystack/document_stores/elasticsearch.py#L1053-L1059

**Happy to implement this and make a PR if I get the go-ahead :)**'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b'Hi @adri1wald thanks for pointing out this issue and great to see that you already suggest a fix.  I think the reason why the "Naive retrieval without BM25, only filtering" part of the code doesn\'t use the `top_k` parameter is that the returned documents have no relevance scores and thus cannot be sorted. Therefore, it is not well defined which of the relevant documents are returned if there are more than `top_k`.\r\nI would say the expected behavior of the ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever is to return all documents that match the given filter and not use a `top_k` at all. Do you know whether that\'s currently the case or does it always return no more than 10 documents? '

b'Ah, thanks for the reminder @mathislucka . Yes, the limitation to 10 documents most likely comes from Elasticsearch. @adri1wald A quick fix could be to add `"size"` to the query body, setting it to the maximum that Elasticsearch allows by default for example:
```
 body = {"size": 10000, "query": {"bool": {"must": {"match_all": {}}}}}  # type: Dict[str, Any]
```
A better solution would be to use the `scan` functionality as used in the `get_all_documents` method:
https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/692cde11e736884cbd1a5f99416cee94c4f0921b/haystack/document_stores/elasticsearch.py#L898

Could you maybe just call `get_all_documents` with the filters set within `ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever.retrieve` instead of the `ElasticsearchDocumentStore.query` method?'

Title: b'adri1wald'
Body:
b"Hey @julian-risch @mathislucka!

Thanks for taking a look at this.

My usecase is definitely met by getting all the filtered documents. I really like the idea of using `get_all_documents` in `ElasticsearchFilterOnlyRetriever.retrieve`. I will implement that for our project now.

Happy to make the same change in haystack and submit a PR once I've made it work for us! Also, if the semantics of `top_k` without a `query` don't make sense, might it also be reasonable to entirely remove the code for handling `query is None` in `ElasticsearchDocumentStore.query` (and change the method signature to `query: str`)?

If you're interested:

I'm trying to build a question generation pipeline that retrieves all the documents given some filters, samples `k` documents, and then runs question generation. The sampling is useful because question generation is slow (there can be > 1000 docs after filtering), and even if it was fast it would generate an unmanageable amount of questions for a user. With this pipeline a user gets a reasonable amount of questions back, and they can generate questions on a different sample by pressing a refresh button.

I think a more effective way to achieve this would be something like a `DocumentStore.sample_documents(self, sample_k: int, filters...)` method that performs the sampling within the store backend, but I don't know if this is possible with Elasticsearch (or indeed any other store backend)."

Title: b'mathislucka'
Body:
b"I think the storage backends do not support random samples. I think what I'd do when implementing this as a custom node:

- have a separate index where you store all ids as metadata in a single document
- retrieve all ids from that index
- take a random sample of the id list
- query the actual document index with the sampled ids and `get_documents_by_id`"

Title: b'Discrepancy between no_answer score definition in `QuestionAnsweringHead` and `FARMReader`'
Body:
b"**Describe the bug**
For calculating meaningful no_answer scores all answer candidates from all retrieved documents have to be considered.

`QuestionAnsweringHead` calculates no_answer score and confidence in https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/96a538b18238ce723208cd18a1c11034ee5a90d1/haystack/modeling/model/prediction_head.py#L792 and sorts the results according to this value. By doing this, `QuestionAnsweringHead` assumes that all the retrieved documents have been passed along as one dataset in order to calculate a global no_answer score.

`FARMReader` however passes each retrieved document separately to the `QuestionAnsweringHead` using the `QAInferencer`. That's why `FARMReader` has its own no_answer score calculation logic in https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/96a538b18238ce723208cd18a1c11034ee5a90d1/haystack/nodes/reader/base.py#L53
This logic differs from the one in `QuestionAnsweringHead` resulting in different rankings (e.g. no_answer jumps to the first place in `FARMReader` while it would be on the second in `QuestionAnsweringHead` or vice versa). 

Whether the one or the other is better is hard to say. Some tests on SQuAD datasets however suggest that `FARMReader`'s definition might have advantages over `QuestionAnsweringHead`'s. Anyways this introduces an discrepancy between `reader.eval()` and `pipeline.eval()` as the former uses `QuestionAnsweringHead`'s no_answer scores and the latter `FARMReader`'s.

**Additional context**
`FARMReader`'s no_answer score logic is actually implemented in `BaseReader` which means it also affects `TransformerReader`.

**Expected behavior**
There's one consistent definition of no_answer scores.

**To Reproduce**
E.g use script from https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/2216#issuecomment-1090232185 "

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b'I have to admit the crawler is really quite undocumented... so I decided to put together a small tutorial for you two :slightly_smiling_face: @TuanaCelik Maybe worth adding to the tutorials folder somewhere?

Anyway, here is the code. I hope it helps you figure out how to make the Crawler work in your pipelines.

```python
################################################################################
#                                                                              #
#                           CRAWLER EXAMPLE                                    #
#                                                                              #
#  NOTE: You need a running Elasticsearch container for this to work.          #
#  If you don't have, change ElasticsearchDocumentStore with something else,   #
#  like SQLDocumentStore or InMemoryDocumentStore, but the code is untested    #
#  on them and you might meet with bugs.                                       #
#                                                                              #
################################################################################

from haystack.pipelines import Pipeline
from haystack.nodes import Crawler, PreProcessor, ElasticsearchRetriever, FARMReader
from haystack.document_stores import ElasticsearchDocumentStore


# Create the document store. You need this to:
#  1. store the documents you crawled and preprocessed (with an indexing pipeline)
#  2. extract the documents that contains the answer to your question (with a query pipeline)
document_store = ElasticsearchDocumentStore(host="localhost", username="", password="", index="document")


#
# Step 1: Get the data, clean it and store it
#

# NOTE: You need to run this code just once, every time you create a new Elasticsearch container. Comment it out afterwards.

# Let's create the indexing pipeline. It will contain
#  1. A crawler node that fetches text from a website
#  2. A PreProcessor that makes the documents friendly to the retriever
#  3. The Document Store at the end, that will receive the documents and store them
crawler = Crawler(
    urls=["https://haystack.deepset.ai"],   # Websites to crawl
    crawler_depth=1,    # How many links to follow
    output_dir="crawled_files",  # Not very important, we don't use the files in this example
)
preprocessor = PreProcessor(
    clean_empty_lines=True,
    clean_whitespace=True,
    clean_header_footer=False,
    split_by="word",
    split_length=500,
    split_respect_sentence_boundary=True,
)
indexing_pipeline = Pipeline()
indexing_pipeline.add_node(component=crawler, name="crawler", inputs=['File'])
indexing_pipeline.add_node(component=preprocessor, name="preprocessor", inputs=['crawler'])
indexing_pipeline.add_node(component=document_store, name="document_store", inputs=['preprocessor'])

indexing_pipeline.run(params={"crawler": {'return_documents': True}})


#
# Step 2: Use the data to answer questions
#

# NOTE: You can run this code as many times as you like.

# Let's create a query pipeline. It will contain
#  1. A Retriever that gets the relevant documents from the document store
#  2. A Reader that locates the answers inside the documents
retriever = ElasticsearchRetriever(document_store=document_store)
reader =  FARMReader(model_name_or_path="deepset/roberta-base-squad2-distilled")

query_pipeline = Pipeline()
query_pipeline.add_node(component=retriever, name="retriever", inputs=["Query"])
query_pipeline.add_node(component=reader, name="reader", inputs=["retriever"])

results = query_pipeline.run(query="What can I use Haystack for?")

print("\nQuestion: ", results["query"])
print("\nAnswers:")
for answer in results["answers"]:
    print("- ", answer.answer)
print("\n\n")

```

Keep in mind that there are many more ways to use the Crawler. This is just one that came to my mind. Happy to help you out if something still refuses to work.'

Title: b'tstadel'
Body:
b"Discrepancies had 4 reasons:
- inclusion of no_answers in `reader.eval` (a huge fraction were no_answer actually (>95%) and most of them are right)
  -> PR will expose additional metrics that do not use no_answers (this has a huge impact on getting same values)
- `reader.eval` calculates top_1 metrics only while `pipeline.eval` naturally returns top_n metrics.
  -> PR will expose additional metrics that calculate top_n versions of em and f1 (this has a big impact on getting same values)
- bug in reader.eval's label creation mechanism that messed up labels where the last token of a sequence was part of the answer
  -> PR fixes this (this has a small impact on getting same values)
- `pipeline.eval` normalizes strings of answers and predictions before calculating metrics.
  -> cannot be fixed as `reader.eval` works on token_ids only (this has a small impact on getting same values)
"

Title: b'Wrong encoder instance for a sbert-based retriever?'
Body:
b'**Question**
Hi! When I instance a retriever in this way:

```python
from haystack.nodes import EmbeddingRetriever

retriever = EmbeddingRetriever(
    document_store=document_store, 
    embedding_model="sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2"
)
```

I've noticed that the `model_format` property of the `EmbeddingRetriever` instance is always set to `farm`. So an instance of `_DefaultEmbeddingEncoder` is created instead of an instance of `_SentenceTransformersEmbeddingEncoder`.

This implies that `inference_from_dicts` is called when calling `document_store.update_embeddings()` but it I guess it should be not needed for Sentence Transformers model embeddings (it takes a lot more time).

To make things run faster, one should do:

```python
from haystack.nodes import EmbeddingRetriever

retriever = EmbeddingRetriever(
    document_store=document_store,
    embedding_model="sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2",
    model_format="sentence_transformers"
)
```

Title: b'Typing issue on `BaseComponent.run()`, `documents` parameter'
Body:
b"The `documents` parameter of the `BaseComponent.run()` method seems to have an issue with typing.

In `BaseComponent`, `documents` is `List[Document]`. This type is respected in query pipelines, but not in indexing pipelines, where `documents` mostly receives `List[dict]`. This causes mypy to throw a bunch of errors which must be, and are, silenced in many nodes. Examples:
- PreProcessor: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/69a0c9f2edc48e25e4633d6154ad1af4035996e6/haystack/preprocessor/base.py#L42
- Retriever: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/69a0c9f2edc48e25e4633d6154ad1af4035996e6/haystack/retriever/base.py#L183
- DocumentStore: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/69a0c9f2edc48e25e4633d6154ad1af4035996e6/haystack/document_store/base.py#L289

This is not a big issue per-se (all the affected nodes work just fine), but makes hard and confusing for people to contribute new nodes on the indexing side. It's even more confusing in case of nodes, like the `EntityExtractor`, that can be used on both query and indexing pipelines.
"

Title: b'Make `PreProcessor` support `Document` objects'
Body:
b'**Problem**
Right now PreProcessor (as many other "indexing" nodes) do not really support `Document` objects, I don't see a reason why that should be the case other than legacy. In addition, the current error message is highly misleading because, given a Document, PreProcessor will complain that the given value is "neither a list nor a Document", when it should say "neither a list nor a dictionary".

I propose to update PreProcessor to be able to deal with proper `Document` objects and review other nodes with `document: Dict` or `documents: List[Dict]` in their signatures.'

Title: b'Recent breaking changes & Migration guidance'
Body:
b'In preparation for Haystack 1.0, we conduct some major refactorings in the next weeks incl. several breaking changes. 

We will keep a list of breaking changes here to help you migrate your own Haystack scripts and applications.

## Refactoring of primitives (#1398)
We improved the basic datatypes. This might particularly break your code to 
- write `Documents` to the doc store
- process `Answers` from a pipeline / reader

### Document
- Renamed `Document.text` -> `Document.content`
- Removed `Document.question` (was only used a while ago in FAQ search cases)
- Rename `text_field` -> `content_field` in  ElasticsearchDocumentStore & Weaviate init
- Remove `faq_question_field` in  ElasticsearchDocumentStore & Weaviate init 

### Label
- Rename `Label.question` -> `Label.query` 
- Make `Label.answer` an `Answer` obj rather than plain str
- Remove `Label.document_id ` (can now be accessed via `Label.document.id`) 
- Rename `Label.model_id` -> `Label.pipeline_id`
- Remove `Label.offset_start_in_doc` (can now be accessed via label.answer.offsets_in_document[0].start`

### Answer
The reader returns now an `Answer` object rather than a dict. 
It follows this new structure:

Particularly the handling of offsets has changed to be more explicit and allow for other multiple spans (e.g. TableQA):

```
# Old -> New 

answer["offset_start_in_doc"] -> answer.offsets_in_document[0].start
answer["offset_end_in_doc"] -> answer.offsets_in_document[0].end

answer["offset_start"] -> answer.offset_in_context[0].start
answer["offset_end"] -> answer.offset_in_context[0].end
```
 

 '

Title: b'Better Error Messaging for Users when `docker-compose up` Fails'
Body:
b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I was running `docker-compose up` on a Macbook Pro. Docker Desktop was allotted 4GB of memory. The REST API would continually fail to load the `ElasticsearchDocumentStore` and hence also the `Retriever`. The Elasticsearch instance would keep starting, crashing and restarting. There was no error message as to why this was happening.

After some deep exploration with @tstadel , we found that this machine was able to start up the REST API and the Elasticsearch containers separately. But when started up together using `docker-compose up`, the Elasticsearch container would crash because of insufficient memory. Since the `restart: on-failure` is set in `docker-compose.yml` it would keep trying to restart.

After we changed the restart policy to:
```
deploy:
  restart_policy:
    condition: none
```
Error code 137 would be returned when ES crashed.

Calling `docker container inspect haystack_elasticsearch_1` after crash might show "State"/"OOMKilled": true

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be great to have some kind of error message displayed to the user about why `docker-compose up` is not working in this situation. It would also be good to explain that you might need to allot more memory to Docker to ensure the containers don't crash, and that you can also change the number of workers to reduce memory consumption.



'

Title: b'Basic python interface to interact with DC'
Body:
b"### What?
Seamless interaction with remote DC components from python code: Implement 
- DCDocumentStore
  - will be used locally and in DC jupyter Notebook
  - could also be used within DC (not focus)
  - DC currently only supports OpenSearchDocumentStore, but we should not restrict us here
  - DCDS communicates via HTTP with DC-Backend
  - data will be transfered on-the-fly
  - DC-Backend manages the actual DocumentStore under the hood 
  - DCDS will need some additional id/namespace to identify the DS under the hood: we take index + workspace
  - labels are handled by an equivalent API to documents identified by workspace and the document index
  - sample usage: `doc_store = DCDocumentStore(api_key=API_KEY, index='my_dc_namespace')`
- pipeline.load_from_dc()
  - loads a pipeline from dc
  - needs workspace and pipeline_name
- pipeline.save_to_dc()
  - saves a pipeline to dc
  - needs workspace and pipeline_name

### Why?
DC users want to interact with existing data in DC in local environments (e.g. notebooks) in order to experiment with it

### Identified challenges:
- query() is not part of BaseDocumentStore, but DCDocumentStore would need to implement it in order to support ElasticsearchRetrievers
- proper network patterns like streaming

### Possible Slices:
- Readonly DCDocumentStore
- Writable DCDocumentStore
- pipeline.load_from_dc() 
- pipeline.save_to_dc()

### Misc:
Methods of DCDocumentStore to be (remotely) implemented:
- write_documents -> PUT/POST /document
- get_all_documents -> GET /document
- get_all_documents_generator -> GET /document
- get_all_labels -> GET /label
- get_document_by_id -> GET /document/{id}
- get_document_count -> GET /document-count
- query_by_embedding -> POST /query-by-embedding
- get_label_count -> GET /label-count
- write_labels -> PUT/POST /label
- delete_all_documents -> GET /document + DELETE /document/{id}
- delete_documents -> DELETE /document/{id}
- delete_labels -> DELETE /label/{id}
- get_documents_by_id -> GET /document/{id}
- query -> POST /query"

Title: b'venuraja79'
Body:
b'Milvus supports the capability to tag the partition with a friendly name while inserting data. While querying this tag can be used to filter the search. Should we use this feature to implement "filters"? Please advise.

https://www.milvus.io/docs/v1.0.0/storage_concept.md
Quoting from this page - "A partition is identified by a tag. When inserting vector data, you can use the tag to specify which partition to insert the data into. When querying vector data, you can use the tag to specify the partition where the query should be executed. Milvus supports both the exact matching and regular expression matching for partition tags."

Currently index (default is 'document') in haystack is used as the collection name and we can allow the user to specify the tag names in the write_documents method (optional parameter) and the same can be used to query. This is just a high level design thought and will dig into this further if we are OK this approach.'

Title: b'lalitpagaria'
Body:
b'@tholor I asked Milvus slack channel about this and following response I got from them -

> The milvus v1.0.0/v0.10.x doesn't support filtered query. In current version, you have to increase top_k value then apply filter on top of it's returned results.
> We had v0.11.0 to support filtered query, but we found the old architecture is hard to meet the more and more requirements of users. So we declare the 0.11.0 to be "experimental" and decide remake milvus.
> Now we are developing a new milvus with new architecture: real-distributed, cloud-native, golang. The new milvus version will start from v2.0.0. The new milvus can allow user define multiple fields for collection, filed type can be vector/float/integer, user can use non-vector filed as "tag" for vector. The sdk api of new milvus is similar to the v1.0.0. The new milvus is code-ready, we are now testing it and fix critical issues, hopefully we can public its source code in recent days. By the way, the new milvus also has a stand-along edition for users.

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b"That's an interesting, creative idea @lalitpagaria . 

I think it could work if your filters were kinda static (e.g. always querying for filter `company=a` or `company=b`). However, if you have sometimes queries without any filter or a filter on another field (e.g. `year=2019`), I think it might affect the quality of your search results. With that I mean: the filtering might work but at the cost of less similar docs for your query.

I actually hoped the milvus team would implement it, but the release of their next version seems to take longer than expected. 
I could therefore see another hacky temporary solution: 
- Let's say you want top_k=10 and a certain filter
- Query milvus/faiss for top_k >> 10 (e.g. 100)
- Filter results in memory
- If results are less than 10, query faiss again with top_k >> 100
- Break in any case after a max of X secs to avoid crazy runtimes

Pros: 
- simple implementation
- works well if your filter criteria are addressing a rather big segment of your documents

Cons: 
- long, worst-case runtimes for filters that just target a few docs in a large dataset"

Title: b'Property id_hash_keys of documents never set'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
The attributes of objects of type `Document` always have `id_hash_keys = None`.

**Context**
Documents have a property called `id_hash_keys` which is used to generate the id. Before merging this [pr](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/1910) Haystack used strings to generate the id. Now we pass attributes on which the hash should be generated, i.e. `content`, `meta`, ...
If we create two documents with the same content and generate the ids from two different keys, we get different ids, but in both cases the "id_hash_keys" field is "None".

```py
from haystack import Document
doc = Document(content="some text", content_type="text", id_hash_keys=["key1"])
doc2 = Document(content="some text", content_type="text", id_hash_keys=["key2"])
```
The parameter `id_hash_keys` is passed to the init function but never set by `self.id_hash_keys = id_hash_keys`.

There are now two options: 
**Remove the parameter from the `Document` primitive.** 
Since this paramerter is already not set, it will not cause any errors as long as the creation of the id works as expected. However, we may need to discuss whether a document needs to store these values.

**Store the `id_hash_keys` by  `self.id_hash_keys = id_hash_keys`**
This will cause some tests to fail: 
1. Weaviate will complain, since the list of strings can not be parsed.
2. `Document.to_dict` will need some fixes

**General question:** 
How do we want to define document similarity in general? At the document store level, the id is used to determine whether a document is replaced on insert. Since this id is based on context, this is basically equivalent to comparing only the context. The `__eq__` function of documents additionally takes the metadata and other fields to compare the documents. So there is a possibility that `doc1==doc2` returns `False`, but when both documents are inserted into a document store, only the second document is inserted, which is passed to `write_documents`.
'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b"@bogdankostic @ArzelaAscoIi As of now we don't need `Document` to store `id_hash_keys` as an attribute. I can't come up with a potential use case that requires that. In the unlikely event that we need a `Document` to tell how its id was generated in future, we can add that functionality later. Until then, I'd say we remove `id_hash_keys` as an attribute of `Document` and just use `id_hash_keys` as a parameter to decide how to generate the id."

Title: b'Change return type of File Converters to `List[Document]`'
Body: b'Currently, the file converters are returning `List[Dict]`.  We should make use of our `Document` primitive here and return `List[Document]` instead.'

Title: b'tholor'

When working on this, we should take into account that we create the document's `id` at the moment when we instantiate the `Document`. If this now happens within different nodes, we probably need to add a param there to control the way how these ids are created (default: hash of `content`). For example, in DC we want to create the ID based on content + a pipeline_id. This can be done via `id_hash_keys` parameter in `Document.init()`.

Title: b'Normalize `component` and `node` usage across the codebase'
Body: b"In many places of the code, `component` and `node` are synonyms. We might want to normalize the usage by choosing only one of them (probably `node`, as it's used in the documentation too) and keeping it consistent across the codebase.\r\n\r\n"

Title: b'tstadel'
Body:
b'I think we wouldn't get around a distinction between those two: In the config we first create components and in the second step we define the pipeline by specifying nodes (component + inputs (connections to other components)) within the pipeline graph.
Additionally there are nodes that are not visible components to the user: The `RootNode` is an artificial component, the user should not need to specify. Thus the RootNode should not be considered as a component as such but definitely as a node.

What could and should be improved however are the `get_node` and `set_node` methods within `Pipeline`. `get_node` returns the node's component instead of all node infos (e.g. component + inputs). `set_node` replaces the component of the node. So prefixing both methods with "_component" would make more sense.

@ZanSara  are there other places in the codebase where this distinction is not clear?'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body: b"Good points! I'll note down other occurrences of name mismatches in the codebase. Maybe even worth documenting, even though I have no idea where this could be written down..."

Title: b'Topic based text generation pipeline'
Body:
b"Hello, 

I am currently dealing with a project about topic based text generation. I want to create a system in which the user can create texts based on two inputs: the keywords and the starting words of the text that will be generated. 

For example, let's say that the user specified the keywords as **'education, usa, university, boston'** and wants the text to start with **'The number of...'**. I want to create a system in which a list of documents that are about the keywords **(education, usa, university, boston)** will be retrieved with a retriever and texts that will start with **'The number of...'** are created with GPT2 based on these retrieved documents **_(e.g. The number of universities in the Boston area is higher than many of other cities in the USA. This might be seen as a good indication of the importance of the education in the area.)_** without fine-tuning the model every time the inputs change.

Normally, I could easily create this system by fine-tuning GPT2 based on the retrieved documents every time the user specified new inputs but as you might guess, this is a lot time consuming and is not an efficient way to do this. 

So, can I create this kind of system using the current capabilities of the Haystack ? Or do you know any other packages that can help me to create this kind of project ?

"

Title: b'mkkuemmel'
Body:
b"Hi @ozyurtf!

This is not a usecase I have worked on before, but these would be ideas off the top of my head:

The first step can be implemented via Haystack's `Retriever`. As your queries will be keywords (i.e. words that will reoccur in your retrieved documents), the `ElasticsearchRetriever` might do the trick for you! The query would be all keywords as one string (just as you put it above: 'education, usa, university, boston').
You can easily tweak the size of the corpus created by playing with the `top_k` param of your `Retriever`.

You can then add a summarizer to your pipeline that summarizes the documents you just retrieved. Make sure to set the param `generate_single_summary` to `True` to obtain a summary of all retrieved documents. Please check out the [docs](https://haystack.deepset.ai/components/summarizer) for more info about the summarizer.
I assume that using a summarizer here would cut down on training times for the model you want to use.

This summary can then, followed by your desired sentence beginning, be used as a base for your Generator. For infos about Haystack's current Generator possibilities, please check out [the Seq2Seq part](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/docs/_src/api/api/generator.md#seq2seqgenerator) of the documentation. So far, Haystack holds a [model input converter](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/a5501c72cf717396cd1b5238bddcc6ce00cba490/haystack/nodes/answer_generator/transformers.py#L463) for `yjernite/bart_eli5`, it is possible to write a custom converter for GPT2.

For more ideas you can also check out [LFQA](https://haystack.deepset.ai/tutorials/lfqa) and [RAG](https://haystack.deepset.ai/tutorials/retrieval-augmented-generation).

I hope this is helpful to you.


"

Title: b'Simplify YAML exportability of nodes'
Body:
b'**Problem**
Right now new nodes must always remember to call `self.set_config` with all their parameters explicitly copied over in order to be YAML exportable. 

**Solution**
For the YAML validation tests, I realized that a simple wrapper over `BaseComponent.__init__()` would do the job automatically for all `BaseComponent` subclasses, as long as they call `super().__init__()` (which they should to anyway). 

The only disadvantage is that all nodes would only take named parameters in input, which I believe is a minor inconvenience: nodes that work well with unnamed args are rare anyway.

I propose to get rid of the old `set_config` and use this wrapper method to make custom nodes implementation less error-prone.'

Title: b'Stricter Pipeline validation'
Body:
b"**Problem**
A discussion recently started on https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2214 about how to handle malformed and/or malicious pipelines. We realized pipelines do not do much validation on the configuration they're given: as long as a graph can be built, they are going to accept it.

**Solution**
This situation can be improved on several levels:
- [ ] Ensure that pipeline graphs are DAGs (https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2214#discussion_r812037550)
- [ ] Ensure that node names or other pipeline/node parameters do not contain malicious strings, as much as possible (https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/2214#discussion_r812002522)
- [ ] Raise warnings for detached nodes

**Alternatives**
- Pushing this responsibility to `Pipeline.to_code()` seems incorrect. Pipelines should be validated at creation time
- Pushing this responsibility to `Pipeline.validate_config()` seems incorrect. It has no access to the pipeline graph, because it's supposed to run right before the pipeline's creation. Only some of the validation can occur there (like validation against the JSON schema).
"

Title: b'YAML Pipeline Validation'
Body:
b"### Rationale

Pipelines can be defined as YAML files. However right now it's nearly impossible to understand if the supplied pipeline is actually valid and if not, and if not, what's the reason.

Providing validation can be extremely useful to users, especially less experienced ones, or users with very complex pipeline designs.

### Main Goals

 - [x] Investigate YAML schema possibilities
 - [ ] Define how strict the validation should be. For example, shall we allow for almost nonsensical pipelines, as long as the system could technically work with no exceptions? Shall warnings be thrown?
 - [ ] Validate pipeline syntax: verify from a YAML if it's valid (e.g. params, node classes ...)
 - [ ] Validate pipeline semantics: verify if combination of nodes makes sense (e.g. no retriever after reader)

"

Title: b'mkkuemmel'
Body:
b"Hi @arater,

 about your first question:

> But I wanted to get response or context part as whole sentence. Is there any configuration to get context in this way?

The way the context is being extracted works by character index - therefore possibly cutting into sentences/words.  
You can see the context creation [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/fd46a421301db03b6fc56f2fb72ba024ae5333ca/haystack/nodes/reader/transformers.py#L146).

What you could do to obtain full sentences: While initialising the `Reader`, you can set the `context_window_size` as a parameter (by default it's 70). If you set it higher, you can make sure that the whole sentence that contains your answer (and more) is part of the context. Then you can use a sentence tokenizer tool (e.g. by [nltk](https://www.nltk.org/api/nltk.tokenize.html)) to split the context into sentences.

For your second question I would need to understand better at which point you're using this dictionary / where this snippet is from."

Title: b'Pipeline.deploy_on_deepset_cloud() and Pipeline.undeploy_on_deepset_cloud()'
Body:
b'In order to enable smooth experimentation with pipelines, we want to enable the deployment and unemployment of pipelines so that indexed pipelines can be updated.

Save YAML to DC
Deploy pipeline to DC
API exists in DC
'

Title: b'tstadel'
Body:
b'We add two methods `deploy_on_deepset_cloud()` and `undeploy_on_deepset_cloud` to `BasePipeline`.
Handling would be:

```python
# a pipeline exists we like to deploy, otherwise we can save it to deepset cloud
# Pipeline.save_to_deepset_cloud(index_pipeline=index_pipeline, query_pipeline=query_pipeline, pipeline_config_name="my-pipeline-to-deploy")

# deploy pipeline
Pipeline.deploy_on_deepset_cloud(pipeline_config_name="pipeline-to-deploy")
```
Output:
`INFO: pipeline 'pipeline-to-deploy' successfully deployed.`

The we live happy with pipeline until we want to change it:

```python
# undeploy pipeline
Pipeline.undeploy_on_deepset_cloud(pipeline_config_name="pipeline-to-deploy")
```
Output: 
`INFO: pipeline 'pipeline-to-deploy' successfully undeployed.`

@PiffPaffM is that the intended behavior?'

Title: b'tstadel'
Body:
b"We should also add a hint to `save_to_deepset_cloud`'s case of an existing deployed pipeline.
Current error message: `Deployed pipeline configs are not allowed to be updated. Please undeploy pipeline config '{pipeline_config_name}' first.`

New error message: `Deployed pipeline configs are not allowed to be updated. Please undeploy pipeline config '{pipeline_config_name}' first. See Pipeline.undeploy_on_deepset_cloud().`"

Title: b'tstadel'
Body:
b'@PiffPaffM @ArzelaAscoIi  Just found that the api calls are non-blocking. So if the pipeline is in status "UNDEPLOYED" and we call deploy_on_deepset_cloud() we should ensure that it's in state "DEPLOYED" afterwards. So we have to poll the pipeline status for a while. Are my assumptions about the status flow correct?
`UNDEPLOYED`-> deploy() -> `DEPLOYEMENT_SCHEDULED` -> `DEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` -> `DEPLOYED` OR `UNDEPLOYED` if not successful
And same for undeploy_on_deepset_cloud(): flow?
`DEPLOYED`-> deploy() -> `UNDEPLOYEMENT_SCHEDULED` -> `UNDEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` -> `UNDEPLOYED` OR `DEPLOYED` if not successful?

What is the status `DEPLOYED_UNHEALTHY` in https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack-hub-api/blob/3a4ba1ef8679c8bd9c7f630007147df30b16b6b5/rest_api/controller/models.py#L45 about? Do we have to take care of this too here?
'

Title: b'ArzelaAscoIi'
Body: b'Both flows are correct :) \r\n`DEPLOYED_UNHEALTHY` is an additional state of a pipeline that is set when the pipeline has been successfully deployed but at runtime there is an error, there are scaling issues or the cluster is unavailable for some reason. '

Title: b'Replace node of type documentstore by DeepsetCloudDocumentstore on pipeline.save_to_deepset_cloud'
Body:
b'Since the `DeepsetCloudDocumentStore` currently requires that the namespace (= `pipeline.yaml["name"]`) exists before connecting to the Deepset Cloud, we cannot create a pipeline locally and transfer it to DC after running experiments/testing parameters/training. The current solution is to create a pipeline in DC and use a `DeepsetCloudDocumentStore` (read-only) that reuses the documents in that pipeline. 

To allow users to use Haystack and later move the final pipeline into DC (e.g. for production), we should allow calling `save_to_deepset_cloud` without having to overwrite an existing pipeline. 

**Proposed solution:**
On `pipeline.save_to_deepset_cloud`, we should replace existing nodes of type `document_store` by `DeepsetCloudDocumentStore` and print a warning that looks like: 

```
"Documentstore 'XY' is not allowed to be used in Deepset Cloud. 
This document store has been automatically replaced by DeepsetCloudDocumentStore.
This may affect the quality of the pipeline! For more information see: <link-to-pr>/<link-to-this-issue>"
```

This will enable users to upload any (or at least every supported type of pipeline in DC) to DC after optimization.



'

Title: b'tstadel'
Body:
b'@ArzelaAscoIi to get the details about this straight: We need to create a Pipeline (with DeepsetCloudDocumentStore) first in order to make it accessable via DeepsetCloudDocumentStore?

So todo:
- if pipeline does not exist yet check document store
- if document store is not `DeepsetCloudDocumentStore` exchange current document store in pipeline config with `DeepsetCloudDocumentStore`
- call `client.save_pipeline_config()`'

Title: b'ArzelaAscoIi'
Body:
b'Hi @tstadel ! 
Yes, we need a pipeline since the pipeline name defines the document store index :) 

Your ToDos are also correct, with one additional note. We always need to replace the document store with the deepset cloud documenstore if there is no pipeline, as using this document store locally will cause errors (index does not exist). Therefore, it is also necessary to use a different documenstore if you want to test your pipeline locally first. 

The only downside I see is that if you use e.g. `ElasticsearchDocumentStore` in your pipeline, push this pipeline to DC and load it again it will result in two different pipelines (one using Elasticsearch and one Opensearch). '

Title: b'mathislucka'
Body:
b'Hey @ozyurtf,

we recommend that you use a model which is already fine-tuned on a qa dataset because the results are usually much better. Still, you can also use a model which was never fine-tuned on QA.

However, if you could fine-tune on some other QA-data first or if there is an existing model (like the SQuAD models), then your results will likely be better. Why do you think continuing fine-tuning a SQuAD model is not suitable in your case?


As for the data transformation, we have a SQuAD utility class here: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/a59bca366174d9c692fa19750c24d65f47660ef7/haystack/utils/squad_data.py#L23

It's a bit tricky to convert a dataframe, but still possible.

```python
import pandas as pd
from haystack.utils import SquadData

sq = SquadData({'data': {}})


# This should be replaced by your actual dataframe. It needs to have the same columns.
df = pd.DataFrame([], columns=["title", "context", "question", "id", "answer_text", "answer_start", "is_impossible"])

squad_docs = sq.df_to_squad(df)

converted_squad = SquadData(squad_docs)

converted_squad.save('path/where/you/want/to/save')
```

Hope this helps!
'

Title: b'Fine tuning model on user feedbacks'
Body:
b"Hello, 

I have a question answering system in which the user can ask a question and give feedback about the answers with thumbs up/down buttons. But note that the user can only give feedbacks to the answers and not to documents specifically. 

I am planning to use these feedbacks for fine-tuning my current QA model and I don't want to include only positively rated answers. I want to include negatively rated answers in the fine-tuning process as well because I believe that using the incorrectly predicted data will improve the model performance more than the correctly predicted data.

My question is how can I use the negatively rated answers during the fine-tuning process. Is the only way is to follow the steps below ?

1) Asking the user to give feedback about the retrieved document as well as the answer.
2) Correcting the negatively rated answers manually (e.g. If the answer is incorrect and the document is correct, finding the right answer in that document. If both the answer and document is incorrect, finding the right document first and then finding the right answer in that document).
3) Using this corrected data along with the positively rated data during the fine-tuning process."

Title: b'mathislucka'
Body:
b"Hi @ozyurtf,

I think your intuition to use user feedback to improve your models is very good and it will allow you to continually improve the quality of your predictions.

Regarding your questions:
- I'd ask the users to give feedback both on the document and on the answer (like we do in our demo in evaluation mode https://haystack-demo.deepset.ai/)
- if you are using a dense retriever, you can directly use the documents that users marked as incorrect as `hard_negatives` during fine-tuning. This will probably improve your retriever model and thus also feed a better selection of candidate passages to the reader
- I am not aware of any way to directly use negatives for fine-tuning a qa-model (maybe @julian-risch has an idea?). If you are using a custom ui, you could maybe ask your users to also mark the correct answer if they give negative feedback.

Hope this helps!"

Title: b'ozyurtf'
Body:
b"Thank you @mathislucka. Yes that was helpful! 

As you said, we can currently be able to use the negatively rated answers in dense retriever.  And as you know we can also be able to specify if the answer and document is correct during the evaluation process with the parameters 'is_correct_document' and 'is_correct_answer'. 

I don't have in-depth knowledge about the backend process and that's why I don't know how logical question this will be but in the future, would it be possible to integrate these parameters to the fine-tuning process as well so that negatively rated answers could be used to improve the reader ? "

Title: b'mathislucka'
Body:
b"You're welcome @ozyurtf :)

Just to add some pointers:
- here is our tutorial on how to fine-tune the DPR model https://haystack.deepset.ai/tutorials/train-dpr
- the train methode also accepts a num_hard_negatives parameter https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/9974593c5eb0d682cbd9ddb48f0693594b667509/haystack/nodes/retriever/dense.py#L315

As for the integration of negative answers to train the reader:
- What you could try to do is that when a user marks a passage as both wrong answer and wrong document and you are training a model, which also has the no answer option (SQuaD 2.0 style) then you could add these passages with the no answer label to the training process. This might help the model to better distinguish between passages that contain an answer vs. those that do not. However, this doesn't help for the case where the answer is in the passage but the model predicted the wrong span."

I just read the last response you wrote and thank you for your suggestion. It was useful! 

There is one thing I didn't understand though. You wrote that I can add the passages with the no answer label if both question and context are rated negatively by the user. Title: b'Distilling new student models from scratch'
Body:
b'To be able to best utilize the new distillation feature for finetuning, it is necessary to have better pretrained distilled students.

For this, we still need to implement the following:
- [x] #2024 (open for better name suggestions): This processor should just read a text file line by line and tokenize this line without creating a label
- ~~Reintroduce `StreamingDataSilo`~~ (not even necessary as dataset should fit into memory)

The following teachers would seem promising/interesting
- [x] #2019: The published TinyBERT is based on BERT-Base. It would be interesting to see if using a better teacher would result in performance improvements. In case it does, we should consider using large models as teachers in later distillations
- [x] #2197
- [ ] Distilling DeBERTaV3: This model seems to be SOTA when just using a single language model and the usual sizes. For example, microsoft/deberta-v3-base is more than 5% points better in F1 than deepset/roberta-base-squad2 with about the same number of parameters. Without using distillation, microsoft/deberta-v3-small is already about on par with deepset/roberta-base-squad2 while being much smaller.
- [ ] Distilling GElectra: GElectra is the best available German language model and by distilling it, we would create the first small German language model with competitive performance.

All of these models are very similar in size and architecture so it should be possible to use the same configuration (number of attention heads: 12, number hidden layers: 6, hidden layer dimensions: 768, intermediate dimensions: 3072) as the original TinyBERT for all student models. The only exceptions is the case when we use a large model as the teacher. To align the number of attention heads, I would propose increasing them to 16 for the student. Because the hidden layer dimension of 768 is still divisible by 16, we would not need to change any other hyperparameter and the total number of parameters would stay the same.'

Title: b'Model compression: knowledge distillation'
Body:
b'Models and predictions are resource-hungry. We would like to save on inference time, memory space, and energy consumption by using model compression methods, mainly for the reader model.

More specifically, we would like to have a knowledge distillation method, where a large, parameter-heavy model (teacher) can be distilled into a smaller, less complex model (student). Knowledge distillation from output logits seems to be a good way forward. I imagine that a user has a large trained teacher model, e.g., https://huggingface.co/deepset/xlm-roberta-large-squad2
This model could make predictions and generate output logits on a given dataset, e.g., SQuAD 2.
Now the user could choose a model architecture for the student model from a small set of pre-defined options, e.g., a BiLSTM-based neural network consisting of multiple layers.
The next step would be to train the student to predict the same output logits as the large teacher model on the given dataset.
Finally, it would be nice to have a small comparison of the teacher and the student model in terms of inference time, number of parameters, and also classification performance (exact match accuracy, F1-score, semantic answer similarity, ...)

We considered other model compression methods, such as model pruning. However, we would prefer a model-agnostic method.

- [x] Implementation of model distillation: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/1758#pullrequestreview-816180081
- [x] Training and evaluating distilled models: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1812
- [x] Add a documentation page about distillation: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1814
- [x] https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1873
- [x] https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1874
- [x] https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1947
- [ ] https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/2021

**Additional context**

Title: b'Define supported data types for meta data fields'

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body:
b'I would suggest to support the following data types:

- `bool`
    - Elasticsearch: corresponds to `boolean`
    - Weaviate: corresponds to `boolean`
    - Milvus: corresponds to `BOOL`
- `float`
    - Elasticsearch: corresponds to `float`
    - Weaviate: corresponds to `number`
    - Milvus: corresponds to `FLOAT`
- `int`
    - Elasticsearch: corresponds to  `integer`
    - Weaviate: corresponds to `int`
    - Milvus: corresponds to `INT`
- `string`
    - Elasticsearch: correponds to `keyword` / `text`
    - Weaviate: correponds to `string` / `text`
    - Milvus: corresponds to `string`
- `date`
    - formatted as `yyyy-MM-dd`, `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` or `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ`
    - Elasticsearch: corresponds to `date`
    - Weaviate: corresponds to `date`
        - only supports date + time format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` 
        --> add 00:00:00 as time if no time is given
    - Milvus: does not support dates
        - We might build a workaround by indexing dates as `int` using UNIX epoch time'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'Hi @ilseva we didn't publish these files. For training your own seq2seq model you would need to create training, validation and test data yourself with data from your domain and with identifiers as in your own knowledge graph. Essentially the format of a training sample is the input sequence you give to the model (natural language question) and the output sequence that you would like to get from the model (SPARQL query).
So the input could be `What is the actor's name who portrays the main character in the Harry Potter movies?` and the expected output could be `"SELECT ?obj WHERE { wd:Q3244512 p:P2868 ?s . ?s ps:P2868 ?obj . ?s pq:P642 wd:Q8337 }"`in SPARQL format with identifiers from wiki data. 
However, we wanted to allow the model to come up with identifiers (e.g. [wd:Q8337](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q8337)) without needing to memorize them from the training data. To this end, we made identifiers encode the name of the entity. The model can then come up with identifiers no matter it has seen this exact identifier at training time (and as a downside no matter it exists in your knowledge graph or not).
Given input in with our identifiers could be: `In which house is Nicola Dodworth?` and expected output would `SELECT ?uri WHERE { <https://deepset.ai/harry_potter/Nicola_dodworth> <https://deepset.ai/harry_potter/house> ?uri }`. Each such pair of a natural language question and the corresponding SPARQL query with the identifiers from your knowledge graph form a training/validation/testing data sample.'

Body:
b'**Question**
Hello , and thanks for this great work,

I'm trying to fine tune the DPR model with mt own dataset, i'm using your tutorial "https://haystack.deepset.ai/docs/latest/tutorial9md" for that.

my dataset contain: 
INFO - haystack.modeling.data_handler.data_silo -  Examples in train: 135

however, when the teaining, i got this report:

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body: b"Hey @Elfilali-Taoufiq! It's true that the evaluation report might be a bit confusing. For training DPR models, we make use of in-batch negatives. This means that for each question, we don't only use the hard negative context as negative label but also all the other contexts that are inside the same batch (i.e. positive and hard-negative contexts of other questions). This makes training computationally more efficient.\r\n\r\nDuring training, the model is evaluated based on these in-batch negatives. That means that the evaluation values you see in the report describe how well the model detects the positive context among all the contexts inside a batch. If you change the batch_size, you will see that the number of hard_negatives will change."

Title: b'Elfilali-Taoufiq'
Body: b"Hi @bogdankostic, thanks for the reply, i'm still confusing a bit about the usefulness of evaluating the model using the trainig examples also."

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body:
b'The model is not evaluated on the training examples, but on the examples in the dev set. Compare this line
```
INFO - haystack.modeling.data_handler.data_silo - Examples in dev : 45
```
to the number of positive labels in the evaluation report. Both say 45 (you have 45 questions with 45 positive contexts in your dev set).'

Title: b'Elfilali-Taoufiq'
Body: b"Yes I see, but i'm talking about hard_negatives, \r\nin my dev set i have 45 examples with 45 negative contexts, however i see 1317 in the report !!"

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body:
b'We are using in-batch negatives also for the evaluation during training. I assume you are using a batch_size of 16. As you have 45 examples in your dev set, this would result ion two batches of size 16 and one batch of size 13. You get to 1317 like this:

- 2 * (16 [batch_size] * (1 [hard-negative] + (15 * 2) [in-batch negatives])) = 992
- 1 * (13 [batch_size] * (1 [hard-negative] + (12 * 2) [in-batch negatives])) = 325

992 + 325 = 1317

For each hard-negative, you get (batch_size - 1) * 2 in-batch negatives.'

Title: b'baregawi'
Body:
b'Hi @Krak91 , I just started using FARM but I'm familiar with its dependencies and have been reading the code. If someone can double check what my responses that would be nice. To try to answer your questions:

**"First question is, does farm tokenize text differently from transformers?"**

- The readers and retrievers delegate tokenization to huggingface's `transformers` package when you pass in the name of a public `transformers` model or a local path to a saved `transformers` model. Thus when you  pass a transformers model name or path to Farm you can expect it to tokenize the same as when you pass it to `transformers` .

- That being said Farm does have it's own `Inferencer` classes that can load different models. Those are based on Torch for `AdaptiveModel` and ONNX for `ONNXAdaptiveModel`. I didn't look into `Roberta` but `AdaptiveModel` is directly based on Torch rather than having the `transformers` intermediary.
Loading code is here if you're interested: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/modeling/infer.py#L175

**"Does farm expect different inputs?"**

- Assuming you mean "different inputs from `transformers`", the queries for readers and retrievers take text in text. The training process for `FarmReader` takes in QA datasets in SQuAD format. You can find a description and samples of SQuAD data here: https://rajpurkar.github.io/SQuAD-explorer/. The data is available in json format and is provided to `FarmReader` as file path. The `DocumentStore`s take in a `list` of `dict`s or a `list` of `haystack.schema.Document` objects.

**"Does it treat the inputs differently than transformers?"**

- I am not clear on this question. They both take in text for inference but the training data for huggingface transformer models is obviously different than that need for QA models. I can't speak for ONNX models.

**"Does the model exported in ONNX format expect the same inputs as the farm format?"**

- I know even less about ONNX than I do about Farm. But I know that `FarmReader` can use an ONNX formatted model as described above.

**"If not, does it expect the same inputs as the transformers format?"**

- If your concerns are about the `FarmReader` I would say the code looks like it is doing its best for you to not have to think about the model type. So just try it.

As for running this all on a Triton server, I don't see how that could work at the current moment since there is currently no way to get `FarmReader` to call a REST service to run a model without modifying haystack yourself.

I hope that helps!'

Title: b'Easier Usage of Haystack on Existing Databases'
Body:
b'Currently, it is not always possible to create a Haystack search system around an existing document database. The biggest challenge is that the documents might not yet be split into the right sized chunks for certain Nodes in the pipeline. 
e.g. 
- Document might not be 100 words long for DPR
- Documents might be very long, thus slowing down the Reader

Currently, the solution to working with existing databases would be to manually apply the preprocessing steps and recreate the database.

The proposal here is to have a class or DocumentStore method in Haystack which handles this
. I can imagine:
- The DocumentStore class (or some new class) connects to an existing database
- It can apply a PreProcessor to the existing documents
- Behind the scenes, it generates a new database / index that can be searched by Haystack and retains all metadata
- The newly generated database / index can replace the old one, or exist along side it

This idea is motivated by interaction with users of OpenSearch who were interested in either a plugin or an easy set of steps to apply QA to existing databases.'

Title: b'Rethink Document Stores'
Body:
b'The current implementation of Haystack's document stores seems to be unsuitable to account for the great differences that exist between every document store's implementations.

This can be observed in several places:
- Introducing custom parameters for one single document store is borderline impossible to do cleanly (#1861)
- The current implementation of `BaseDocumentStore` pushes on the actual implementation some abstractions that hardly make sense for some of them (like the concept of `index`)
- Testing is really, really hard, and what we have currently barely serves us: the issues are getting more and more frequent (https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Atopic%3Adocument_store)
- Tests are slow and repetitive.
- The current implementations are quite difficult to mock
- Adding your own Document Store implementation is really hard too

Thanks to #1861 I came to the conclusion that a better architecture for doc stores is possible and would solve basically all of the above. In addition, it could be made backwards compatible until Haystack 2.0 (or any later major version) is released.

The suggested architecture is the following (the code is entirely runnable):

### Classes

```python
from typing import List, Optional, Dict, Union
from abc import abstractmethod


# ----- base.py -----

class BaseDocStoreBackend:
    """
    BaseDocStoreBackend would be the superclass of most current document stores.

    BaseDocStoreBackend contains (almost) only abstract methods with the very minimum 
    amount of arguments that make sense for every document store's implementation.
    So for `get_documents`, those could be `ids` and `index`, but little more.
    For example, no custom doc store's params like `custom_headers` 
    (for doc stores that make network calls)
    """
    @abstractmethod
    def get_documents_by_id(self, ids: List[str], index: Optional[str] = None):
        raise NotImplementedError("BaseDocStoreBackend is an abstract class. Use one of its implementations.")


# ----- [implementations] -----

class ElasticsearchDocStoreBackend(BaseDocStoreBackend):
    """
    This is a reincarnation of ElasticsearchDocumentStore.
    """
    def get_documents_by_id(self, ids: List[str], index: Optional[str] = None, custom_headers: Dict[str, str] = None):
        """
        Example implementation that adds an extra argument to the base signature from BaseDocStoreBackend.
        This code is fine with mypy.
        """
        print(" --- Getting documents from Elasticsearch --- ")
        return []


class SQLDatabase:
    """
    This class is a reincarnation of SQLDocumentStore.
    Note that it has no base class anymore.
    """
    def __init__(self, url: str):
        self.url = url

    def query(self, query: str):
        print(" --- Querying the SQL Database  --- ")
        return []


class FAISSDocStoreBackend(BaseDocStoreBackend):

    def __init__(self, sql_url: str):
        """
        In the case of FAISS, which used to be a subclass of SQLDocumentStore,
        we can also use a similar "composite" approach by defining an SQLDatabase class.
        This makes it really easy to mock during tests (see below) and keeps FAISSDocStoreBackend
        identical to any other BaseDocStoreBackend subclass (no other superclasses involved).
        """
        self.sql = SQLDatabase(url=sql_url)

    def get_documents_by_id(self, ids: List[str], index: Optional[str] = None):
        print(" --- Getting documents from FAISS --- ")
        return self.sql.query("query")


# ----- document_store.py ----- 

BACKEND_NAMES = {
    "elasticsearch": ElasticsearchDocStoreBackend,
    "faiss": FAISSDocStoreBackend
}


class UnknownBackendError(Exception):
    pass


class DocumentStore:
    """
    This class exposes all the public API of the Document Stores,
    and owns a BaseDocStoreBackend subclass that does most of the work.

    The BaseDocStoreBackend subclass could be either named ("elasticsearch", 
    "faiss", etc...) or passed directly. This second way makes providing
    your own doc store implementation really straightforward.

    Given that the backends will be allowed to have different parameters
    (see below), a lot of methods will accept *args and **kwargs here.
    Proactive validation will be possible but not necessary: error
    messages are readable anyway.
    """
    def __init__(self, backend: Union[str, BaseDocStoreBackend], *args, **kwargs):

        self._backend: BaseDocStoreBackend

        if isinstance(backend, BaseDocStoreBackend):
            self._backend = backend

        elif isinstance(backend, str) and backend in BACKEND_NAMES.keys():
            self._backend = BACKEND_NAMES[backend](*args, **kwargs)

        else:
            raise UnknownBackendError(f"Unknown document store backend ({backend}). "
                                       "Please provide a `BaseDocStoreBackend` subclass, "
                                       "or set `backend` to one of the following values: "
                                       ", ".join(BACKEND_NAMES.keys()))

    def get_documents_by_id(self, *args, **kwargs):
        """
        Example of a simple "forwarded" call to the backend.
        In here, we can perform proactive validation by inspecting the
        signature of the present backend, but it's not strictly necessary
        as the error message will be readable.
        """
        return self._backend.get_documents_by_id(self, *args, **kwargs)



# ----- API from the user's perspective ----- 

def my_function(doc_store: DocumentStore):
    """
    As expected, this function will work if the DocumentStore is 
    using an ElasticsearchDocStoreBackend, and will fail if the
    backend is an FAISSDocStoreBackend.

    This code is also fine with mypy.
    """
    return doc_store.get_documents_by_id(["uuid2"], custom_headers={"custom":"header"})


my_function(DocumentStore(backend="elasticsearch"))

# Example of error message
#my_function(DocumentStore(backend="faiss"))

# Traceback (most recent call last):
#   File "/home/sara/work/haystack/example.py", line 210, in <module>
#     my_function(DocumentStore(backend="faiss"))
#   File "/home/sara/work/haystack/example.py", line 206, in my_function
#     return doc_store.get_documents_by_id(["uuid2"], custom_headers={"custom":"header"})
#   File "/home/sara/work/haystack/example.py", line 192, in get_documents_by_id
#     self._backend.get_documents_by_id(self, *args, **kwargs)
# TypeError: get_documents_by_id() got an unexpected keyword argument 'custom_headers'

```

### Testing & Mocking:

```python

# ----- test_document_store.py ----- 

import pytest

DOCUMENTS = [{"meta": {"name": "name_1"}, "content": "text_1"}]


class MockBackend(BaseDocStoreBackend):
    def get_documents_by_id(self, ids: List[str], index: Optional[str] = None, *args, **kwargs):
        return DOCUMENTS


@pytest.fixture
def document_store():
    yield DocumentStore(backend=MockBackend())  # Also an example of how "3rd party" doc store could be set up


def test_document_store(document_store):
    assert document_store.get_documents_by_id(["uuid2"]) == DOCUMENTS


# ----- test_faiss.py ----- 

import pytest

DOCUMENTS = [{"meta": {"name": "name_1"}, "content": "text_1"}]


class MockSQL(BaseDocStoreBackend):
    def query(self, query: str, *args, **kwargs):
        return DOCUMENTS


@pytest.fixture
def faiss():
    docstore = DocumentStore(backend="faiss")
    docstore.sql = MockSQL()
    yield docstore


def test_faiss(document_store):
    assert document_store.get_documents_by_id(["uuid2"]) == DOCUMENTS

```

### Make it backwards compatible

```python
class ElasticsearchDocumentStore(DocumentStore):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(self, backend="elasticsearch", *args, **kwargs)

    
class FAISSDocumentStore(DocumentStore):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(self, backend="faiss", *args, **kwargs)
```
These small classes are the full implementation. I expect them to be sufficient. Later, once we release a new major version, we can consider removing them, as they add no other value than backward-compatibility.

### Time estimate

I want to be optimistic and believe that this could take me a few days (i.e. 2 to 5) to put in place, once we agree on its final form. I won't tackle the tests simplification into the same PR. It can be done later in a separate one if the resulting arch is really backwards compatible (that is, if all existing tests pass on the new code without touching them).

--- 

I'm very open to better suggestion regarding the naming, and in general please highlight all the issues you see in this implementation, so we can iterate. I see it mostly as a cleanup operation: the functionality will be moved in the backends and not a lot of new code will need to be written.'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b'Another idea: during the dependencies refactoring (#1994), it became rather evident that not many users would ever want to have more than one or two document stores backends. For the time being, having different extras_require groups could be sufficient, but like in the case of Milvus1/2 and FAISS CPU/GPU, in some cases separate groups are not really sufficient.

An even cleaner solution would be to have each document store as a separate package. The base Haystack package could come with `InMemoryDocumentStore` as a fallback, while other doc stores will need to be installed separately. Note that we could still have a `pip install haystack[all_docstores]`, which will simply pull the document store packages ad dependencies.

An external package would have full control over its dependencies, so a single `haystack-milvus` package could have `1x` and `2x` as dependency groups as long as needed, and `haystack-faiss` could have `cpu` and `gpu`, without polluting the `extra_requires` of `haystack`. Separate packages will also mean separate test suites, which is a benefit in my opinion. Integration tests in Haystack, however, should still test against all doc stores that we officially support.

Another advantage of these external packages approach is that it will be easier to share the maintenance burden with external contributors, and allow third parties to easily extend/fork/develop their own document store implementations without having to wait for us.'

b'**Describe the bug**
While running some code using haystack I stumbled upon an issue where I always had a list of seemingly empty dicts when getting aggregated labels from a document store. Turns out the issue is just that __repr__ and __str__ are broken on MultiLabel because the data class is missing annotations.

**Expected behavior**
I'm not sure but I think for `asdict()` to work we need annotations like in the other data classes. So MultiLabel should probably look like this:

```python
@dataclass
class MultiLabel:

    query: str
    document_ids: List[str]
    gold_offsets_in_contexts: List[Dict]

    def __init__(self,
                 labels: List[Label],
                 drop_negative_labels=False,
                 drop_no_answers=False
                 ):
#...
```
