While those have some nicely formatted output such as `"<Answer ... >"`, `Label` and `MultiLabel` simply have their dict versions as representations. This could be confusing when the underlying data class shows different behaviour from an actual dict.

Title: b'Distilling BERT-Large'
Body:
b'As a next step to distilling better language models, we want to explore the difference between a distilling from a base model and a large model.

For this, we would need to decide on a dataset:
- English Wikipedia: We could probably use the version from SimplifiedTinyBERT: https://github.com/cxa-unique/Simplified-TinyBERT#resources Advantages: No conversion necessary; good comparability with original TinyBERT. Disadvantages: Short sequence length (at least when reading line by line; could not matter that much due to distillation; however no new line characters)
- The Pile: Advantages: Very high quality, does actually distinguish between documents and paragraphs. Disadvantages: Less comparability, format slightly more complicated -> Probably better to use in later experiments

We also need to consider changing the model architecture:
- BERT-Large has more attention heads so TinyBERT needs to have more attention heads as well.
- Perhaps we could reduce hidden dims to counteract an increase in parameters?

After that, we should be able to use the existing scripts. Due to being slower with BERT-Large, this should take (very rough estimate) about 5 to 6 days on 4 GPUs.
In case we use the English Wikipedia and do not reintroduce `StreamingDataSilo`, this code changes should be achievable in about one day.'

Title: b'Querying from multiple indexes in the same document store at the same time?'
Body:
b'As far as I know, one specify an index when dealing with the document_store object (for example, initialization, querying etc.).

The "index" field is a single string represents the name of the index.

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'Hi @shuaichengli0428 with the current features of Haystack it's not possible to use multiple indices within the same document store at the very same time, e.g., querying multiple indices at once. One reason for that is that Haystack supports different kinds of document stores (elasticsearch, faiss, weaviate, ...) and it would be practically impossible to support a consistent set of features across all the document stores when allowing to query multiple indices per document store at the same time. For some of the document stores, their settings, for example similarity metric, are strongly connected to how the documents are indexed.

If you would like to access data from multiple different indices that can still work by specifying different indices on-the-fly via the `index` parameter. You could the run the retrieve method multiple times, once for each index:
https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/983b20f28d89b869a3f1096425eaef1ad97552b3/haystack/nodes/retriever/sparse.py#L61
Setting the `index` on the fly in REST API calls should also work. You can set params when running a pipeline and thereby pass the `index` name to the retriever. It's described here under `pipeline.run`: https://haystack.deepset.ai/reference/pipelines#pipeline `params={"Retriever": {"index": "yourIndexName"}}`
params is part of a QueryRequest defined [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/2c184e467f590ba825a94098ee8c257d1638b532/rest_api/schema.py#L16) and processed [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/2c184e467f590ba825a94098ee8c257d1638b532/rest_api/controller/search.py#L74).
Does that answer your question? :)'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'Hi @jaehyeongAN the lines of code that check for duplicate documents can be found here: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/4b0ff830ca64a00e95019959ae7716b36b2175de/haystack/document_stores/base.py#L482 Two documents are duplicates if they have the same id. If you don't give IDs to your documents explicitly, they will get an auto-generated ID. In your case, you could add two different IDs to your documents to solve your issue in the following way:
```
{
    "id": "1",
    "text": 'this is iphone.', 
    "meta": {
        "company_code":'apple',
        "doc_category":'IT',
        "doc_title":'iphone13'
}
```

An alternative option is to influence the auto-generation of IDs in a way that it takes into account the meta field, which is what the `id_hash_keys` parameter is for. For that, you would define a document as:
```
Document(content='this is iphone.', meta={"company_code":'apple', "doc_category":'IT', "doc_title":'iphone13'}, 
id_hash_keys=["content", "meta"])
```
Please let me know if that solves your problem. :) '

Title: b'Recall metrics for answer returning nodes'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
For use-cases like named entity extraction (using QA) the currently supported metrics for answer returning nodes are not sufficient. Currently we assume that it is sufficient that one answer per MultiLabel matches (according to exact_match, f1 or sas). So we simply take the maximum of those metrics over all predictions.
In these use-cases however a recall metric would be needed (e.g. predictions must match all gold answers to get recall of 1.0).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
`EvaluationResult.calculate_metrics()` spits out a recall-oriented metric for answer-returning nodes analogous to `recall_multi_hit` for document-returning nodes.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
There is a workaround: Users can simply create one MultiLabel for each gold_answer, set a custom unique id to each MultiLabel and run `pipeline.eval()` in association with `EvaluationResult.calculate_metrics()`. However, no aggregation by query or additional filters (actual multilabe_ids) is taking place here. So the calculated metric would not match a recall score exactly but should be close to it provided the amount of answers per question does not differ significantly.

**Additional context**
This is not a classic QA use-case, but more named entity extraction using QA.
"

Title: b'Extend filter functionality for `ElasticsearchDocumentStore`'

Title: b'Using Tika Converter'
Body:
b'**Question**
How can I run haystack docker container with default file converter as tika?

**Additional context**
And also built in tika converter can convert and process ppt files? If no how can I add tika ppt converter to haystack? To process also from ppt files.

Title: b'MichelBartels'
Body:
b"Hi @arater!
To your first question: As the `TikaConverter` implemented in haystack supports all data formats compatible with Tika (you can find them [here](https://tika.apache.org/2.2.1/formats.html)), using it with a `.ppt` file shouldn't be a problem.

To your second question: To load a file using `TikaConverter`, you need to adjust the indexing pipeline which is defined in [`pipelines.yaml`](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/00dc30ae547bd4a55e035e51cd0bfe50f2e5b47d/rest_api/pipeline/pipelines.yaml#L39-L53). This file contains the following lines:
```
  - name: indexing
    type: Indexing
    nodes:
      - name: FileTypeClassifier
        inputs: [File]
      - name: TextFileConverter
        inputs: [FileTypeClassifier.output_1]
      - name: PDFFileConverter
        inputs: [FileTypeClassifier.output_2]
      - name: Preprocessor
        inputs: [PDFFileConverter, TextFileConverter]
      - name: Retriever
        inputs: [Preprocessor]
      - name: DocumentStore
        inputs: [Retriever]
```
To use `TikaConverter` instead just replace the snippet by the following:
```
  - name: indexing
    type: Indexing
    nodes:
      - name: TikaConverter
        inputs: [File]
      - name: Preprocessor
        inputs: [TikaConverter]
      - name: Retriever
        inputs: [Preprocessor]
      - name: DocumentStore
        inputs: [Retriever]
```
Additionally, you also need to start a Tika server. This can be done by running the following command: `docker run -d --name tika -p 9998:9998 apache/tika:1.24.1`. After that, you should be able to upload your files either using the demo interface or using the REST api."

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'Hi @SasikiranJ I think our pipelines tutorial will be helpful for you: https://colab.research.google.com/github/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/tutorials/Tutorial11_Pipelines.ipynb
There you can see that you can create a custom node for the classification you would like to do. You need to make some changes to the code in the tutorial though. Something along the following lines should work:
```
class CustomClassifier(BaseComponent):
    outgoing_edges = 2

    def run(self, query: str):
        if "?" in query:
            return {}, "output_2"
        else:
            return {}, "output_1"

# your pipeline:
p = Pipeline()
# start with your FAQ pipeline
p.add_node(component=retriever, name="Retriever", inputs=["Query"])
p.add_node(component=Docs2Answers(), name="Docs2Answers", inputs=["Retriever"])
# classify the output of the FAQ pipeline
p.add_node(component=CustomClassifier(), name="CustomClassifier", inputs=["Docs2Answers"])
# case 1: run in the ExtractiveQA pipeline
p.add_node(component=es_retriever, name="ESRetriever", inputs=["CustomClassifier.output_1"])
p.add_node(component=reader, name="QAReader", inputs=["ESRetriever"])
# case 2: nothing needs to be done
# join the results of case 1 and 2
p.add_node(component=JoinAnswers(join_mode="concatenate"), name="JoinResults", inputs=["QAReader", "CustomClassifier.output_2"])
```
The JoinAnswers node you would need to implement yourself similar to the JoinDocuments node here: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/07cf3c614a1bcb97531d233dd933d750c689a5d1/haystack/nodes/other/join_docs.py#L7
Further, you would need to implement the CustomClassifier node with your own logic that checks the query and the retrieved FAQ stored query.'

the default similarity function of ElasticsearchDocumentStore is `dot_product`. As the dot product can take any positive or negative value we scale it with [expit](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.special.expit.html) to a value between 0 and 1. Note, that this does not guarantee a perfect match to receive a value of 1 as the value depends on the magnitudes of the vectors itself and not only their angle. To achieve this, you can set the similarity function to `cosine` within ElasticsearchDocumentStore.

To correctly understand the second question: do you rather mean the conteXt of the answer?'

Title: b'timpal0l'
Body:
b'I see, but even if we use plain dot_product, the query = "What is a novel coronavirus?" and the content="What is a novel coronavirus?" does have the exact same embeddings, hence their dot_product would be 1.0 aswell. Do you have any clue why the dot product between the same texts get `0.6059359910992558`?

The second question was probably just me mixing up context and content...  

If you follow the FAQ tutorial and query with something that has an exact content, do you get 1.0?
'

Title: b'tstadel'
Body: b"To answer your first question, the raw dot product here produces a value of sum 40ish (I previously saw that during debugging). As mentioned before, this value coming from the dot product can be anything from -verybignumber to +verybignumber depending on the magnitudes of the vectors (they are not normalized before calculating the dot product). Afterwards we scale this value to something between 0 and 1 by dividing by 100 and applying the expit function. This scaling however has not the property to produce 1 if there is perfect match. It's merely a heuristic to not produce insanely big numbers."

Title: b'timpal0l'
Body: b'I see, but why use this option as default? I mean the number 0.6 isnt that intuitive for a perfect match. I think its a "better practice" to use cosine similarity normalized to the [0, 1] range for interpretation. If I query with a empty string I get 0.5 isch, as a number, meaning that there is a very small range where I would need to find a good threshhold for an application.'

Title: b'tstadel'
Body:
b'I totally get your point. In your case (finding a good threshold) interpretability of the score is the leading factor. However, (according to our docstrings) dot product simply performs better in some settings like Dense Passage Retrieval, where interpretability is not of special concern. Most of the time we just want to have some order. So we had to make a decision here on the API level.

At least in my opinion, it isn't too intuitive why these two metrics would produce a different order/ranking, this [article](https://towardsdatascience.com/similarity-metrics-in-nlp-acc0777e234c) shows a very illustrative example.

On the other hand, I see no reason to not set `similarity="cosine"` in the tutorial including a simple description what the cosine values mean. 
@timpal0l Would you like to make that contribution in a PR?'

Title: b'DPR embedding is not "invalidated" after calling DocumentStore.update_document_meta'
Body:
b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

DocumentStore has a method `update_document_meta` which allows you to update the `meta` on a document by id.

If the `embed_title` flag is set on the `DensePassageRetriever`, document `meta["name"]` is concatenated with `content` before computing the embedding.

When changing `meta["name"]` using `update_document_meta`, the embedding is not "invalidated" / removed / recomputed and thus doesn't reflect the concat of `meta["name"]` and `content` post-update.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Three options I can think of:
1. Always remove the embedding when calling `update_document_meta`.
2. Somehow detect whether `meta["name"]` will be changed after calling `update_document_meta`, and remove the embedding if that's the case.
3. A flag you can set when calling `update_document_meta` which removes the embedding on update (maybe something like `remove_embedding`). This seems less ideal, because the embedding can get out of sync if the end user does not take care to set the flag when changing `meta["name"]`.

In all cases, calling `DocumentStore.update_embeddings` at a later point would compute the missing embeddings.
'

Title: b'Handle unsupported Unicode Sequences in Indexing Pipelines'
Body:
b'## Describe the bug

Some databases do not support all available unique sequences. For instance, [Postgres does not support `\u0000` Unicode](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/31671634/handling-unicode-sequences-in-postgresql).

It creates problems when storing search results in a Postgres database.

## Error message
```python
sqlalchemy.exc.DataError: (psycopg2.errors.UntranslatableCharacter) unsupported Unicode escape sequence
LINE 1: ...d', 'ff309ab7-e52a-41a1-bde8-243g'::uuid, '{"answer"...
^
DETAIL: \u0000 cannot be converted to text.
```

## Expected behavior
We should provide a cleaning functionality to sanitize the documents extracted from a file.

## Proposed Solutions
1. we can add a parameter(`remove_unique_sequence` or `remove_substrings`) in the `Preprocessor` that takes a list of unique sequences to remove. The defaults can already include the most problematic ones.
1. we could make cleaning unicode sequences an attribute of the document stores. The argument being it may be easier to map problematic unique sequences to the document store implementation. 

cc: @dmigo 
'

Title: b'dmigo'
Body:
b"Just to illustrate. The first approach will look something like:

```yaml
  - name: Preprocessor
    type: PreProcessor
    params:
      clean_whitespace: true
      remove_substrings: ['\u0000', '<something>', '\u4321']
```

The second something like this:

```yaml
  - name: NewFAISSDocumentStore
    type: FAISSDocumentStore
    params:
      remove_substrings: ['\u0000', '<something>', '\u4321']
```"

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b'Ok so I got some more insights on this issue. First of all I wanted to make sure whether the documents triggering this error are really duplicates or not: apparently, they are.

The data we use in the tutorials comes from Wikipedia and similar sources, and the pre-processing function `convert_files_to_dicts` tends to split out paragraph titles as if they were sentences. In my test, this has been the cause of the duplicate documents error.

You can see it by inspecting the content of your `data.txt`. Look for example for the string `==External links==`: you are going to find at least 52 occurrences of documents that look like this `{"content": "\n==External links==", "meta": {"name": "511_After_the_Thrones.txt"}}` This are effectively duplicate documents from Haystack's perspective, so the warning is correct.

I hope this clarifies the issue. To avoid the warning, you should filter out documents with identical content. A more complex solution to keep these duplicates (assuming that at least the metadata is different) could be to create `Document` objects manually before passing the data to `write documents` and setting the `id_hash_keys` to them (see the docs: https://haystack.deepset.ai/reference/primitives#user-content-document). 

For example:
```python
import json
from haystack import Document
from haystack.document_stores import InMemoryDocumentStore

document_store = InMemoryDocumentStore()

with open('data.txt') as jsonfile:
    dicts = json.load(jsonfile)

docs = [Document(**content, id_hash_keys=["content", "meta"]) for content in dicts]

document_store.write_documents(docs, duplicate_documents='overwrite')
```
Running the above script I don't see any more duplicate id warning on the GoT dataset.

I hope this helps. let me know if you have further questions! :slightly_smiling_face: '

Title: b'ElasticSearchDocumentStore create_index param: Why is this useful?'
Body:
b'**Question**
While working with the ElasticSearchDocumentStore and trying out different analyzers, I realized that there is no way to re-create an existing elasticsearch index (which would be needed to update the mapping). I found the `create_index` param but when looking at the source code, I realized that it does not re-create an existing index and instead skips creation when the index already exists. ( see https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/c6f23dce8897ab00fcb15e272282d459dcfa564a/haystack/document_stores/elasticsearch.py#L172 and https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/c6f23dce8897ab00fcb15e272282d459dcfa564a/haystack/document_stores/elasticsearch.py#L252 ). I think this is fine in general, but what do we need the `create_index` parameter for. As it is, an existing index can never be overwritten so it does not matter if you pass `True` or `False` for the `create_index` param. Only in the case when there is no existing index and you pass `create_index=False` then there will probably be an error, so it actually would never make sense to pass `False`.

An option to re-create an existing index would be great though :) 


**FAQ Check**
- [ x] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?
'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body: b"Hello @mathislucka, I think your analysis is correct: I can't see what this need this parameter for either :sweat_smile: I would open a PR to either remove it or make it behave properly (that is, to re-create the index regardless whether it exists or not, and default it to `False` in the init function) and ask @tstadel for a review :slightly_smiling_face: "

Title: b'mathislucka'
Body: b"thanks for looking it it @ZanSara . In the spirit of backwards compatibility I think it could be dangerous to just change the behaviour of the parameter, especially if we will be deleting an existing elasticsearch index. People might have set this parameter to True and forgot about it and after the next haystack update, their indices start to get deleted.\r\n\r\nI'd propose adding a deprecation warning for the existing parameter so that we can remove it in some later version and the introduction of a new parameter like `delete_if_index_exists` or `recreate_index` (not sure about the naming yet), which we would set to `False` by default. This would mean that we wouldn't break any existing code but we'd give people a useful way to recreate indices if they want to. What do you think?"

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body: b"Sounds perfect to me! Right now we don't have a very clear procedure for deprecations, I assume we're gonna drop deprecated features at the next major release (which is not on the horizon yet), so take into consideration that the two params will have to live together for a while. Otherwise feel free to proceed :+1: \n"

Title: b'Print output_loading_info when loading models with Transformers AutoModel.'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When loading a model using Transformers AutoModel Haystack does not report any mismatches between the names of the keys expected in the model and the keys in the loaded file. As a result, if the loaded model has a prefix or keys incompatible with the instantiated model, there isn't any output suggesting that there might be an issue.

In Transformers such a situation generates a warning, showing that some are all of the parameters might be invalid. Yet in Haystack there isn't any such warning issued.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
`AutoModel.from_prerained` has a flag [output_loading_info](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/23ee06ed5551cf5d5701ed2e917c60b6dd584a88/src/transformers/modeling_utils.py#L1133). Turning it on returns a dictionary with mismatches between the expected and the actual keys in the model. Issuing a warning based on that data would be very helpful for debugging model-related bugs.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An alternative solution would be requiring a strict compliance between the loaded and the actual model. Instead of issuing a warning, an exception might be thrown.

**Additional context**
The request is a related to the `enelpol/czywiesz-context` and `enelpol/czywiesz-question` Polish selective question answering models I am developing. I have discovered the issue after several hours of debugging. If the warning was available, I except that it would help me a lot.
"

Title: b'Implement Phrase Retrieval based on DensePhrases'
Body:
b'**Phrase Retrieval**
@jhyuklee and I had a quick chat regarding the integration of phrase retrieval into haystack. More precisely, the idea is to include a retriever that can retrieve text on different levels of granularity, such as short phrases, sentences, paragraphs or full documents. This change in granularity becomes possible to a much larger index that works on a token basis. Figure 4 in [his paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2109.08133.pdf) shows how retrieval accuracy slowly drops when reducing the index size from 69GB to 23GB for a Wikipedia snapshot.

There is an [existing implementation](https://github.com/princeton-nlp/DensePhrases) called DensePhrases. However, it uses transformers version 2.9.0 and it would need to be migrated to haystacks transformers version, which is 4.7.0 as of now but will soon be >4.12.3 after a fix is released on transformers side for this issue https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/14277.

The functionality in the `search` method of DensePhrases is similar to the `retrieve` method of retrievers in haystack: https://github.com/princeton-nlp/DensePhrases/blob/main/densephrases/model.py#L55
https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/91cafb49bb45cca701e576e26f4fe0e80a01809a/haystack/nodes/retriever/sparse.py#L61
Therefore, I think the best way forward is to create a new retriever within haystack. As we have a [FAISSDocumentStore](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/91cafb49bb45cca701e576e26f4fe0e80a01809a/haystack/document_stores/faiss.py#L26) in haystack, that component can be used by the phrase retrieval implementation.

@Timoeller @tholor at one point in time FARM also went through this migration and its transformers dependency was upgraded from 2.x to 3.x and then to 4.x. Do you have any tips for Jinhyuk Lee? The [official migration guide](https://huggingface.co/transformers/migration.html) covers only the migration from 3.x to 4.x.

@jhyuklee When you start working on this issue (probably in the next two weeks), could you please create a draft pull request early on so that we can give feedback and discuss the code? Thank you! Very much looking forward to your contribution.

**Additional resources**
Learning Dense Representations of Phrases at Scale: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.12624.pdf
Phrase Retrieval Learns Passage Retrieval, Too: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2109.08133.pdf
https://github.com/princeton-nlp/DensePhrases
'

Title: b'jhyuklee'
Body:
b'Hi @julian-risch , I've been checking and using the Haystack code (it's awesome!), but it seems like implementing phrase retrieval here is nontrivial and would take a lot of time. I would love to get some feedback on this. Specifically I was checking the following possibilities:
* Create `PhraseRetriever` similar to `DensePassageRetriever` in [dense.py](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/nodes/retriever/dense.py) => this is the most basic step but it requires other modules such as `TriAdaptiveModel` or `TextSimilarityProcessor` to be adapted to phrase retrieval (note that DensePhrases uses two question encoders and one phrase encoder so it's different from the current implementation of `TriAdaptiveModel`).
* Create `MultiGranularitySearchPipeline` based on `DocumentSearchPipeline` in [standard_pipelines.py](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/pipelines/standard_pipelines.py) => given a single phrase retriever, we need to implement a new pipeline that supports `retrieval_unit` as an argument (e.g., phrase, sentence, or paragraph).

Ideally, the tutorial would look something like this:
```python
    (...)
    
    ### Document store
    document_store = FAISSDocumentStore(faiss_index_factory_str="OPQ96_768,IVF256,PQ96")
    
    (...)
    
    ### Retriever (currently phrase and query encoders are not separated in the HF model hub)
    retriever = PhraseRetriever(document_store=document_store,
                                      embedding_model="princeton-nlp/densephrases-multi-query-nq",                                      max_seq_len_query=64,
                                      max_seq_len_passage=256,
                                      batch_size=2,
                                      use_gpu=True,
                                      embed_title=True,
                                      use_fast_tokenizers=True
                                      )

    document_store.update_embeddings(retriever)

    ### Pipeline
    from haystack.pipelines import MultiGranularitySearchPipeline
    pipe = MultiGranularitySearchPipeline(retriever)

    ## Voil! Ask a question!
    prediction = pipe.run(
        query="Who is the father of Arya Stark?", params={"Retriever": {"top_k": 10, "retrieval_unit": "phrase"}}
    )
```


I don't think I can implement all these features alone due to my personal timeline. Do you think there's a better way of integrating phrase retrieval in Haystack? I've thought of installing `densephrases` package through pip and make use of it, but the classes in the original implementation are not very compatible with the classes in Haystack. Thanks!'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b"Hi @jhyuklee I like that plan and if we can make it work I think that's a better integration than installing and using `densephrases` package. Let's break that plan down into smaller work packages. For example, I'd be happy to implement the `MultiGranularitySearchPipeline` as I'm quite familiar with haystack's pipeline concept. ;) The tutorial itself is also something I can do in the end. Could you then implement `PhraseRetriever` similar to `DensePassageRetriever`? Is there anything we can help with? Happy to have another call if it helps. Just let me know."

Title: b'Improve dependency management'
Body:
b'The current handling of dependencies is quite monolithic: users must install them all regardless of the subset of features they want to use. We should make Haystack more modular at install time.

### Options

Nowadays there are several ways to properly handle dependency groups:
- several `requirement.txt` files: quite old fashioned by now and a bit harder to manage
- `extras_require` in `setup.py`: "traditional" way, safe and widely used
- `pyproject.toml`: the new way, as recommended by [PEP517](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0517/) and [PEP660](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0660/).

### Proposed dependency groups

- `minimal`: basic Haystack on CPU with one single document store (inMemory maybe)
- `gpu`: for running Haystack on GPU
- `rest`: install also the REST server API deps
- `ui`: install Streamlit deps
- `demo`: `rest` + `ui`
- `ci`: for GitHub runners
- `win`: for Windows installs (if possible)
- `colab`: to workaround Colab specific issues when necessary
- One group for each document store
- `all_doc_stores`: install all possible dependency from document stores
- `test` for the test dependencies
- `docs`: for building documentation
- `code`: black, linter and possible extra tools if/when we introduce them
- `all` (or `dev`): complete dependency list for development and contributing. Includes all of the above.

We can also consider adding smaller groups for special components with exotic dependencies, like `crawler`, `ocr`, etc.

### Default install

It's up to debate what the default install (`pip install haystack`) should look like.

The important point is that the dependencies that are installed in this case must be marked as mandatory. This at least is the case for `extras_require` in `setup.py`, and might have changed in `pyproject.toml`. If it's the case, the default install should be effectively a minimal install. For example, if we include GPU deps in this group, they will become mandatory, and having a pure CPU install will be impossible.

I will investigate the options and update this section with new information.

### Related issues

Related to #1291, #1716, #1826, #1806 

Closes #1070

### Next steps

- [x] Learn more about what's currently possible with `pyproject.toml` and whether all of our dependencies can actually work with it. As of last year that were still some issues with large libraries that needed complex build steps.
- [x] Finalize dependency groups list
- [x] Define what a default install should look like
- [x] Investigate how to properly handle failed imports for unmet dependencies
- [x] Fix dependency related issues (like #1806)

'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b'Unfortunately I don't think it is an option. This doesn't have to do with your idea (in principle it's not bad), but with the way pip and Python's dependency management works right now.

The issue here is that, currently, there is no way to specify "opt-out" dependencies in a `setup.py` or `setup.cfg` file. This implies that every optional dependency has to be explicitly opt-in, and I believe that asking every user to explicitly ask for `pytorch` and `transformers` alongside their Haystack install would be a bit awkward. We want `pip install farm-haystack` to come with sensible defaults; unfortunately, those sensible defaults have to also be part of the "mandatory" requirements, due to this fact. That's why, for example, Elasticsearch is also included in the mandatory dependencies, when it's clearly an optional: because that's what to our knowledge most people use, and would be odd to have to opt-in explicitly.

If by any chance you know a good way to implement opt-out dependencies, I'll be glad to learn about it! Unfortunately after a few days of research I came back empty-handed (see https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/pull/1503, https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/issues/1139). I even experimented with custom `extra` markers based on environment variables with no avail. But as soon as the feature is implemented in pip, your idea will become viable, so let us know if you find a way to handle this :slightly_smiling_face: 


'

Title: b'Make `top_k_join` overridable when calling `JoinDocuments.run`'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Retrievers allow you to set `top_k` on instantiation and override it when calling `retrieve` or `run` in a pipeline. `JoinDocuments` allows you to set `top_k_join` on instantiation but **does not** provide a way of overriding it when calling `run`.

Since retriever `top_k`s can be adjusted when running a pipeline, it make sense for `JoinDocuments` to offer the same functionality. Without this, there's no way of implementing a constant reduction ratio at the `JoinDocuments` node.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A parameter `top_k_join` on `JoinDocuments.run` that allows you override the instance `top_k_join`. You could then access this in a pipeline using `params` just like with retrievers.

Also would love to try implementing this and make a contribution to Haystack! Let me know what you think:)
"

Title: b'Different records with same text field is getting removed. '
Body:
b'**Question**
If the "text" field of 2 records are same but other fields are different. How can we index it ? 
**Additional context**
Currently when we use 2 or more records with same text field but different other fields, its getting dropped due to same hash value created by `Document`. 
The `Document` has a param called `id_hash_keys` is present, but how can we leverage it during write_documents. 
Eg : 

```
from haystack.document_store import ElasticsearchDocumentStore
document_store = ElasticsearchDocumentStore(host="localhost",index="document")
document_store.delete_all_documents(index="document")
documents = [
    {"text": "text1","tag" : "1"},
    {"text": "text1","tag" : "2"},
]


document_store.write_documents(documents, index="document")
print(len(document_store.get_all_documents()))
```
'

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body:
b'Hi @Threepointone4! In order to make use of the `id_hash_key` parameter, you can directly create `Document` objects and pass those to the `write_documents` method instead of dictionaries, for example:
```python
from haystack.document_store import ElasticsearchDocumentStore
from haystack import Document
document_store = ElasticsearchDocumentStore(host="localhost",index="document")
document_store.delete_all_documents(index="document")
documents = [
  Document(content="text1", meta={"tag": "1"}, id_hash_keys=[LIST_OF_HASH_KEYS]),
  Document(content="text1", meta={"tag": "2"}, id_hash_keys=[LIST_OF_HASH_KEYS]),
]

document_store.write_documents(documents, index="document")
```'

Title: b'Standardization of dependency management '
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Issue raised on stack [thread](https://haystack-community.slack.com/archives/C01J3TZM9HT/p1621267033292700) by Sam Joy. Currently there many optional dependencies are installed via setup.py. For example flask, fastapi, uvcorn etc packages installed by default even if doesn't want to use rest interface. There are few like tox, coverage etc are only applicable during test or build time. Hence proper dependency management is required.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
@tholor Proposed to use [`extras_require`](https://setuptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/userguide/dependency_management.html) in `setup.py` to properly manage dependencies.

By default `pip install haystack` will install minimal required dependencies to work Haystack on CPU. 
Proposing following `extras_require` options -
- `pip install haystack[minimal]`: It is similar to `pip install haystack` install minimal required dependencies
- `pip install haystack[rest]`: `pip install haystack[minimal]` plus fastapi, uvicorn, gunicorn etc rest interface related packages
- `pip install haystack[gpu]`: It will install minimal required dependencies to work Haystack on GPU (faiss_gpu and torch_gpu)
- `pip install haystack[crawer]`: It will add selenium and webdriver-manager
- `pip install haystack[ui]`: It will add streamlit
- `pip install haystack[all]`: It will install all essential and optional dependencies 
"

Title: b'Create distilled models based on TinyBERT'
Body:
b'With #1873 and #1874 we implemented loss functions and data augmentation for knowledge distillation based on the TinyBERT paper. This issue here is about training distilled models with that technique for question answering.

**Tasks:**
* Create two distilled models with augmented versions of GermanQuAD and SQuAD
* Compare their performance to our other distilled models and experiment with distillation parameter settings
* Publish the distilled models on the model hub and also store the augmented versions of the datasets in our S3
* Update the documentation with experiment results and also with advise on when to use which of the two distillation techniques that we now have: https://haystack.deepset.ai/guides/model-distillation'

Title: b'MichelBartels'
Body:
b'With the upload of [deepset/tinybert-6l-768d-squad2](https://huggingface.co/deepset/tinybert-6l-768d-squad2), the first step of this issue has been completed.
A rough estimate of the remaning steps:
1) Pretraining a German TinyBERT. To implement this, we have two options:
- Training using [original implementation](https://github.com/huawei-noah/Pretrained-Language-Model/tree/master/TinyBERT): Then we would only need to do some data preprocessing. Estimate: about one day
- Training using haystack implementation: It is the same as intermediate layer distillation so we would only need to implement data loading. An advantage of this would be that we could also use other models than BERT e.g. (G)Electra as teacher. Estimate: 2 to 3 days
Training time: about 3.5 days with 4 GPUs (very rough estimate)
2) Augmenting GermanQuAD
Here we can reuse existing script completely. Run time depends on multiplication factor, but not more than 3 hours.
3) Fine tuning German model
Depends again on multiplication factor of previous step and we can again reuse existing script. Should take about 4 days with 1 GPU.'

Title: b'Improve evaluation: Separate Answer Prediction from Calculation and Presentation of Eval Metrics'
Body:
b"**Problem**
Currently, evaluation prints aggregated results but does not allow to check eval results of individual questions or analyze eval results in detail. As a result, it's a complex task to understand which node in a pipeline is causing which of the wrong predictions. As a user, I would like to find out, for example, for how many questions the retriever or the reader node fails on my evaluation dataset and I would like to inspect these questions easily. Based on the challenges and ideas reported in: #1561

**Proposed Solution**
In addition to pipeline.run(), there should be a way to run pipeline.eval() that uses an annotated dataset to run the pipeline as usual and in addition generates scores with regard to different evaluation metrics on the level of individual questions. For every sample in the evaluation dataset (every question) we need to:
1. Generate output (predictions) of every node in the pipeline
2. Calculate eval metrics by comparing predicted output with expected output
3. Store eval metrics as a dataframe containing all intermediate evaluation info, such as predicted text answer, retrieved doc IDs, F1-score.

After that, in a separate step, we need to present eval metrics to the user by providing different views/aggregations of the dataframe, including limiting number of decimals in printed outputs. Optionally, we could generate simple charts, e.g., bar plots so that a user could easily compare multiple pipelines (parameter settings).

While the evaluation should work in the same way for all supported kinds of pipelines, the focus of this issue is on Retriever-Reader-QA-Pipelines.

Related smaller issues:

First phase:
- [x] https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1711
- [x] https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1718
- [x] https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1719
- [x] https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1739
- [x] https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1715
- [x] https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1717
- [x] Check whether all challenges reported in https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1561 have been addressed.

Second Phase:
- [x] https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1769
"

Title: b'Closed-domain/open-domain eval in pipeline.eval()'
Body:
b'`pipeline.eval()` on an extractive QA should support running the evaluation under the assumption that the retriever always returns the relevant document as top 1 result. In that case, the reader can be evaluated in closed-domain style.

In addition, the evaluation, more precisely, the calculation of evaluation metrics, should allow to switch between string-based and index-based evaluation of the reader. In a similar way the retriever can be evaluated either on whether it returns correct document ids or whether the returned documents contain the answer string. These options were also called closed-domain/open-domain in the past but we should name them differently to better explain when to use them.

Related larger issue: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1589

We broke this issue down again into two smaller issues: #1848 and #1849'

Title: b'tstadel'
Body:
b'With the above here are 3 requirements to support:
- string based / index based (spans) evaluation of reader -> we have string based implemented, no real need for index based
- string based / index based (document ids) evaluation of retriever -> already implemented with `doc_relevance_col`
- evaluate reader as if there was a perfect retriever sitting in front of it. There are multiple ways to achieve this
  - make `pipeline.eval()` support documents as input (currently query only). One would need to build a reader only pipeline and call eval() passing the documents from the labels -> So separate evaluation than with a real retriever
  - extend reader's `run` to receive labels and if in debug mode run second `predict` on label's documents providing the results as `"answers_perfect_retriever"`

Furthermore the old code is heavily scatter and parts of it are in `BaseDocumentStore` where they do not belong:
- `document_store.get_all_labels_aggreagted` has `open_domain` param to support the old index based retriever eval if `False`, which isn't really necessary here -> should be removed to reduce complexity
- `document_store.add_eval_data` has `open_domain` param to not set documents into labels if `True` which is awkward and never used throughout our codebase -> should be removed to reduce complexity'

Title: b'tstadel'
Body:
b'Results from sync with @julian-risch and @tholor 
- no index based eval for reader needed
- for `doc_relevance_col` we have to check if it's intuitive enough. For now it's fine
- "perfect retriever mode for reader":
   - first option is not what we want 
   - it should be as simple and intuitive as possible from caller view (best would be to set a flag in pipeline.eval)
   - two prediction runs in reader sounds promising (one with inputs from actual retriever, one with "perfect" inputs from labels)
   - how to handle two (or more) separate outputs/predictions per node?
      - introduce new column (e.g. "eval_mode") in dataframe
      - we prefer a common concept in eval_modes that can be reused throughout different nodes (e.g. "pipeline_input", "perfect_label_input")
      - metrics for non-default modes won't be calculated when simulated_top_k_retriever is set
      - naming of different eval_modes should be tailored to feedback from field engineering
- for refactoring of `open_domain` in document_store we have to ensure that use-cases from the book about working with haystack (especially about getting answers from different documents/products) still work'

Title: b'LorenzBuehmann'
Body:
b'Just to give you an idea how it works:

``` python
class MetaDocumentORM(ORMBase):
    __tablename__ = "meta_document"
    __table_args__ = (
                ForeignKeyConstraint(
                       ["document_id", "document_index"],
                       ["document.id", "document.index"],
                        ondelete="CASCADE", onupdate="CASCADE"
                   ),
    )

    name = Column(String(100), index=True)
    value = Column(String(1000), index=True)
    document_id = Column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
        index=True
    )
    document_index = Column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
        index=True
    )

    documents = relationship("DocumentORM", back_populates="meta")
```
As you can see i) because the primary key is a composite one (`id`, `index`) we ii) have to reference all those columns which iii) in fact means we also have to add another column for the index name then (here `document_index`) . Analogous for the `label` vs `meta_label` tables indeed'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body:
b"Hey @LorenzBuehmann, just a quick update on my progress on this one. It was easy to reproduce and, as you correctly pointed out, there is a composite PK being misused in SQLDocumentStore as a simple PK.

I discovered, to my surprise, that SQLite does not enforce FK contraints in general (https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/dialects/sqlite.html#foreign-key-support), but can support them, so I'm going to address this issue too and enforce FK checks, unless I see a noticeable performance drop. For the rest is matter to refactor a bit `SQLDocumentStore` to properly handle the composite PK of `DocumentORM` and `LabelORM`.

If you need an urgent fix, removing `primary_key=True` from `index` in both `DocumentORM` and `LabelORM` will make Haystack work on PostgreSQL, as long as you don't need to have the same document on two different indexes. Of course I'll notify you when a better fix is merged.  However I'm afraid it will take a few days of work from me, as I also want to enable our tests to run on different SQL databases to double-check that everything works smoothly on PostgreSQL."

Title: b'Store pipeline configuration (or reference to it) in eval result'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When we create an evaluation report based on an EvaluationResult, we currently don't have access anymore to the pipeline configuration, including for example the `top_k` parameter value that was used for the retriever or reader when the pipeline was executed. However, the report should list for each metric what `top_k` value was used.
What we have in evaluation reports:
```
                      Query
                        |
                      Retriever
                        |
                        | recall_single_hit:   0.5
                        | recall_single_hit_top_1:   0.5
                        |
                      Reader
                        |
                        | exact_match upper bound:   1.0
                        | exact_match:   0.5
                        | exact_match_top_1:   0.5
...
```

What we need: 
```
                      Query
                        |
                      Retriever
                        |
                        | recall_single_hit_top_10:   0.5
                        | recall_single_hit_top_1:   0.5
                        |
                      Reader
                        |
                        | exact_match_top_5 upper bound:   1.0
                        | exact_match_top_5:   0.5
                        | exact_match_top_1:   0.5
...
```

Note that the pipeline.yaml might not explicitly define the `top_k` values if we are using the default values of reader/retriever. In that case, we still need to show the used `top_k` in the evaluation report. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
When creating an evaluation report, we should be able to access all info about a pipeline's run configuration, including parameters where the default was used. I have two steps in mind: 1. generate a detailed version of a pipeline.yaml that includes all parameter settings with their default values if not specified otherwise. 2. make this configuration accessible in an EvaluationResult by storing it or a reference to it in the EvaluationResult.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The Dataframes of the EvaluationResult contain columns called `rank`. With the help of this column and the maximum value in it, we could infer the `top_k` used by each node in the pipeline. That would be a quite hacky solution and I'd prefer a cleaner way.
"

Title: b'Fix dot_product similarity calculation in InMemoryDocumentStore'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
The current implementation of query_by_embedding in memory.py:

```python
  if self.similarity == "dot_product":
      score = dot(query_emb, doc.embedding) / (
          norm(query_emb) * norm(doc.embedding)
      )
  elif self.similarity == "cosine":
      # cosine similarity score = 1 - cosine distance
      score = 1 - cosine(query_emb, doc.embedding)
```

**Expected behavior**
But dividing of dot product by magnitudes/norms is the exact formula for COSINE similarity. Should not it be just

```python
  if self.similarity == "dot_product":
      score = dot(query_emb, doc.embedding)
      )
  elif self.similarity == "cosine":
      # cosine similarity score = 1 - cosine distance
      score = 1 - cosine(query_emb, doc.embedding)
```


**FAQ Check**
- [ V] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?

**System:**
 - Haystack version (commit or version number): 
 1.0.0rc1
 - DocumentStore:
Memory
'

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body: b'Hey @fingoldo! You are right that this does not really make sense here. We divide by the norm in order to scale the score to a value between 0 and 1. However, this scaling should be applied *after* we sort the documents with regard to their dot_product similarity. In our backlog we have an issue (#672) to align the similarity functions across different document stores. We should tackle this problem that you mentioned here when we work on #672.'

Title: b'Align similarity functions across DocumentStores'
Body:
b'Each document store has its own implementation of the cosine and dot_product similarity functions. They seem to each differ somewhat in their behaviour and scaling methods are not consistent. We should make sure that each document store has the exact same behavior.

Tested using Tutorial 4 with the following questions:
```
"How is the virus spreading?"
"What is COVID?"
"What is Robotic Process Automation (RPA)?"
```
The probabilities that were obtained are as follows

ES - Cosine
99 - 64 - 68

ES DP
93 - 83 - 72

FAISS - DP
93 - 83 - 72

InMemory - Cosine
99 - 82 - 68

InMemory - DP
99 - 82 - 68'

Title: b'bogdankostic'

Title: b'Dependency license checker with CI step '
Body:
b'As the number of contributors is increasing better to add a CI step to avoid any dependency with non-compliant or conflicting licenses like StrongCopyLeft, GPLv3, etc.

- CI step only runs if the hash of requirements.txt, setup.py, or something related file changes (this may be used https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/.github/workflows/linux_ci.yml#L72)
- CI step should check all the dependencies of the newly added dependency (in case parent lib violating license or using dual license). Tools like [`pip-complie`](https://pypi.org/project/pip-tools/) or `pip freeze` can be used to uncover all the underlying dependencies)

Title: b'SQLAlchemy 2.0 migration changes'
Body:
b'Placeholder ticket to prepare haystack for SQLAlchemy 2.0 migration as it will have few major breaking changes.
Refer [link](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/changelog/migration_20.html) for more detail.

Brief information about migration by SQLAlchemy -

> SQLAlchemy 2.0 presents a major shift for a wide variety of key SQLAlchemy usage patterns in both the Core and ORM components. The goal of this release is to make a slight readjustment in some of the most fundamental assumptions of SQLAlchemy since its early beginnings, and to deliver a newly streamlined usage model that is hoped to be significantly more minimalist and consistent between the Core and ORM components, as well as more capable. The move of Python to be Python 3 only as well as the emergence of gradual typing systems for Python 3 are the initial inspirations for this shift, as is the changing nature of the Python community which now includes not just hardcore database programmers but a vast new community of data scientists and students of many different disciplines.
> 
> SQLAlchemy started with Python 2.3 which had no context managers, no function decorators, Unicode as a second class feature, and a variety of other shortcomings that would be unknown today. The biggest changes in SQLAlchemy 2.0 are targeting the residual assumptions left over from this early period in SQLAlchemys development as well as the leftover artifacts resulting from the incremental introduction of key API features such as Query and Declarative. It also hopes standardize some newer capabilities that have proven to be very effective.'

Title: b'Unify `vector_dim`/`embedding_dim` parameter in DocumentStores'
Body:
b'In `MilvusDocumentStore` and `FAISSDocumentStore` we are using the parameter `vector_dim` to determine the size of the vectors that will be stored in the DocumentStores, wheras in `ElasticsearchDocumentStore`, `InMemoryDocumentStore` and `WeaviateDocumentStore`, we call this parameter `embedding_dim`. 

I think, we should decide for either `vector_dim` or `embedding_dim` and make all DocumentStores use the same name for this parameter.
'

Title: b'tholor'
Body: b"Good point. Let's go for `embedding_dim` as we use this naming in other parts of haystack as well (e.g. `document.embedding` or `embedding_field`). I'd suggest we keep the old param for one release and add a deprecation warning to ease the transition of users.  "

Title: b'Align QA models with human feedback'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Haystack already has a feature to collect human feedback for the answers generated. This feedback can be used to improve the transformer based QA models by fine tuning them further.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The framework proposed in this paper (https://openai.com/blog/learning-to-summarize-with-human-feedback/) helps to align the model towards the human preferred answers.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None

**Additional context**
Hope this will be a great addition to haystack. If the team feels the same way, willing to spend more time to drill-through the solution further to fit this for haystack QA. Currently, this paper focuses on summarization."

Title: b'MichelBartels'
Body:
b"Hi @venuraja79.
What you are describing sounds really interesting! Although we suppose that it's less useful for extractive QA, there could be interesting use cases for generative QA and summarization.

Sadly, it isn't currently on our roadmap and at this point we would like to focus on other things. However, if you would like to take a closer look at this, we would be happy to discuss your ideas."

I think I have a rough idea about that but I haven't heard anything about Proximal Policy Optimization(PPO) so that would be new to me. Overall it seems like a complex topic but after your having seen your various great contributions to haystack I am confident you would be up to it.  "

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b"Hi @nisrj10 let me list the steps that I followed to get haystack running on Mac M1 aka Apple Silicon in more detail:
1. Install brew and miniforge [simple steps are described in this tutorial](https://towardsdatascience.com/yes-you-can-run-pytorch-natively-on-m1-macbooks-and-heres-how-35d2eaa07a83)
2. Create a virtual environment. I decided to go with python3.9: `conda create --name py39 python=3.9` and activate it afterward: `conda activate py39`
3. Clone FARM repository and install FARM and its dependencies. (FARM itself is a dependency of haystack.)
   - `git clone https://github.com/deepset-ai/FARM.git`
   - `cd FARM`
   - `conda install pytorch scikit-learn`
   - `conda install -c conda-forge sentencepiece`
   -  `pip install -r requirements.txt`
   - `pip install -e .`
4. Optionally, you can try to run `python examples/doc_classification.py` now or any other example. If it shows some nice ASCII art, you're all good.
5. Clone haystack repository and install some haystack dependencies:
   - `cd ..`
   - `git clone https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack.git`
   - `cd haystack`
   - `conda install -c conda-forge psycopg2-binary`
   - `conda install -c conda-forge uvloop`
7. Edit `requirements.txt` to remove (comment out) dependencies that I could not get installed (so far) or that are already installed:
   - `#farm==0.8.0`
   - `#--find-links=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html`
   - `#psycopg2-binary; sys_platform != 'win32' and sys_platform != 'cygwin'`

Title: b'UserWarning in Tutorial2 finetuning notebook'

b'**Describe the bug**
This is not really a bug but there is a UserWarning when training the model because a list is directly converted to a tensor:
`haystack/modeling/data_handler/dataset.py:65: UserWarning: Creating a tensor from a list of numpy.ndarrays is extremely slow. Please consider converting the list to a single numpy.ndarray with numpy.array() before converting to a tensor. (Triggered internally at  ../torch/csrc/utils/tensor_new.cpp:201.)`

This does not look so nice and it's also easily fixed.

**Error message**
`haystack/modeling/data_handler/dataset.py:65: UserWarning: Creating a tensor from a list of numpy.ndarrays is extremely slow. Please consider converting the list to a single numpy.ndarray with numpy.array() before converting to a tensor. (Triggered internally at  ../torch/csrc/utils/tensor_new.cpp:201.)`

**Expected behavior**
The list could be converted to an np.array first. I don't know if it really has any performance benefits in this case but it will at least avoid the UserWarning. I was actually interested in the performance difference and made a little script to compare the two approaches:

```python
import torch
import numpy as np
import timeit

def compare_speed(runs, conversion=False):
    lst = range(1000000)
    if conversion:
        lst = np.array(lst)

    times = []
    for run in range(runs):
        t0 = timeit.default_timer()
        tense = torch.tensor(lst, dtype=torch.long)
        t1 = timeit.default_timer()
        times.append(t1-t0)
    
    print(f'Executed {runs} runs converting {"np.array" if conversion else "list"} to tensor. Took {sum(times)/runs} ms on average.')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    compare_speed(1000)
    compare_speed(1000, True)
```

This results in:
```
Executed 1000 runs converting list to tensor. Took 0.022728791695000018 ms on average.
Executed 1000 runs converting np.array to tensor. Took 0.00040228743899997 ms on average.
```
Which is still quite a difference.

My understanding is that 
https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/3e0ef1cc8a6e6cef44056fd18f4e94089fc90311/haystack/modeling/data_handler/dataset.py#L65
Could simply be changed to:
```python

```

From the PR it looks like this is in a different place though.\r\n\r\nI just realized that my test script isn't entirely accurate though and the warning actually indicates that it's a list of numpy arrays whereas I assumed a list of ints, I'll make some quick changes to see if it fixes it."

Title: b'mathislucka'
Body:
b'Ok, I've updated the script and it should now reflect the data structures used in this place:

```python
import torch
import numpy as np
import timeit

def compare_speed(runs, conversion=False, share_memory=False):
    lst = [np.array(range(20)) for _ in range(10000)]

    times = []
    for run in range(runs):
        t0 = timeit.default_timer()
        if conversion and share_memory:
            tense = torch.as_tensor(np.array(lst), dtype=torch.long)
        elif conversion and not share_memory:
            tense = torch.tensor(np.array(lst), dtype=torch.long)
        else:
            tense = torch.tensor(lst, dtype=torch.long)
        t1 = timeit.default_timer()
        times.append(t1-t0)
    
    print(f'Executed {runs} runs converting {"np.array" if conversion else "list"} to tensor using {"torch.as_tensor" if share_memory else "torch.tensor"}. Took {sum(times)/runs} ms on average.')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    compare_speed(1000)
    compare_speed(1000, True)
    compare_speed(1000, True, True)

```

This yields:
```
Executed 1000 runs converting list to tensor using torch.tensor. Took 0.009287434434999993 ms on average.
Executed 1000 runs converting np.array to tensor using torch.tensor. Took 0.0014557391410000395 ms on average.
Executed 1000 runs converting np.array to tensor using torch.as_tensor. Took 0.001208238316999971 ms on average.
```
The UserWarning disappears and as using `torch.as_tensor` brings some performance improvements over `torch.tensor` as the memory between the np.array and the tensor is shared (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.as_tensor.html).

I think it would be save to change this line accordingly. What do you think?'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b"I agree that we should do that change, yes. Getting rid of the warning is nice so that users are not confused. The actual speed improvement doesn't seem big though. Thanks for bringing it up and testing the performance!  If you create a PR I'd be happy to review it."

Title: b'mathislucka'
Body: b"Alright, thanks. I'll create a PR. For the performance I wouldn't be so sure. I didn't backtrack the code entirely so I'm not very sure, but if there is a lot of training samples this could still save some time because this code would run many times and there's roughly a 7x speed-up when changing it. Might accumulate to something meaningful."

Title: b'speed up slow retriever evaluation'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Recently, I played around with haystack and its evaluation features. I followed along your blog post https://www.deepset.ai/blog/how-to-evaluate-a-question-answering-system and I played around with different scenarios for evaluation. I then realized, that the evaluation method is quite slow and for me, it also had issues with colab notebooks because tqdm progress bars were printed for each query. Another thing that I didn't like was that you can only measure recall at one k at a time. If you want to have a chart of recall @ different k's you will have to run the evaluation multiple times.

To quantify it a bit more:

Evaluating a sentence transformer model on the german dpr test set took about 8 minutes on a P100-GPU whereas the evaluation of the same model in the sentence-transformers library took about 20 seconds. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I know that there is much more overhead when compared to a library like sentence transformers because haystack has to use a real retrieval pipeline including a document store like elasticsearch. What I would like is that the eval method in the retriever (at least for dense retrievers) https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/3539e6b041668df2673b668b042fd7e005d7a7ad/haystack/retriever/base.py#L49 makes a call to a `bulk_retrieve` or `batch_retrieve` method on the retriever. This bulk retrieval method could at least embed all the queries at once instead of embedding the queries one by one. Ideally, the document store would also be queried in batches although I realize that this might mean too much complexity when accounting for different document stores. Still, embedding all queries at once (or batches of queries to avoid OOM errors) will still make the evaluation much faster.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None

**Additional context**
This is just a feature that I think would be nice to have. It's not really urgent or anything like that."

We already added batch indexing in https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/1231 and have an open issue for batch querying in https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1239 
Feel free to discuss the design we laid out in that issue.

Btw do you have other feedback regarding the evaluation? E.g. is it clear what closed domain vs open domain means and how it is implemented? I am asking since we realized the evaluation is rather complex and we want to simplify it. Getting your feedback there would help.'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @monika1800, 

Such an expiration schedule is currently not supported in Haystack. We are open for community contributions here, but I am wondering what equivalent you have in mind on the plain elasticsearch side. There was something like `_ttl` in earlier versions but it seems deprecated and replaced by something else (https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/mapping-ttl-field.html).

As for now, maybe this workflow would work as well: at indexing time you provide a meta field `expires_at="2020-07-20"` or `created_at=2020-07-06`. You could then run daily jobs to delete all documents that have certain tags `document_store.delete_documents(filters={"expires_at":"2020-07-20"})`. While the filtering here currently only supports strings, we will soon extend this to dateranges (e.g. >= 2020-07-20)
'

Title: b'monika1800'

Body: b'This will be possible when we extend the capabilities of `filters` in haystack. We could either have custom headers as optional instance variable when initializing an `ElasticsearchDocumentStore` or have an optional argument in the query methods and then pass these header (either from instance variable or argument) to elasticsearch's [`search`](https://elasticsearch-py.readthedocs.io/en/v7.15.2/api.html#elasticsearch.Elasticsearch.search) method.\r\n\r\n@tholor What do you think about this?"

Title: b'tholor'

b'> We could either have custom headers as optional instance variable when initializing an ElasticsearchDocumentStore or have an optional argument in the query methods and then pass these header (either from instance variable or argument) to elasticsearch's search method.

If I understood you correct @DJokes , you want to change the auth params dynamically for every request? In that case, passing custom headers when initializing the `ElasticsearchDocumentStore` wouldn't be an option and I'd see two options: 
a) passing it as an optional `token` param to `Retriever.run()` and from there down to the doc store's query methods
b) adjusting the state of the doc store from a higher level on a request base  (e.g. when a request hits the REST API with auth infos different to the current ones, we can re-configure the `ElasticsearchDocumentStore.client`) => this seems quite ugly when we expect the auth to change quite often between requests 

@DJokes How does your current auth with JWT work? Where do you set the HTTP header in the elasticsearch client? If you have a small code example of how you envision the elasticsearch request, we can work us back "upstream" to discuss how we pass it there nicely from the pipeline.

Title: b'Dev split in preprocessing not working when not using multiprocessing'

b'**Describe the bug**
When disabling multiprocessing, preprocessing is done in one huge chunk:
https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/8082549663f741d966791625ed7b78f0e2113c3b/haystack/modeling/data_handler/data_silo.py#L156

https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/8082549663f741d966791625ed7b78f0e2113c3b/haystack/modeling/data_handler/data_silo.py#L384-L408

https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/8082549663f741d966791625ed7b78f0e2113c3b/haystack/modeling/data_handler/data_silo.py#L156
to:
```
results = map(partial(self._dataset_from_chunk, processor=self.processor), grouper(dicts, 1))  # type: ignore
```
This would mean that there would be a chunk for each sample so dev split would be possible again. But perhaps it would be better to overthink random_split_ConcatDataset because it also causes other problems (#96).

logging.warn(f"print_answers received details='{details}', which was not understood. "

valid_values = ", ".join(fields_to_keep_by_level.keys()) + " and 'all'."

Title: b'Add synonyms to elasticsearch'

Body:

Title: b'ierezell'
Body:
b'Hi @tholor, 

### Creating the index
As I understood ([from the ES docs](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/analysis-synonym-tokenfilter.html)) you can give either an array or a path to a formated file. 

[This french blog post](https://www.elastic.co/fr/blog/boosting-the-power-of-elasticsearch-with-synonyms)(the code snippets should explain it, sorry it's in french)

With `"updateable": True` if we modify the file, the index will update and new queries will be computed with the latest synonyms file. However I don't know for the array (as you cannot really modify it ?)

Thus I would add a `synonym` parameter when creating the index were you can give either a file or an array (or maybe only a file path). 

Then I just copy pasted the analyser from ES and replaced the synonym field to include my file. 

### Query time
At query time, ES do everything for us for the synonyms.

You can also add the code from the dropdown I gave to include positive and negative boost words. Which can be given as arrays of string at query time.  


Hope it's more clear, don't hesitate to ask if it's not ! 
'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @lerezell, 

In general, I see the tradeoff between
a) Creating an index outside of Haystack (more work, but very powerful since you can use all available Elasticsearch configs)
b) Creating an index automatically from Haystack (convenient, but only most command useful configs)

Even today you can create an index with a synonym file outside of Haystack. Not a problem, but it might require some deeper elastic understanding and inconvenient "extra steps".

So let's talk about b). What parts of configuring synonyms make sense to do from within Haystack? 
- passing a list of synonyms => yes, that's easy to understand and very helpful
- passing a filepath => maybe, but the user would need to make sure that this file is available in the config directory of the elasticsearch node. I haven't seen a way to "upload" that file easily via elastic's API.
- the other custom parts of your analyzer / filter (french ellision etc.) => not directly synonym-related. I would probably descope it from this issue and a potential pull request   
 
What do you think? '

Title: b'ierezell'
Body:
b'I agree that for complex use cases creating the index "on the side" is really relevant (and the best tradeoff). 

For b) : 
    - List of synonyms yes it's simple but not modifiable. It's the best tradeoff between complexity/works out of the box. 
    - File path, you're right, it need to be written in the elasticsearch config folder... I used a function to copy it from my work directory to the elasticsearch one to have a bit more abstraction. It's more complex but allow a much nicer experience. If by giving a path to a random file we copy it before creating the index it can be a nice UX solution.   

For the other parts of the analyser, it's just the same as the french ES one, I just copy pasted it to add synonyms but I guess there is other ways to do it (and it's indeed not relevant to the synonyms request).   

Thanks for taking in consideration the request and taking time for it. 
Have a great day'

Title: b'Fine-tune search retriever on custom dataset using MLM'
Body:
b"**Question**
I want to use Haystack for searching documents, i.e. as a search engine, not necessarily to answer questions. I was thinking of using the retriever only with EmbeddingRetriever. Hence, when the query and the document are close, it returns some results. 

However, I don't have labelled data, I have only a huge text corpus of a **specific domain**. As I understood from Haystack documentation, I should fine-tune the retriever model on my own dataset and use it as an embedding_model

Am I doing the right thing? What is the best way to fine-tune LM? can I fine-tune Bert for MLM for example? 

```
emb_retriever = EmbeddingRetriever(
    document_store_es,
    embedding_model='distilroberta-base-msmarco-v2',
    model_format='sentence_transformers',
    use_gpu=True,

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'Hi @Omarnabk you are right that a retriever is the best choice for your document search scenario. In haystack, we encapsulate that in a DocumentSearchPipeline, which is also part of our tutorial on pipelines: https://colab.research.google.com/github/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/tutorials/Tutorial11_Pipelines.ipynb

You can find a list of models that could be used in an EmbeddingRetriever in this table: https://www.sbert.net/docs/pretrained_models.html I would suggest that you try out some of these models for example "sentence-transformers/multi-qa-mpnet-base-dot-v1" and "sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2" in comparison to "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2". 
Unfortunately, domain adaptation of these models is not so easy (yet). There are pre-trained on more than just a MLM task. Instead these models were trained on pairs of semantically similar questions and paragraphs. For example, "sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2" has been trained on a dataset of 1 billion sentence pairs. If you are aiming to finetune a model to your domain the model card you can find detailed info in the model cards of these model but that would require a large dataset of such semantically similar sentence pairs and a lot of computational power. 
May I ask what domain you are interested in? Is it medical domain, financial domain, etc.? Maybe there is a public dataset available that contains sentence pairs.
You are right that finetuning a language model to you domain would be a good first step towards a domain-specific retrieval model. However, I think that the lack of a dataset of sentence pairs from your domain limits any gains in search performance improvements.

If you would like to further improve your search results, you might want to consider a cross-encoder-based document reranking step after the retrieval of the top most relevant documents. It's explained here: https://haystack.deepset.ai/docs/latest/rankermd 
'

Title: b'Weight the title and the URL of a website for better ranking'
Body:
b"**Question**
I'm using Haystack to search a huge amount of documents (long docs) ~2.5M. However, the most searchable term exists if most of the documents but not frequently on their titles and URLs

I want the engine to focus on the document title and its URL before addressing the content. Can I weight the title and the ULR and to give them a higher semantic similarity score? 

I'm using EmbeddingRetriever for the task with Elastic datastore"

Title: b'brandenchan'
Body:
b"Hi @omarnabk, I can think of a way to achieve this using a custom pipeline design. 

The idea is that you index the Title+URL separately from the document content. You can do this either by having 2 separate document stores or by storing them in two different indexes of the one document store. You would then generate embeddings for each.

Your pipeline should look something like [this](https://haystack.deepset.ai/components/pipelines#example-multiple-retrievers) except with a few significant differences
- Instead of the ES and DPR Retrievers, you have two instances of sentence retriever
- Each sentence retriever performs retrieval on either Title+URL or document content

You will then want to modify JoinResults so that it weights the scores of each branch.

I hope this helps! Let me know if you'd like more pointers on any part of this implementation"

Title: b'julian-risch'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @anirbansaha96 , 

Yes, there is a PDF converter within haystack that you can use:
```
from haystack.indexing.file_converters.pdf import PDFToTextConverter

converter = PDFToTextConverter(remove_header_footer=True, remove_numeric_tables=True, valid_languages=["de","en"])
pages = converter.extract_pages(file_path=file)
```
It comes with some basic cleaning functions as well. 
(see also https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/README.rst#7-indexing-pdf-files) 

You could use the converter in the indexing part of your pipeline like this: 

```
converter = PDFToTextConverter(remove_header_footer=True, remove_numeric_tables=True)
document_store = ElasticsearchDocumentStore()

dicts = []
for file in Path("<PATH-TO_DIR-WITH-PDFs>").iterdir():
    pages = converter.extract_pages(file_path=file)
    text = "\n".join(pages)
    # optional: do more cleaning here or index single pages instead of whole docs ...
    dicts.append({"name": file.name, "text": text})

document_store.write_documents(dicts)
```

We also plan a feature that you can later display your search results directly in the original PDFs, but it's currently a bit further down the roadmap.

Hope this helps!
'
