Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'> The solution you provided is giving the following error[...]

Sorry, I should have mentioned that we only added this feature recently. If you want to try this, please install from the latest master branch (via `git pull && pip install -e .`). 

> When you suggest the last line document_store.write_documents(dicts), this is instead of write_documents_to_db(document_store=document_store, document_dir=doc_dir, clean_func=clean_wiki_text, only_empty_db=True) and achieves the same purpose?

Yes, exactly. In an early version of haystack `write_documents_to_db` did both jobs of converting files to dictionaries and writing them to the DocumentStore. After some user feedback, we found that it's better to split this into two separate methods that are easier to understand and customize. So in the latest haystack version you won't find `write_documents_to_db` anymore but rather two separate functions: 
1) `convert_files_to_dicts()`: taking a file directory as input and returning python dictionaries incl. plain text 
2) `document_store.write_documents()`: indexing a list of dictionaries (e.g. coming from `convert_files_to_dicts()` into your DocumentStore 

Example from the current Tutorial: 

https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/84a25c73b3e3d80a0dc02f97876c9ef51f4a1c95/tutorials/Tutorial1_Basic_QA_Pipeline.py#L73-L80


> Does this directly access the PDFs in the directory "<PATH-TO_DIR-WITH-PDFs>" and write them directly to Document Store so that we can proceed with the usual working with retriever accessing them from the document store?

`convert_files_to_dicts()` will read & clean the PDFs from the directory and `document_store.write_documents()` will do the actual "writing". If you want to debug / inspect the results of conversion, it'll be straight forward to just print the dicts returned by `convert_files_to_dicts()` 

> Also, what would this implementation be for using InMemoryDocumentStore().

Just exchanging the line with the DocumentStore should work. 
```
converter = PDFToTextConverter(remove_header_footer=True, remove_numeric_tables=True)
document_store = InMemoryDocumentStore()

dicts = []
for file in Path("<PATH-TO_DIR-WITH-PDFs>").iterdir():
    pages = converter.extract_pages(file_path=file)
    text = "\n".join(pages)
    # optional: do more cleaning here or index single pages instead of whole docs ...
    dicts.append({"name": file.name, "text": text})

document_store.write_documents(dicts)
``` 
(Didn't test this snippet, so let me know if you face any particular issue here)


'

Title: b'Support ranges of top-k in evaluation'
Body:
b"When users evaluate a pipeline, we would like to list evaluation metrics for different values of top-k, e.g., 1, 5, and 10. This issue is about calculating these metrics and presenting them in a tabular format. In future, we could draw plots based on the calculated metrics.

When we evaluate a pipeline with a specific value of `top-k` and store the result in a dataframe, this result also contains parts of the information that we need to calculate evaluation metrics not only for this `top-k` but also for all smaller `top-k`. For example, if we run a pipeline with `top-k=10` for a retriever, we could consider the top 5 retrieved documents and calculate the retriever metrics for this subset.
This approach does not always work for subsequent nodes in the pipeline. For example, the reader might have found the best answers in documents retrieved at rank 6 to 10. As a result, we don't have the readers predictions precalculated for the case when the retriever only returned the top 5 documents and we need to rerun the reader. 

Related larger issue: #1589"

Title: b'tholor'
Body: b"@julian-risch Isn't this covered by now with the new `simulate_top_k` parameters? "

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'Your data format looks good to me. The group by statements are just for datasets with multiple annotated answers to the same questions, which does not seem to be the case for you. The problem is something else:
`_aggregate_answers` is a static method of the SquadData class. So the `self` in `self._aggregate_answers).rename("answers")` in `df_to_data` does not refer to a dataframe but `SquadData`. So what you would like to do is use `SquadData._aggregate_answers`.
You can find its implementation here:
https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/13510aa753d4e390f244398cc50654185dddbcde/haystack/utils/squad_data.py#L216

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:

```
from haystack.utils.squad_data import SquadData
squad_formatted_data = SquadData.df_to_data(df)
```
However, at the moment, this won't work although I think we should make that work.
At the moment, you would need an object of class `SquadData` because `df_to_data` is a method that you could call on that object. Problem is that you need to initialize this object with some data. As a hack around that maybe you could try something like 
```
from haystack.utils.squad_data import SquadData

squad_formatted_data = s.df_to_data(df)
```
with `df` being your dataframe."

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b"Hey @mapapa , 

Thanks for flagging this and sorry to hear that you face such an annoying dependency problem. What python version are you using? After a quick look into it, it seems that this is a general python issue and the most severe XML vulnerabilities have been fixed since python 3.6. See python [docs](https://docs.python.org/3.10/library/xml.html) and this [thread](https://github.com/networkx/networkx/issues/5001#issuecomment-963565097) in the networkx repo for further references.

In addition, our implementation of networkx in Haystack doesn't seem to expose this vulnerability as we are not using any of the mentioned formats (graphml and gexf) from networkx.

If there's no way to relax your enterprise restrictions here, it also seems that the networx folks have implemented the switch from `xml` to the safer `defusedxml` (see https://github.com/yurnov/networkx/commit/2ac4c8ef1d3366671549d565cedfa78ed229e070). With their next release, this should resolve the issue."

Our recent[ blog post on the generation of question-answer pairs](https://www.deepset.ai/blog/generate-questions-automatically-for-faster-annotation), describes how to use generated pairs as a training dataset and how to modify generated pairs with a human in the loop process.

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'Hi @chandana01 what you could try is to change this line of code: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/0aba5ca57dc1714d19f189658dc609a27c6fab22/haystack/document_store/elasticsearch.py#L843

to something like:
`"source": f"doc['{self.embedding_field}'].size() == 0 ? 0 :{similarity_fn_name}(params.query_vector,'{self.embedding_field}') + 1000",`
based on this suggestion here: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/67666697/elastic-search-query-with-cosine-similarity-run-time-error
Thereby, documents that don't have an embedding (yet) are considered dissimilar to any query.

If I am not mistaken, the "wait_for" only waits until the new documents are included in the index. However, the embeddings still need to be calculated and added before you can run a query that makes use of embedding similarity. This is where the `update_embeddings()` method needs to be used with the `update_existing_embeddings`set to `False`: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/0aba5ca57dc1714d19f189658dc609a27c6fab22/haystack/document_store/elasticsearch.py#L910'

Title: b'How to setup documentsearch pipeline with minimal overheads across multiple indexes in same Elasticsearch client'
Body:
b'**Question**
We have a scenario where the documentsearch pipeline has to be setup for different indexes on same ES client. However the pipeline setup with document store, retriever and document search pipeline is taking 10-20 seconds which is not acceptable. The problem becomes acute if one wants to do this in autoscaling setup as the object is not shared across multiple instances. The primary change is only index and all other parameter related to setup remain indentical. 

Are there any smarter ways to reuse the documentsearch pipeline of one index and update with minimal overheads (i.e takes few ms rather than 10-20 seconds for setup)

**Additional context**
Add any other context or screenshots about the question (optional).

**FAQ Check**
- [x] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?

@julian-risch @tholor : Any quick feedback on this shall be very helpful.'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @cvgoudar , 

If I understood you correctly, the problem is twofold: 

**1. Switching the index between queries on the same machine**
This should be possible at query time without any re-loading of the pipeline. Have you tried using this `index` param? You can simply pass it to the pipeline.run() as any other node parameter. For example: 
```pipe.run(query="some", params={"RetrieverNodeName": {"index": "some_index"}})```

**2. Time to load a new pipeline (e.g. when provisioning new instance in autoscaling situation)**
Loading a new pipeline is currently expected to take 5-20 sec. For example, loading a `DocumentSearchPipeline` with a DPR retriever takes on my machine ~ 13 sec, with an `EmbeddingRetriever` it goes down to ~ 7sec. Most of this time is probably spent on loading the actual model from disk into PyTorch / transformers but we should do some more detailed profiling here to understand how we can accelerate this further. Would be helpful if you share some more details on your use case and how this time relates to overall autoscaling times. 
 
 '

It reverts to the index initialized at the time of document_store object creation by default. Without editing the code we may not be able to use this approach on 0.9.0 version. Any thoughts

```
class DocumentSearchPipeline(BaseStandardPipeline):
    def __init__(self, retriever: BaseRetriever):
        """
        Initialize a Pipeline for semantic document search.

        :param retriever: Retriever instance
        """
        self.pipeline = Pipeline()
        self.pipeline.add_node(component=retriever, name="Retriever", inputs=["Query"])

   def run(self, query: str, filters: Optional[Dict] = None, top_k_retriever: Optional[int] = None):
        output = self.pipeline.run(query=query, filters=filters, top_k_retriever=top_k_retriever)
        document_dicts = [doc.to_dict() for doc in output["documents"]]
        output["documents"] = document_dicts
        return output
```

Title: b'Expected behavior of Embedding Retriever with missing embeddings'
Body:
b'**Question**
What is the expected behavior of Embedding based retriever if some documents do not have embeddings

**Additional context**
Unlike tutorial setup where write to document store and retrieval are sequential, in production setup both the writing of documents and retrieval can happen in parallel. However, the write of key-value pair happens faster to document store but embedding creation (update_embeddings) and indexing may take longer. During that time if any other embedding retriever tries to do cosine similarity the code is likely to throw errors as few records may not have embeddings.

If there is an issue it will be a serious concern for production systems where read and writes from document stores happen concurrently and embeddings may be temporarily missing. We are observing a few issues and may be related to this aspect.

**FAQ Check**
- [x] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?

@julian-risch @tholor
'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b"Hi @cvgoudar I understand the concerns and agree that we should think about a different solution than the one we have in place at the moment. 
The document stores handle the documents without embeddings differently. ElasticsearchDocumentStore indeed raises an error message if you try to query by embedding and there are documents without embeddings: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/892ce4a760c6b7d7d108aa01eee985ab6ecf8483/haystack/document_stores/elasticsearch.py#L822
In contrast to that, WeaviateDocumentStore creates dummy embeddings for new documents so query by embedding cannot run into the same problem.

Embedding creation and indexing may take longer than querying, yes. However, we think that parallelization with ray could drastically speed up embedding creation and indexing.
What behavior of embedding-based retrievers would be best for your use case? Allowing queries if some documents don't have embeddings and excluding these documents from the search? Or do you have a different solution in mind? How frequently (rough estimation) would you like to add documents to the document store? "

Title: b'cvgoudar'
Body:
b"Thanks @julian-risch 

For our use case we are good with the following option:   
**Allowing queries if some documents don't have embeddings and excluding these documents from the search**

My suggestion is that this makes a good default option. Based on the document_store type and available option we can support other functionality as well. In summary, we need a parameter that controls the behavior with how retriever works with documents not having embeddings. My recommendation would be to skip the records not having embeddings as the default method or None which makes the default choice based on document_store type."

Title: b'Error in docs/error in documentsearch pipeline node name'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
The documentation describes using documentsearch pipeline with: 
`result = pipeline.run(query, params={"retriever": {"top_k": 2})'`
However, in the [code](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/pipelines/standard_pipelines.py#:~:text=self.pipeline%20%3D%20Pipeline()-,self.pipeline.add_node\(component%3Dretriever%2C%20name%3D%22Retriever%22%2C%20inputs%3D%5B%22Query%22%5D\),-def%20run\(self), when the node is added it is initialized with name "Retriever" - R capitalized.



So either the node name has to be changed to "retriever" (small r) to be consistent with the docs or the docs have to be changed to
`result = pipeline.run(query, params={"Retriever": {"top_k": 2})'`
where r in retriever is capitalized

**Error message**

ValueError: No node(s) or global parameter(s) named retriever found in pipeline.

**Expected behavior**
Pipeline should run and give results

**Additional context**
To fix, either change the example code in the docs or change node name in the documentsearch pipeline

**To Reproduce**
run `result = pipeline.run(query, params={"retriever": {"top_k": 2})'`

- Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?
- Yes I have

 - OS: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
 - GPU/CPU:

 - Retriever: Any
'

b"oh, I fix it!
My external Elasticsearch protocol was 'https', so, I add `scheme='https'` parameter  to `ElasticsearchDocumentStore`.
and my docker es port is 9200, but aws es port was 443!, so I add `port=443` 

```
ES_HOST = 'my es host ip' # ! remove 'http' or 'https' in your Elasticsearh IP 
document_store = ElasticsearchDocumentStore(
        host=ES_HOST,
        port=443,
        scheme='https',
        index=INDEX_NAME,
)
```

thanks!"

Title: b'Eval pipeline on multiple queries and aggregate results'
Body:
b'In https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/1691 we created a first draft of how to run `pipeline.eval()` with one Query and one MultiLabel and store the output of each pipeline node in addition the to the expected ground truth output in a DataFrame.
This issue is about extending that functionality so that we can:

- Run `pipeline.eval()` with a list of queries and labels and aggregate the result of each query into one aggregated DataFrame
- Allow calculation of metrics on the aggregated DataFrame, such as percentage of exact matches

Related larger issue: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1589'

Title: b'Simplify logs management'
Body:
b'After the introduction of the logs capture in the Pipeline's debug function, the loggers have a rather complex configuration that can he hard to debug and understand from the outside. Specific issues are:

- Changing the logger level does not affect the logs output, due to the handlers
- A bit of logs duplication in some scenarios
- Code duplication in the Haystack modules that need a lower log level

and other smaller annoyances.

I propose we rather:
 - Drop the log capture feature from the Pipeline's debug function
 - Remove all handlers from all loggers
 - Set the root logger to `WARNING` to keep most of the underlying libraries quiet (Elasticsearch, FAISS, etc)
 - Set the `haystack` logger to `INFO` to see enough logs during the execution of tutorials and scripts
 - Remove custom log levels from any Haystack module
 - Normalize out usage of log levels across different modules, pushing some logs back to `DEBUG` and a few others up to `INFO`
 - Format all logs coming from `haystack` in a standard way

With all these changes, the only logger configuration needed across the entire Haystack will be concentrated in two lines into `haystack/__init__.py`:

```python 
import logging

logging.basicConfig(format="%(levelname)s - %(name)s -  %(message)s", datefmt="%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S", level=logging.WARNING)
logging.getLogger("haystack").setLevel(logging.INFO)
```

while any other code block related to logging can be removed from the codebase.'

Title: b'Indexing Pipeline with Document Classifier'
Body:
b'https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/1265 introduced a document classification node `FARMClassifier`.
We should check whether this new node can be used in an indexing pipeline (mentioned here: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/1265/files#r668842533). In that case, the classifier could be used to enrich the meta data of documents at indexing time, for example, with zero-shot classification models. The `FARMClassifier` expects a List of Documents as input und returns a List of Documents as outputs. I don't see a reason why it should not work.

We would need to test, for example, a Converter node with a FARMClassifier
```
converter = TextConverter(remove_numeric_tables=True, valid_languages=["en"])
doc_txt = converter.convert(file_path="data/preprocessing_tutorial/classics.txt", meta=None)
...
classifier = FARMClassifier(model_name_or_path="deepset/bert-base-german-cased-sentiment-Germeval17")
...
```
Finally, we would need to check whether the meta field of documents indexed in the document store contain class labels.
'

Title: b'tstadel'
Body:
b'https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1508 replaced FARMClassifier with TransformersDocumentClassifier, so it would look more like this:

```
converter = TextConverter(remove_numeric_tables=True, valid_languages=["en"])
doc_txt = converter.convert(file_path="data/preprocessing_tutorial/classics.txt", meta=None)
...
classifier = TransformersDocumentClassifier(model_name_or_path="deepset/bert-base-german-cased-sentiment-Germeval17")
...
```
Probably it makes more sense to do it after using the PreProcessor, but we might want to keep the flexibility to use it right after the converters or after further preprocessing (e.g. document splitting).

There's a small hurdle to take, as preprocessing usually works on dicts, TransformersDocumentClassifier currently expects Document objects as input. As there is no common conversion logic from dicts to Documents throughout the different DocumentStores we might want to make TransformersDocumentClassifier also work with dicts.'

Title: b'Make all transformers and torch dependencies optional?'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Whenever there is the need to only use the datamodels for documents stored, or ElasticSearch queries directly using text queries only, there is the need to have large dependencies in pytorch and transformers. It would make sense to me to put them as optional, as many parts of the code actually does not explicitly depends on those libraries.
It also can create conflicts of versions for torch and transformers and can prevent using our own models developed separately alongside haystack. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A good way to do this is to simply put the requirements on those libraries optional, and potentially do it in FARM as well. I have seen there are issues on the subject of removing FARM and moving necessary things from there to here, and therefore it would make the dependency management for torch and transformers easier to put as optional.


**Additional context**
This would be especially useful to have models which are trained separately (or were trained using something else than transformers, or were trained long ago) and still use haystack wherever useful for testing and even deployments.
"

Title: b'Evaluate logic of `index` to group Labels and Documents more closely'
Body:
b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As of today, we have two major entities that we store in DocumentStores: `Label` and `Document`. 
Coming from Elasticsearch in the early Haystack days, we stored them in two completely separate "indices" - one label index, one document index.  We kept this "index" logic for other DocumentStores. 

This was problematic as `Labels` had a `document_id` field and it was up to the user that a) the related document is actually existent and b) the right document index was selected. Exporting a training/eval dataset after collecting user feedback only worked when the document index contained the related document. However, when collecting user feedback over time, changing preprocessing settings etc., it happens very easily that many of your existing "user labels" become corrupt and useless as documents have changed over time.

After the refactoring of primitives in #1398 , `Label` has now a `document` field where we directly have all needed information. It's also just persisted as part of the `Label` object in the DB and therefore completely decoupled of the `Document` table/index. 
That solves some of the above problems but creates quite some overhead in storage. Also, users still have to write both labels and documents manually to the DocumentStore when adding an eval set that they want to use for experiments / evaluation runs.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
- Instead of having two separate label and document "indices", it could be useful to choose **one** "index" or "collection" when initializing a DocumentStore. Internally we could still create two indices in elastic with standardized "suffixes" (e.g. <index_name>_docs and <index_name>_labels) but this can differ among document stores.
- Evaluate the relationship between `Label` and `Document` in ORM and if we really want to store `Document` as part of every `Label`
'

Title: b'lalitpagaria'
Body: b'Recently I thought about such scenario in Obsei, while writing issue related to Rubrix integration (https://github.com/obsei/obsei/issues/194)\r\n\r\nThis is what I settled for (mainly inline with your second point). Not all documents may have labels. So idea to keep relationship between them. If there link between Document and Label then, ORM or another collection contains that link information. Now each update calls (which indirectly modify Document), should check if Document linked with Label. If yes then invalidate it. Label should contains all meta data as well like model used, checkpoint used, etc.'

Title: b'Extending for Conversational QA with QueryRewriting'
Body:
b"I think Haystack can be made suitable for Conversational Systems with little adjustments.
- [Open-Retrieval Conversational Question Answering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11364)
Conversation history is prepended to the current question and the result is encoded using BERT-based model.
- [Query Resolution for Conversational Search with Limited Supervision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11723)
Used a BERT-based classifier for picking relevant terms in the conversation history and appends the relevant terms to current question. The rest of the pipeline is based on BM25.
- [A Comparison of Question Rewriting Methods for Conversational Passage Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07382)
An example of an ablation study which could be very quickly done if the proposed solution below would be added to Haystack.

**Proposed solution**
The system could be made conversational by adding a `history: Optional[str[]]` property to [`Label`](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/1244d16010bbfcebc7acd35253383335e6360f04/haystack/schema.py#L80) and a QueryRewriting pipeline node which would work similarly to QueryExpander mentioned in #574 . Then the rest of the pipeline can be built using pipeline elements already present in the framework.

I think adding this feature would make Haystack suitable for researchers of the [TREC CAsT](http://www.treccast.ai) challenge.

I'm looking forward to your feedback!"

Title: b'Timoeller'
Body:
b'Hey @giguru I am super excited about those features :rocket: 

### conversational NLP tests
To be honest I am not an expert in conversational QA but the methods you proposed seem be of good quality (sigir publications) and are recent methods that work well.
From reading the benchmark paper it seems that QuReTeC (your second proposition about query resolution by classifying keywords) seems to be promising. How about we focus on this approach? Since QuReTeC does not add natural text we could use the resulting keywords as input to an Elasticsearch query and combine the retrieved documents with a DPR retriever on the current question (in natural text). How about you start with initial tests, get a term classification model and apply it to some conversational turns?

### conversational data structure
About your proposed solution of adding the history to the Label. So you want to start with a single question (associated to a single user) and then add follow up questions to the history? 
I would rather keep labels and history separate, since they are different concepts. A Label relates to a question - a history relates to one user/session with multiple questions + answer posed. Or maybe I misunderstood your proposition?

### integration with other conversational approaches
We should also make sure that the solution we develop here could be used with other software, e.g. rasa. We have started a discussion on rasa integration in #809 
afaict in this thread we only discuss answering fact seeking questions (after intent classification). Still we should try to make our modelling approaches fit with what is possible to export from other conversational frameworks.'

Title: b'giguru'
Body:
b"**conversational NLP tests**
Then I'll start with coding the term classification model QuReTec and do some tests.

**conversational data structure**
If users would design a new pipeline with a structure like this:
`QueryRewriter` -> `Retriever` -> `Reader`
In order to evaluate this new pipeline, the test data could be a conversational query rewriting datasets like from TREC Cast, CANARD or QUaC in which the input is the current question + list of historical questions and the output is the rewritten question.

For using the pipeline ad-hoc, a `Session` object could manage the history and you could provide to [`pipeline.run`](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/32050fdce3cc6d55ed744e2475b8c2dcee2edd4b/haystack/pipeline.py#L106) via  a `session` argument. However, for evaluation, there is not one ongoing Session. For every question/Label stored in the DocumentStore there is a different history/Session. How do you propose making the historical data available when looping through questions during evaluation?"

Title: b'giguru'
Body:
b"> Hey Giguru, I actually attended the SCAI workshop and talked with Svitlana Vakulenko. She remembered you working with Haystack and I wondered if there is any update on the progress for the conversational query rewriting? It seemed like a promising approach and easy to integrate into haystack.
> 
> We also worked on an integration with Rasa, see https://haystack.deepset.ai/guides/chatbots The query rewriting would of course not work out of the box like this (the chat history will be needed) but I think the existing integration could be extended to include your approach and would make people quite happy.
> 
> What do you say?

@Timoeller , I have finally wrapped up my thesis for my masters ([Github repo](https://github.com/giguru/converse)). 
In the end, I have focused on extending Haystack to be more suitable for research into Conversational Passage Ranking (CPR). Below is a list of the things I have added to Haystack. It seems like the research group where I did my thesis wants to maintain and expand the functionalities.

I have some time now to potentially add some of the features to the Haystack master's. Which of the features do you envision would be useful to integrate into Haystack?

### History
Right now, I simply provide a `history` argument to the `Pipeline.run` which is used by some components, such as the reformulators. 

### Conversational Reformulators
I have implemented a few CQR methods which you could read about in this ([readme and examples here](https://github.com/giguru/converse/tree/master/haystack/query_rewriting)). A reformulator modifies the `query` argument in a pipeline. The `GenerativeReformulator` can be easily added to Haystack, I think. The `ClassificationReformulator`, which implements QuReTec, requires some refactoring. 

### EvalTREC
Additionally, I have added a [`EvalTREC`](https://github.com/giguru/converse/blob/bfe5ccc0af50455074abf7926a31145ac96834a5/haystack/eval.py#L41) Evaluator which uses pytrec_eval, because I found out its computed metrics were not the same as EvalDocuments's computed results. For instance, MRR was not the same. It also allows for using all metrics available in pytrec_eval, such as NDCG@k.

### Qrels support
Furthermore, I have added a `Pipeline.eval_qrels` method to be able to evaluate a pipeline using qrels.

### Anserini support
I have added Anserini based [retrievers](https://github.com/giguru/converse/blob/master/haystack/retriever/anserini.py) which can be used for both sparse and dense retrieval methods. I'm not sure if this would be relevant for Haystack, but its search/indexing methods and prebuilt indices are frequently used in the field of CPR.

### BPR
I have started implementing the BinaryPassageRetrieval ([paper](https://github.com/studio-ousia/bpr/tree/08b70cf4806758223b73b7553df8eeeb5745c8df)) ([repo](https://github.com/studio-ousia/bpr/tree/08b70cf4806758223b73b7553df8eeeb5745c8df)) method in the DenseAnseriniRetriever. If Haystack aims to support huge datasets, BPR is very promising. The passage embeddings of Natural questions are reduced from 61Gb using a Flat index type to only 2GB using a Binary Flat index type.



"

Title: b'Implementing cosine similarity in Milvus and Weaviate doc stores'
Body:
b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In Milvus docstore's documentation, it's mentioned that cosine similarity is not supported. In Weaviate's there is no mention of that fact, but from the source codes it can be seen that the similarity parameter is not used anywhere within the module.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Can't we implement cosine on our side for both Milvus and Weaviate, since it's pretty easy?
I would suggest **normalize_embedding()** abstract method in the Base docstore, which would resolve to:

```python
def normalize_embedding(emb: np.ndarray)->np.ndarray:
  return faiss.normalize_L2(emb)
```
in the FAISS doc store, to a stub

```python
def normalize_embedding(emb: np.ndarray)->np.ndarray:
  return emb
```
in Elastic Search and InMemory doc stores, since they implement cosine similarity search directly, and to

```python
@njit(fastmath=True)
def normalize_embedding(emb: np.ndarray)->np.ndarray:
  norm=np.sqrt(emb.dot(emb))
  if norm==0.0:
    return emb
  else:
    return emb/norm

```
in Milvus and Weaviate.

_(in my testing np.sqrt(emb.dot(emb)) is twice faster than linalg.norm) And utilizing of Numba makes it another ~7 times faster._

normalize_embedding would be called at **write_documents**, **update_embeddings**, and **query_by_embedding** steps if sel.similarity is "cosine".

**write_documents()** method should acquire a new parameter, already_normalized: bool=False, which will only be used if documents come with precomputed embedding. With already_normalized=True, they will be treated as already normalized.

Plus maybe we could support some checking for normalization like **are_embeddings_normalized(fast:int=0)**, that, with fast=100, would sample 100 random embeddings and return if all they are normalized.

Smth like that. What do you think?

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Are there some other useful transformations that can be applied to embeddings?
'

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body:
b"Hi @fingoldo! I think it would definitely be nice to support cosine similarity across all document stores, given that it is recommended to use cosine similarity with sentence-transformers models. Nice that you already provided a way how this could be implemented! One minor thing: I think faiss' normalize_l2 method normalized the vector in place, so the method would probably need to look something like this:

```python
def normalize_embedding(emb: np.ndarray)->np.ndarray:
  faiss.normalize_L2(emb)
  return emb
```

@tholor What do you think about this?"

Title: b'fingoldo'
Body:
b"> One minor thing: I think faiss' normalize_l2 method normalized the vector in place, so the method would probably need to look something like this:
> 
> ```python
> def normalize_embedding(emb: np.ndarray)->np.ndarray:
>   faiss.normalize_L2(emb)
>   return emb
> ```
> 
> @tholor What do you think about this?

Indeed, you are right. All needs to be done inplace then, actually it's no need to waste time allocating new memory. The signature becomes ->None then:

```python
@njit(fastmath=True)
def normalize_embedding(emb: np.ndarray)->None:
  norm=np.sqrt(emb.dot(emb))
  if norm!=0.0: emb/=norm
```"

Title: b'Implement get_document_store() based on retriever in pipeline'

The `get_document_store()` method in the pipeline only works if the document store is a component within the pipeline. That's the case for indexing pipelines but not for query pipelines. I would like to be able to use `get_document_store()` with a query pipeline and get the document store from the retriever in the pipeline.

`get_document_store()` could check first if there is a document store component in the pipeline. If not, it could check if there is a retriever node and what document store it uses.
Note:There might be edge cases where we have multiple retrievers with different document stores.

I accessed the retriever node in the pipeline and then its document store manually here:

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b"I had a look at where the exception is raised: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/13510aa753d4e390f244398cc50654185dddbcde/haystack/nodes/retriever/sparse.py#L177

The problem is that the TfidfRetriever uses a dataframe `df` to store paragraphs and term frequencies and inverse document frequencies that need to be calculated in the `fit()` method based on documents stored in the document store. This calculation needs to be done before any document retrieval step can be executed. To this end, `fit()`is called in the `init()` method of the TfidfRetriever here: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/13510aa753d4e390f244398cc50654185dddbcde/haystack/nodes/retriever/sparse.py#L134
However, if there aren't any documents yet, the dataframe `df` remains empty, no scores are calculated and any retrieval step fails with the reported exception.

A quick fix is to run `self.fit()` if self.df is None and before the check that throws the exception: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/13510aa753d4e390f244398cc50654185dddbcde/haystack/nodes/retriever/sparse.py#L176
I created a PR for that #1665"

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'You just need to put the arguments in your run method that you expect from a previous node. In the case of a PreProcessor that is very likely `documents`. Then you can modify those documents as you wish and return them. 
Be aware that the second element you return is the name of the outgoing edge that the next node can connect you. Unless you want to do more complex branching in your graph, you should always return "output_1" here: 

```

class DataPreprocess(BaseComponent):
    outgoing_edges = 1

    def run(self, documents):
        # do whatever you want here and modify the documents
        preprocessor = PreProcessor(
            clean_empty_lines=True,
            clean_whitespace=True,
            clean_header_footer=False,
            split_by="word",
            split_length=200,
            split_respect_sentence_boundary=True
        )
        docs_default = preprocessor.process(documents)
        # put everything in a dict so that the next node can access these documents again
        output= {"documents" docs_default}
        return output, "output_1"

```

'

Title: b'MichaelBitard'
Body:
b'I found a really ugly ~~solution~~hack: instanciate multiple pipelines, and ensure they are not used concurrently via mutex.

in rest_api/controller/search.py I replaced the PIPELINE and /query code by:

```python

from random import randrange
from threading import Lock

NUMBER_OF_PIPELINES = 6
PIPELINES = []
MUTEXES = []
for i in range(NUMBER_OF_PIPELINES):
    logger.info(f"Loading pipeline: {i}")
    PIPELINES.append(Pipeline.load_from_yaml(Path(PIPELINE_YAML_PATH), pipeline_name=QUERY_PIPELINE_NAME))
    MUTEXES.append(Lock())
    logger.info(f"Loaded pipeline nodes: {PIPELINES[i].graph.nodes.keys()}")

PIPELINE = PIPELINES[0]
concurrency_limiter = RequestLimiter(CONCURRENT_REQUEST_PER_WORKER)


@router.post("/query", response_model=Response)
def query(request: Request):
    logger.error("QUERY got request")
    with concurrency_limiter.run():
        pipeline_to_use = randrange(NUMBER_OF_PIPELINES)
        logger.error(f"QUERY Running on pipeline {pipeline_to_use}")
        MUTEXES[pipeline_to_use].acquire()
        try:
            logger.error(f'QUERY concurrency limit not reached, using pipeline: {pipeline_to_use}')
            result = _process_request(PIPELINES[pipeline_to_use], request)
            logger.error("QUERY request processed")
            return result
        finally:
            MUTEXES[pipeline_to_use].release()
```

I needed a quick fix because my client has some tests coming soon, but that's really not a valid workaround.'

b"Firstly, thanks @lalitpagaria for pointing this issue to me over slack!

Hi @tholor, I have been exploring the best way of answering questions from tables as well for some other work. Yes, even if we split the table when passing to TAPAS / TaBERT, in the worst-case scenario when the answer is not in the table or i.e., is in the last batch of the table, it'd considerably slow it down and generally, for all cases, you'd have to fine-tune it, even then 100% accuracy isn't guaranteed, however, in structured data, the data can be extracted with 100% accuracy, given human is writing the query (SQL/DSL), etc.


What I propose:
Use a text2sql seq2seq model, user inputs the text query model generates the corresponding SQL then run the generated query on ES index. I believe we can also publish something (a small research paper) out of this by giving the comparative analysis with approaches that directly feed data to the model instead of generating text queries i.e., comparison of extractive vs generative tabular QA approaches.

We can use this as a starting point --> [https://github.com/naver/sqlova](https://github.com/naver/sqlova), and train our own models using transformers package of all sizes (small, medium, large) and host them on huggingface and have plug and play models. Let me know what do you think of this approach?

b'**Question**
Is there a way to save the trained model after each epoch on haystack?

**Additional context**
from haystack.reader import FARMReader
reader = FARMReader("ahotrod/albert_xxlargev1_squad2_512")
reader.train(
    data_dir=data_dir,
    train_filename="dev-v2.0.json",
    use_gpu=True,
    n_epochs=50,
    save_dir="my_model"
)

I am using a huge model for QA model training, and it takes around 1.5 hours to complete one epoch. So I usually have to train this model on Colab for more than 24 hours (more than 50 epochs). If there is any interruption, the training stops, and there won't be any model to use for inference. Can you please let me know if there is a feature to save the model after each epoch and if not, can you introduce this feature at the earliest?

**FAQ Check**
- [x] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?
'

Title: b'bogdankostic'
Body: b"Hi @gak97! As of now, this is not possible, unfortunately. \r\n\r\n@tholor In principle, this should be quite easy to implement, as the functionality is available in the Trainer. We would just need to add the arguments `checkpoint_every` and `checkpoint_root_dir` to the reader's train method and pass them on to the Trainer."

Title: b'tholor'
Body: b"Yeah, let's expose those existing arguments from the [Trainer](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/24483d7bad9132e0551457f5dda9a1e16e99a37e/haystack/modeling/training/base.py#L131) in `reader.train()`. @gak97 Are you maybe interested in creating a pull request yourself here? We can guide you :). If not, we can tackle it with our team in one of the next sprints."

Title: b'gak97'
Body: b'Hi @tholor, Thank you for the quick response! Please let me know how I can add the checkpoint after every epoch to the reader.train() function in farm reader. I have created a new branch. I will make the changes and create a pull request once it is done.'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @gak97 , It should be sufficient to: 
- add three new args to reader.train():  `checkpoint_every, checkpoint_root_dir,  checkpoints_to_keep`
- pass these new args down to the Trainer init [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/7e063b77d29988ad6ca210448e80b3403533ddc1/haystack/reader/farm.py#L246)
- the Trainer class will then use them [internally](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/24483d7bad9132e0551457f5dda9a1e16e99a37e/haystack/modeling/training/base.py#L131) to store checkpoints every X steps in the chosen directory'

Title: b'gak97'
Body: b'Hey @tholor , I have made the changes that you mentioned above. Is it not required to have `from_epoch` and `from_step` arguments in the reader.train(), if we need to resume training from a particular checkpoint?'

Title: b'tholor'
Body: b'@gak97 No, we would then rather need to replace the regular Trainer init in reader.train by `create_or_load_checkpoint()`(see  https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/24483d7bad9132e0551457f5dda9a1e16e99a37e/haystack/modeling/training/base.py#L389). This method will check if a checkpoint is there and if yes continue training from it. If no checkpoint is there, it will just create a new Trainer instance. '

Title: b'gak97'
Body: b'@tholor I think resuming training from a checkpoint is an essential feature here. Because, even if we could save the model after each epoch, it is not possible to train the model beyond certain epochs (25 epochs in my case) due to colab runtime limitations. So, should I replace the reader.train init by https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/24483d7bad9132e0551457f5dda9a1e16e99a37e/haystack/modeling/training/base.py#L113 and add the `create_or_load_checkpoint()` function?'

Title: b'tholor'
Body: b'Yes, instead of calling `Trainer(...)` in `reader.train()` we use `create_or_load_checkpoint()`'

Body: b'I have made the changes and created pull request #1554. Please let me know if I have to make any other changes. '

Title: b'Can InMemoryDocumentStore save and load?'
Body:
b'**Question**
When I using InMemoryDocumentStore for large documents, there seems no method to save the documents and load them afterward. Will InMemoryDocumentStore support save and load in the future? Or am I just missing some relevant information?

**FAQ Check**
- [x] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://haystack.deepset.ai/overview/faq)?
'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body: b"Hello @CandiceYu8, currently `InMemoryDocumentStore` doesn't support save and load operations. If you work with large collections of documents, you might consider simply switching to a document store that support save and load (for example `FAISSDocumentStore`), or to one that persists your data (like `ElasticsearchDocumentStore`).\r\n\r\nHowever, if you have in mind a specific usecase where this feature is useful or necessary, let us know! In principle it can be done, it's just not implemented right now."

Title: b'CandiceYu8'
Body: b'@ZanSara Thank you for your answer. I do not have a specific use case, but just use InMemoryDocumentStore for quick testing. Hoping to find save and load support soon.'

Title: b'ZanSara'
Body: b'@CandiceYu8 understood. In any case, I believe this would be a quick and simple feature to implement (for example, using the `pickle` module from the standard library). So if you are interested in contributing, this could be a good issue to start from :)'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b"Hey @predoctech, 

I had a quick look at the paper. Looks interesting!
They also added a bit more code to the repo today.

As the models are rather generating the answers (text2text) than extracting them, I could imagine integrating them in Haystack via a separate Reader class (e.g. TransformersGenerativeReader). 
Usage on single passages seems straightforward, but scaling this to longer docs + aggregating results might involve more work. 

I will put this in our backlog with medium priority. I don't see it on our immediate roadmap, but we are definitely open for community contributions in the meantime. 



 
> On a related note is T5 model found on HuggingFace already functional in Haystack?

No, not yet as it's not an extractive QA model and therefore cannot be used in the regular QA pipelines. Also: Have you seen any T5 QA model on the model hub yet? 
The T5 models in the unifiedQA repo are the first ones that I saw in transformers format out there, but maybe I missed some.
"

b'@ZanSara no problem. Below are some changes we made to the docker-compose.yml file. 
To use the **network_mode:bridge**, otherwise the default ip created by docker MAY conflict with your internal network ip addresses. The sample file after changing is as below:

```yaml
version: "3"
services:
  haystack-api:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    image: "/deepset/haystack-cpu:latest"
    # Mount custom Pipeline YAML and custom Components.
    # volumes:
    #   - ./rest_api/pipeline:/home/user/rest_api/pipeline
    ports:
      - 8000:8000
    environment:

      #- ELASTICSEARCHDOCUMENTSTORE_PARAMS_HOST=elasticsearch
      #- DOCUMENTSTORE_PARAMS_HOST=elasticsearch
      - DOCUMENTSTORE_PARAMS_HOST={ip address of elasticsearch host}
    restart: always
    #depends_on:
    #  - elasticsearch
    command: "/bin/bash -c 'sleep 15 && gunicorn rest_api.application:app -b 0.0.0.0 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker --workers 1 --timeout 180'"
    network_mode: "bridge"
  elasticsearch:
    # This will start an empty elasticsearch instance (so you have to add your documents yourself)
    #image: "elasticsearch:7.9.2"
    # If you want a demo image instead that is "ready-to-query" with some indexed Game of Thrones articles:
    image: "/deepset/elasticsearch-game-of-thrones"
    ports:
      - 9200:9200
    environment:
      - discovery.type=single-node
    network_mode: "bridge"
  ui:
    build:
      context: ui
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    image: "/deepset/haystack-streamlit-ui:latest"
    ports:
      - 8501:8501
    environment:
      - API_ENDPOINT=http://{your ip address}:8000
      - EVAL_FILE=eval_labels_example.csv
    network_mode: "bridge"
```

```

Do you guys have some thought for this feature?

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b"@akkefa We had another discussion in the team about the use cases for it and how to keep the scope of this PR manageable. 

Let me try to summarize our thinking about this:
- Let's treat pipelines as the core object here and not think more granularly about nodes that we want to add or params that we want to change. So there's no need right now to update a pipeline config and thus no need for additional features in the pipeline class itself
- So let's try to sketch the workflow of interacting with pipelines as a central unit via REST API and how this relates to the existing YAMLs: 
- We want to allow multiple pipelines in the REST API. Every pipeline gets stored as a different yaml on disk. Every pipeline has a name as an identifier that can be used for naming the files and identifying different pipelines in the endpoints.
- Add a new pipeline via `POST` to `pipelines/` with the yaml as payload (it will be stored in a separate new yaml on disk with the given name)
- See a pipeline config via `GET` to `pipelines/<name>`
- See all available pipeline names via `GET` to `pipelines`
- Delete a pipeline via `DELETE` to `pipelines/<name>`

So which pipelines will now be active and used for queries? 

Option A: Only a single pipeline active at a time
- activate a pipeline by sending a `GET` to `pipelines/<name>/activate`
=> this will unload the old pipeline and load the new one for all future queries from this point

Option B: Multiple active pipelines
- activate a pipeline by sending a `GET` to `pipelines/<name>/activate` 
- deactivate a pipeline by sending a `GET` to `pipelines/<name>/deactivate`
- set the default pipeline by sending a `GET` to `pipelines/<name>/default` 
=> there can be multiple active pipelines at a time. When you call `/query` you can supply an optional pipeline name to indicate which pipeline to use. if not supplied, the default pipeline will be used.

Our suggestion for moving forward here: 
- Let's focus on Option A, i.e. a single active pipeline at a time 
- We might extend to multiple pipelines later in the future if we see good use cases for it. This should be relatively easy once we have the basics in place
- 
So in summary we would see those endpoints: 
```
GET /pipelines    list of pipelines
GET /pipelines/{pipeline_name}/yaml  get the YAML
POST /pipelines  add pipeline
POST /pipelines/{pipeline_name}/activate
POST /pipelines/{pipeline_name}/deactivate (edited) 
```

Does this make sense to you? Do you have any other design questions / concerns before starting with a first draft PR?"

Title: b'akkefa'
Body:
b'@tholor I have pretty much a good sketch in my mind, how this feature will work.  Thanks for the detailed clarification.

Just needs to clear one thing when we are going to save a pipeline in the YAML file it contains a single pipeline with a unique name identifier.

Right now in  `rest_api/pipelines.yaml` file.  There are two pipelines mentioned **query** & **indexing**.'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Good point. We would suggest that `GET /pipelines` lists the pipeline names, the type (indexing or query), the status (activated/deactivated) and the associated yaml filename. 

So the unique name will be really the name of the pipeline rather than the filename.

The default `rest_api/pipelines.yaml` can still contain two pipelines and users can also post yamls with multiple pipelines via `POST /pipelines  add pipeline`
 
When you call `POST /pipelines/{pipeline_name}/activate` it depends on the pipeline type if you switch the indexing or query pipeline. 
'

Title: b'Making documents import parallel'
Body:
b"Hi, and thanks for this incredible framework. After reading the docs, Haystack seems to be optimized for inference and training.
But what about importing data?

I have tried ES and FAISS as document stores, both times importing speed was not more than 300 docs/second (and I have pretty small documents), and CPU/ram were clearly underutilized. Without persisting step, my Python importing pipeline achieves 30_000 docs/sec (string parsing, dict fields removals, etc). So it's definitely single-threaded write_documents() which is the performance bottleneck.

Bogdan Kosti mentioned in a Slack discussion that multi-threading is not (yet) used in the write_documents methods. In ElasticsearchDocumentStore, according to him, it could be achieved by exchanging the bulk method for parallel_bulk.

As for all other document store types, including FAISS, does any of them allow parallel inserts?
I tried FAISS with the default SQL store, and the results were inferior and clearly limited by single threading. What should I try?

I noticed that in SQL store it creates some unique ID, probably random (like: 'id': '100005c6206be23c9fce1539850b7896'). Is that key assigned by Haystack or the underlying database? In many cases collections already have some natural unique id field. What if Haystack would allow specifying one of the existing fields as an ID field? In that case, at least, dumping data into the underlying SQL store could be performed in parallel by multiple Dask or joblib workers.
Actually, even if the ID is some hash of the document's body, it can be computed in parallel.  

Please advise."

Title: b'oryx1729'
Body:
b'Hi @advaitdeshmukh @lalitpagaria @thegrojas,

The current implementation of FAISSDocumentStore does not play well with the REST APIs. Each instance of the document store creates a new in-memory FAISS index, so, in the case of REST API with Query & Indexing Pipeline, it ends up in two different indices.

As a quick fix, for now, [this PR](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/1430) prevents the use of FAISSDocumentStore in Indexing Pipeline for REST API.

You can choose from Elasticsearch, Milvus, or Weaviate for working with Dense Retrievers. Elasticsearch would suffice for a small number of documents(~few thousand). For larger workloads, it might be worth trying with Milvus or Weaviate. You can find some speed benchmarks for retrievers here: https://haystack.deepset.ai/benchmarks/latest. 

Additionally, with #1430,  the [retriever was added](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/1f859694f13fb4361404e7fd97f3cabd21c809eb/rest_api/pipeline/pipelines.yaml#L48) in the Indexing Pipeline that automates creation of embeddings, and a new [DPR Pipeline YAML](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/rest_api/pipeline/pipelines_dpr.yaml) was introduced. 

Hope that helps. Please feel free to update here if you still face issues. 
'

Title: b'Re-design primitives'
Body:
b'Let's re-think **what** core data types / primitives we need in Haystack and **how** we want to structure them (attributes, methods, types ...).

As of now, we have in schema.py: 
- `Document`
- `Label`
- `MultiLabel`

In addition, we use in the REST API: 
- `Answer`
- `Request`
- `Response`

What we should do: 
 - Let's discuss if we need more primitives (in the past we thought about splitting `Label` into multiple classes for QA / Retrieval; we also want to have "standardized" input / output objects for pipeline nodes)
 - Let's examine if the current primitives need any refactoring (e.g. attribute names, redundancies ...)
- Let's document all primitives 

Related to: 
- Will help to standardize input/outputs of pipelines and therefore enable validation of pipelines (#600)
- Will help to standardize request and response types in REST API for different pipeline types
- Might simplify evaluation of different pipelines types
- Might be needed to store labels for other pipeline types'

Title: b'brandenchan'

b'Hi @VETURISRIRAM, 3mins does sound pretty long to me and I'm pretty sure Haystack can do better. So to start, you have a lot of transformers models being used in this pipeline. Could you just confirm that you have a GPU engaged? (You can use `nvidia-smi -l 1` in the command line to see GPU usage)

My biggest suspicion for why it's taking this amount of time is that your documents might be very long. The amount of work being passed to the reader is a function of you `top_k_retriever` and the length of your documents. Your `top_k_retriever` is already quite low so I would ask how long your documents are. You might want to split them into smaller chunks so that the Reader has less work on its plate. We recently just released [this blog article](https://medium.com/deepset-ai/parameter-tweaking-get-faster-answers-from-your-haystack-pipeline-b94f0f528111) which explains how to do all this. 

And finally, you've using the "ahotrod/albert_xxlargev1_squad2_512" Reader model which is definitely one of the bigger models out there. If you opt for a `base` sized model like "deepset/roberta-base-squad2" or a `small` sized model like "deepset/minilm-uncased-squad2", you could probably increase Reader throughput by at least 2x. See our benchmarks [here](https://haystack.deepset.ai/bm/benchmarks).

I hope these tips help!'

Title: b'brandenchan'
Body:
b"Hi @pjchungmd , you're right in that Haystack shows results on texts after preprocessing. The task of text alignment is really not a very easy one. The PreProcessor performs 2 tasks - cleaning and splitting. While its possible to reconstruct an original text from its split chunks, cleaning is a destructive process, meaning that its not possible to reconstruct the original from cleaned text.

I wonder if you could share some more details about your use case so that we can find a solution for you? Is it essential that your answers are situated in the original, unprocessed text? Do you need to do this for every single search? 

I imagine it must often be the case that the extracted answer string only occurs once in the original document in which case matching is probably trivial. Things get harder if there are multiple occurrences of that string and even harder still if the answer span was affected by preprocessing. Knowing how often each of these cases occurs would be helpful in figuring out an efficient solution.

One general tip I can give is that the processed documents will still have the IDs from their original documents but also have a `split_id` in their meta field. If your original document is split into 3 passages, the `split_id` will tell you whether you're looking at the first, second of third passage of that original document."

Title: b'pjchungmd'
Body: b"Hi @brandenchan , unfortunately my use case does require matching the extracted answer spans to the original text. One way that I've approached this problem has been to only split the text into chunks that fit within the 512 token length limit and use RoBERTa since it uses the BPE tokenizer, because it's fairly easy to reconstitute the text from tokens that way. This was not the case with the BERT tokenizer... One thing I have not done is measure whether not performing preprocessing would improve the performance. Do you perform the preprocessing steps because they are substantially improving performance?"

Title: b'brandenchan'
Body:
b"Ok I see. It seems you're thinking about passage splitting for the sake of ensuring text fits into the 512 token limit. I should mention that Haystack can actually deal with documents of any length. Our lower level framework FARM abstracts away this token limit. The reason we are doing document splitting in Haystack is for system performance - by having shorter documents, less text is being passed on to the Reader which in turn reduces the query time. Because of this, our document splitting is not done in terms of number of tokens but rather the number of words or sentences.

I should state here that preprocessing is only an optional step in Haystack. If you'd rather not do any document cleaning / removal of whitespaces, that's totally an option. The impact of this really depends on the dataset but if you already have relatively clean text, it shouldn't make so much difference. We would still recommend splitting documents into moderate size chunks (1000 words for sparse retrievers or 100 words for dense retrievers).

If you perform document splitting with no cleaning, I am confident that you can actually figure out the exact position of the extracted span in your original documents. Very happy to guide you through any of these steps if you want more information!"

Title: b'Unify Query & Indexing Pipelines in YAML'
Body:
b'In the current YAML configuration, Query & Indexing Pipelines can be defined independently. 

In a typical usage scenario, the Query & Indexing Pipelines are tightly coupled together, hence would be useful to have a unified representation in the YAML. It also enables the implementation of compatibility checks between Query & Indexing Pipelines in the future.

## Proposed Schema 

```YAML
components: 
    ....
    
pipelines:
  query:
    - name: query_pipeline
      type: Pipeline
      nodes:
       - name: ESRetriever
         inputs: [Query]
       - name: Reader
         inputs: [ESRetriever]

  indexing:
  - name: indexing_pipeline
    type: Pipeline
    nodes:
      - name: PDFConverter
        inputs: [File]
      - name: Preprocessor
        inputs: [PDFConverter]
      - name: ESRetriever
        inputs: [Preprocessor]
      - name: DocumentStore
        inputs: [ESRetriever]
```

Both `query` & `indexing` are a list to allow multiple pipelines that could be chosen dynamically at run-time. For now, the APIs would support a single Pipeline for both.'

Title: b'oryx1729'
Body: b'@tholor and I had a discussion on it. We decided to hard-code the pipeline name to `query` & `indexing` in the cases where the unification of pipelines is required. \r\n\r\nClosing the issue for now. In the future, we can reevaluate if we want support for multiple query & indexing pipelines.'

Title: b'Allow embeddings for multiple fields'
Body:
b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Right now we only create **one** embedding per document for **one** text field. 
It would be helpful to increase flexibility here and let users create embeddings for **multiple** fields in one document (e.g. text, title, abstract ...)

Optional: In addition, we could think of allowing multiple embeddings for **one** field. This could be helpful when comparing multiple retrievers and you don't want to re-index all the documents. We should, however, evaluate the downsides here again - especially around usability. So far such kind of "experiments" are quite separated by different indices and it's easy for the retrievers to use the correct embedding by default. With multiple embeddings per field, the user will probably need to supply an additional "name" of the embedding that shall be used. Also, the majority of time is spend on creating the embeddings. So the diff between adding new embeddings and a whole new "index" (docs+embeddings) should not be that huge.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Change the schema in document stores. In SQL: get rid of the single "vector_id" field and create new tables for embeddings (see some ideas below). In elastic: we could simply add multiple embedding fields per doc and maybe introduce some naming conventions (e.g. "_embedding_"+<field_name> 


**Additional context**
Originating from the discussion here (https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1505#issuecomment-930633469) where @fingoldo commented:  

> Could we change SQL tables layout to support more than one embedding, potentially from more than one provider? As I see it, problem is that the documents table has only one unique vector_id field, and different retrievers can create arbitrarily vector IDs. But we could use as many vector_ids fields as we need, in theory.
I actually don't know the reason of limiting all work to only one "text" field. Let's say I am working with scientific papers. I can have many text fields: title, abstract, full_text, reviews. And I can already load all of them into Haystack. But why am I limited to working (creating embeddings, querying) with only one of those fields, which I should decide upfront and can not change without re-importing WHOLE collection each time?
It would be so logical from the end user's point of view, at the update_embeddings() step, to pass a field_name parameter (to specify the exact field they want to create embeddings for) and embedding_name parameter to be able to use more than one model or even vector storage engine for that field, and find the right tradeoff between accuracy vs storage/compute requirements, all that without reimporting possible millions or billions of documents for no reason.
embedding_name by default could serve as a convenient label, I would suggest bookkeeping of the retriever model metadata (model, vector_dim, vector store) in a separate table. When no embedding_name is provided by the user, the retriever can still be matched by that metadata and results would go to the correct DB field without wasting disk space.
We actually could lower requirements a lot by allowing Haystack users to connect to any pre-loaded and existing DB table by specifying its name in the doc store init() method, no?
We would only need to maintain a table of embeddings (id primary key serial, table_name, field_name, model_metadata,vectors_created_at,vectors_updated_at,vectors_queried_at,user_metadata) unique (table_name, field_name, model_metadata)
and a table of vector_ids (embedding_id references embeddings(id),document_id,vector_id) unique(embedding_id,document_id).
PROS:
ability to work with existing tables
ability to work with multiple text fields as first-class citizens
ability to quickly switch between different embedding generation models
ability to track stats (how many time embeddings creation took, hardware used, what was the accuracy for each model/method, etc)
CONS:
a few extra parameters
additional method to delete vector ids not unused for a long time
'

Title: b'fingoldo'
Body: b"I think it depends on where Haystack wants to be in this entire ecosystem and what problems/pain points it focuses on. Since there are currently multiple vector indexing solutions, most are only capable of storing vectors, some beginning to add the ability to store additional data pieces (Milvus), some with the ability to do advanced processing (Weaviate). Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @ankh6 , 

> write documents into a database (POST /documents)
retrieve resources from the database (GET /documents/{documentId})
update existing resources from the database (PUT /documents/{documentId})
delete resources from the database (DELETE /documents/{documentId})

Yep, all of those make sense to me. @lalitpagaria was there any reason why you initially proposed 4x POST endpoints? Distinguishing into POST/GET/PUT/DELETE feels more common and intuitive. 

> Are there requirements for the document id?

We allow either custom IDs supplied by the user (any str, the user has to ensure that these are unique) or if no id is supplied we create UUIDs here: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/schema.py#L32

I would propose we re-use this code also in the endpoint. For example, the payload for POST /documents could look something like this: 
```
[
{
"text": str, 
"id": Optional[str],
"meta: Optional[Dict[str, Any]],
"embedding": Optional[List[float]])
},
...]
``` 
Behind the endpoint we can then construct `Document` object(s) from it via `Document.from_dict(payload)`. If the user did not supply an id, this will automatically create one.

> Should API calls be added into haystack/haystack/document_store/base.py or haystack/rest_api/application.py ?

Let's create a new file `haystack/rest_api/controller/documents.py` where we put those endpoints and include the module in the `haystack/rest_api/controller/router.py` . 


> What's the testing procedure before submitting a PR ?

For the core package, we have quite many tests that will automatically run in our CI once you open a PR. You can also run them locally via calling `pytest test` from the root of the repository. However, for some of the tests, you will need a running elasticsearch instance. So you either run a local elasticsearch container via `docker run -d -p 9200:9200 -e "discovery.type=single-node" elasticsearch:7.9.2` or you can also deselect those tests via `pytest test -m "not elasticsearch"` (see all possible tags for (de)selection [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/test/pytest.ini))

For the REST API, we don't have many automated tests yet, but you can find them in `test/test_rest_api.py` and run them locally via `pytest test/test_rest_api.py`. I would suggest adding there a few test cases for the new endpoints and use our automated CI for testing quite early on.  

Hope this helps. Let me know if you have any further questions about this. '

Title: b'tanaysoni'
Body:
b'Hi @ahotrod

We used the [tutorial](https://github.com/onnx/tutorials/blob/master/tutorials/Inference-PyTorch-Bert-Model-for-High-Performance-in-ONNX-Runtime.ipynb) notebook to run more benchmarks comparing the performance of ONNX and PyTorch Inference with different batch sizes. 

Here's the code for benchmarks

```python
# %env CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1

# ONNX Runtime Inference

import onnxruntime as rt  
import time

sess_options = rt.SessionOptions()

# Set graph optimization level to ORT_ENABLE_EXTENDED to enable bert optimization.
sess_options.graph_optimization_level = rt.GraphOptimizationLevel.ORT_ENABLE_EXTENDED

# To enable model serialization and store the optimized graph to desired location.
sess_options.optimized_model_filepath = os.path.join(output_dir, "optimized_model.onnx")
session = rt.InferenceSession(output_model_path, sess_options)

for batch_size in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64):
    runtimes = []
    for _ in range(5):
        dataloader = DataLoader(dataset=dataset, batch_size=batch_size)
        batch = next(iter(dataloader))
        batch = tuple(t.to("cpu") for t in batch)
        inputs = {
            'input_ids':      batch[0],                       
            'attention_mask': batch[1],
            'token_type_ids': batch[2],
        }

        # evaluate the model
        start = time.time()
        res = session.run(None, {
                    'input_ids': inputs['input_ids'].cpu().numpy(),
                    'input_mask': inputs['attention_mask'].cpu().numpy(),
                    'segment_ids': inputs['token_type_ids'].cpu().numpy()
                })
        end = time.time()
        runtimes.append(end-start)
    print(f"ONNX Runtime inference time for batch_size {batch_size}: {round(sum(runtimes)/len(runtimes), 4)}")


# PyTorch Inference
model.to("cuda")
for batch_size in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64):
    runtimes = []
    for _ in range(5):
        dataloader = DataLoader(dataset=dataset, batch_size=batch_size)
        batch = next(iter(dataloader))
        batch = tuple(t.to("cuda") for t in batch)
        inputs = {
            'input_ids':      batch[0],
            'attention_mask': batch[1],
            'token_type_ids': batch[2],
        }

        # evaluate the model
        start = time.time()
        outputs = model(**inputs)
        end = time.time()
        runtimes.append(end-start)
    print(f"PyTorch inference time for batch_size {batch_size}: {round(sum(runtimes)/len(runtimes), 4)}")
```

The benchmarks were done on an AWS EC2 p3.2xlarge(V100 GPU) instance with pytorch v1.4.0, transformers v2.4.0, onnx v1.6.0, and onnxruntime-gpu v1.2.0

Here's the comparison of Inference times (in seconds)

| Batch Size | ONNX    | PyTorch | ONNX SpeedUp |
| :-----:    |:----:   | :----:  |    :----:    |
| 1          | 0.0075  | 0.0307  | 4.09         |
| 2          | 0.0089  | 0.0329  | 3.70         |
| 4          | 0.0128  | 0.0364  | 2.84         |
| 8          | 0.0193  | 0.0482  | 2.50         |
| 16         | 0.0348  | 0.0660  | 1.90         |
| 32         | 0.0648  | 0.1068  | 1.65         |
| 64         | 0.1288  | 0.1621  | 1.26         |

It seems ONNX Inference is faster compared to PyTorch when using lower batch size, but the difference decreases as we increase the batch size. Wondering if there's any further optimization that could be done for ONNX Runtime with respect to batch sizing?


'

Body:
b'This paper provides a very good overview of different model compression techniques, including pruning: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.11985.pdf There is a table that summarizes speedup and accuracy drop for the different techniques.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4181769/135262109-592e55f0-e70e-47c0-93bc-fe30ce289bce.png)
My main insights from this study are:
- Combinations of multiple compression methods are needed to achieve state-of-the-art results.
- Most compression methods are model-specific (specific to the model's architecture)
- Model-agnostic knowledge distillation on model output logits ("KD" in the table) achieves largest speedups, for example, by using BiLSTM models instead of Transformers but the performance drop can be significant depending on the task
- Pruning might become more interesting when using specialized hardware at inference time

In my opinion, model-agnostic knowledge distillation on model output logits is the best way forward for the near feature. It's not very complex but still powerful.

If there is better support of https://github.com/huggingface/block_movement_pruning in future, that will become another great option. However, I would wait until there is an update on the following statement: "We are currently benchmarking and exploring inference setups specifically for sparse architectures. In particular, hardware manufacturers are announcing devices that will speedup inference for sparse networks considerably." https://github.com/huggingface/block_movement_pruning#inference-speed'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b'After having thought about different options, we would like to go forward with an implementation of a knowledge distillation method, in particular knowledge distillation from output logits, in #1551'

Title: b'Allow switching vector_dim in FAISSDocumentStore'
Body:
b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Related to https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/135#issuecomment-926801064

> I apologize, is changing of vector_dim of a FAISS store supported, without reimporting all the documents? For example, when I want to test many models to see which one gives the most sensible results. 'cause I tried applying "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2" and it turned out to be a mismatch between default vector_dim of the store (768) and the actual dimension size of the retriever's model (384. is there some standard way to query this number from the retriever, by the way?). When I changed FAISS_store.vector_dim = 384 and tried update_embeddings() again, it was the same error, so I guess changing is not supported at all or must be done at store init step.


**Describe the solution you'd like**
Let's investigate if we find a nice way to support the above workflow.

From the top of my head, I could imagine:
- adding a new method `change_faiss_config` that deletes the existing FAISS index and creates a new one with a given config
- adjusting `update_embeddings` to check whether the vector_dim is compatible with the current retriever. If not, we call `change_faiss_config`

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Further down the road, it might be an alternative to have a method that bundles a few automatic checks for FAISS <-> Retriever compatibility. In addition to just vector_dim, the similarity metric might be one of those things.
 '

Title: b'fingoldo'
Body: b"Is it possible to keep several indexes? It would be the best. Some are taking days to build even on a GPU, and it's not clear from the beginning what is the best combination of accuracy and speed, so a researcher could want to get back to the index he tried previously, it would be painful to recreate that one again... Does Milvus doc store support having multiple indexes over the same document collection (and the same text field) already? Or this functionality is the same for FAISS and Milvus doc stores? If we could implement this ability it would be cool. I know people can forget about having multiple indexes and therefore waste disk space unnecessarily, but we could issue warning in such cases at the doc store init step."

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'FAISS keeps its own indices in memory, so it will be very inefficient to just add multiple indices for different experiments. 
I think it will be better to 1) save the current index, 2) adjust for a new experiment (e.g. vector_dim) 3) populate the new embeddings & run the new experiment. 
You can still load earlier experiments back from disk.

For Milvus: we currently group all docs into "one index" for SQL + Milvus. So you can create multiple indices, but it means you will also need to add your documents again to have them stored in SQL. Changing this might complicate quite a few other workflows and I would be very careful about adding more complexity here.'

Title: b'fingoldo'
Body: b"That's totally fine as long as older indexes can be plugged in again without recreating neither them nor metadata store. But Milvus has no means to sideload embeddings from disk, right. So is it possible to support the ability of going back to different retriever/dimensionality for both FAISS and Milvus? That would be logical."
