Title: b'Different document embedding values between DPR repository and Haystack DPR implementation'
Body:
b"**Describe the bug**
I have tried to embed the same document using both DPR repository (as described [here](https://github.com/facebookresearch/DPR#retriever-inference)) and DensePassageRetriever.

For both the strategies, I have used the same pre-trained model published by DPR authors [here](https://github.com/facebookresearch/DPR/blob/master/data/download_data.py#L206).

However, if I compare embedding representations, they are different.
Why does it happen? shouldn't the same results come out?

**To Reproduce**
I have updated a notebook [here](https://github.com/antoniolanza1996/miscellaneous/blob/e2ba55badc1bf5751c73013a75c3ffa1bfc7fc03/haystack/issues/295/DPRvsHaystack_EmbeddingComparison.ipynb) to better explain the bug. Hopefully, it could help you to find the problem.

**System:**
 - GPU with Google Colab
 - Haystack version: latest
 - DocumentStore: ElasticsearchDocumentStore
 - Retriever: DensePassageRetriever
"

Title: b'Timoeller'
Body:
b'Hey thanks for the detailed report.
Currently haystacks `document_store.update_embeddings(retriever)` does not support embedding the title. See the snippet how the documents are embedded:
```
docs = self.get_all_documents(index)
passages = [d.text for d in docs] # only "text" and not title ("name") is being indexed
embeddings = retriever.embed_passages(passages) 
```

So I think the difference comes from the missing title. You could try embedding questions (they dont have titles) and compare both vectors. I would be very surprised though if they differ.

We are currently refactoring DPR completely and also getting DPR training into haystack in #273 
There we will add the feature of embedding the title as well, because it makes a lot of sense of course. 

If you agree with what I just wrote, could you change the title of the issue to reflect the missing title in document embeddings? If you need a solution more quickly I could also help you creating a PR with the functionality.'

Title: b'antoniolanza1996'
Body:
b'Hi @Timoeller, thanks for your detailed reply.

Title: b'antoniolanza1996'

Title: b'Score vs Probability ordering'
Body:
b'**Question**
I see that the order of answers for Farm is sorted by score instead of probability (confidence). Why is it the case that sometimes the probability of an answer can be higher, yet have a lower score? If this is the case, which one should be used in terms of establishing a threshold of how confident the model is that the answer is relevant?

Thanks!


'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'Hi @crossoveranx answers in FARM are sorted by confidence score. Sorry for the confusion with the different terminology of scores, probabilities and  confidence.
If you are interested, here is the line of code in FARM where the score is set: https://github.com/deepset-ai/FARM/blob/47dfa4f9377b57fc0343f6ecc5321a497b1ef884/farm/modeling/prediction_head.py#L1431

And here is the line where the answers are sorted: https://github.com/deepset-ai/FARM/blob/47dfa4f9377b57fc0343f6ecc5321a497b1ef884/farm/modeling/prediction_head.py#L1467

In the QA results, what I recommend to use always is the `probability`, which gives values between 0 and 1. This variable actually contains the confidence score from FARM. I do not see a good reason to use the variable `score`. As the range of this variable is unknown, it is difficult to define a threshold of how confident the model is that the answer is relevant.

The reason why answers sometimes would be ranked differently with regard to `probability` and `score` is FARM's internal calculation of confidence scores, which only takes into account the start index of an answer but not the end index or the length. I opened [a new issue in Haystack](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1220) and [a new issue in FARM](https://github.com/deepset-ai/FARM/issues/808) for renaming `probability` and `score` or dropping `score` in favor of `probability` and maybe extend FARM's internal calculation of confidence scores to start and end indices. Does that answer your question?

Here is an example answer that shows  'probability' and 'score':
```
{'answer': 'Eddard',
 'context': 's Nymeria after a legendary warrior queen. '
            'She travels with her father, Eddard, to '
            "King's Landing when he is made Hand of the "
            'King. Before she leaves,',
 'document_id': 'ba2a8e87ddd95e380bec55983ee7d55f',
 'meta': {'name': '43_Arya_Stark.txt'},
 'offset_end': 78,
 'offset_end_in_doc': 153,
 'offset_start': 72,
 'offset_start_in_doc': 147,
 'probability': 0.9899835586547852,
 'score': 15.927592277526855}
```'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b'Another reason why answers sometimes would be ranked differently with regard to `probability` and `score` is about no_answers. `probability` takes into account how confident the model is that there is no answer to the question and balances the `probability` accordingly. In contrast, `score` does not take into account no_answers properly.'

Title: b'clarahohohoho'
Body: b"Hi Julian,\r\n\r\nMay I ask what is the exact line for FARM's internal calculation of probability from score? Thank you!"

Title: b'Timoeller'
Body: b'Hey Julian is currently on holiday but here is the correspoing PR in FARM with the line highlighted where the conversion takes place: https://github.com/deepset-ai/FARM/pull/710/files#diff-999218147863bd4bd4110bc3fe932d8321ce4baf01eaae92c7d4b4f4de3bfef4R1197\r\nHope that helps?'

Title: b'clarahohohoho'
Body:
b'Hi Timo,

Thanks for the quick reply and the reference link! It helps a lot :)
So is it right to assume that the score is not proportionate to its corresponding probability, is due to the softmax function only being applied to the start_idx? Thank you!'

Title: b'Timoeller'
Body:
b'Hi Clara,

I guess that depends on what you mean by proportionate? There is no linear relation between the two, and no simple inversable function from score to probability. On the other hand the larger the score the larger typically also the probability.

Some details about the softmax:
The softmax goes over all start logits (start_idx is a vector) so also balances start logits for other possible start locations as well as the "no answer logit" at index 0 of start_idx.

We also include end_idx into the probability value in a later [FARM PR](https://github.com/deepset-ai/FARM/pull/824) which hasn't been released to haystack.'

Title: b'clarahohohoho'
Body: b'Hi Timo,\r\n\r\nApologies, I meant there are situations that the highest probability of an answer does not have the highest score and vice versa. Is there a possible reason for this behaviour? Thank you!'

Title: b'Timoeller'
Body:
b'Understood, thanks for the clarification.

As you said, the ordering will be different when sorting by score vs probability - thats why we are implementing a switch in https://github.com/deepset-ai/FARM/issues/808

As I said, the probability is based on the softmax of all start_logits and then selects the highest value, the score is just based on the value of the highest start_logit. If you should need a quick refresher on what the QA logits are I can recommend reading section "modelling" in Brandens medium post: https://medium.com/deepset-ai/modern-question-answering-systems-explained-4d0913744097'

Title: b'Give warning when labels are overwritten in DocumentStore.write_labels()'
Body:
b'If two `Label` objects with the same `id` field are written into a `DocumentStore`, one seems to overwrite the other silently. It would be good to have at least a warning message printed when this happens.

As a side note, I saw this occur because a user populated `Label.id` with the id of the question instead of the annotation as it should be. Since the `Label` object is a pairing of question and annotation, I can see how a user might make this mistake. The above issue then arose because they had multiple `Label` objects with the same `Label.id` (i.e. a question id).

For clarity, I would be in favor of renaming `Label.id` to something clearer (e.g. `Label.annotation_id`) since it is not always immediately clear to a new user if this should be the question or annotation id.'

Title: b'akkefa'
Body: b"@brandenchan I will be working on this issue. I didn't use the Haystack labelling tool. Can you guide me through steps to replicate the behaviour mentioned above? "

Title: b'brandenchan'
Body:
b"Hi @akkefa, that's great to hear! This actually isn't to do with the labeling tool. Rather, this has to do with the `Label` object found at a `haystack.schema`. 

In many datasets, the one question might have multiple correct answers. In this case, we create multiple `Label` objects and write these into the document store so that they can be used later for evaluation. These `Label` objects are a pairing of the question being asked, and one annotated answer. `Label.id` should be populated with the id of the annotation so that each label object has a unique id. Problems arise if `Label.id` is populated with the id of the question since the document store can only store one label per id. Currently, when these labels are written into the document store, they are silently overwritten.

You can see this behavior for yourself if you initialize multiple Label objects with the same id. After writing them into the document store, you'll see you have less `Label`s. Here's some pseudo code to get you started:
```
labels = [Label(id=1234), Label(id=1234)]
document_store.write_labels(labels)
document_store.get_label_count()
``` 
So I see two things that should be covered by this PR
1) A warning should be raised if we write multiple Labels with the same id into a document store. It would be best if it appears only once per call to `document_store.write_labels(labels)` rather than for every duplicate label id. This warning would ideally show a list of ids which are duplicates and also suggest that Label.id be populated with the id of the annotation, not the question.
2) The `Label.id` doc string description should be updated to be made clear that this is the id of the annotation not the question and that repeated ids will cause the document store to overwrite them"

Title: b'Crawler does not write JSON, but serializes the result dict to a string written in a .json file'
Body:
b'First of all, great work on Haystack! Its an incredible library and I really enjoy playing around with it!

I noticed an odd behavior of the Crawler as in this example:

```python
from haystack.connector import Crawler

crawler = Crawler()
# crawl Haystack docs, i.e. all pages that include haystack.deepset.ai/docs/
docs = crawler.crawl(urls=["https://haystack.deepset.ai/docs/latest/get_startedmd"],
    output_dir="crawled_files",

```

The resulting file looks like this:

```
{'meta': {'url': 'https://haystack.deepset.ai/docs/latest/get_startedmd'}, 'text': 'Knowledge...
```

which is not valid JSON, as described in the docs. The Crawler rather simply serializes the data dict to string and writes it into a JSON file.

A working import to load the result in a next step looks like this:

```python
import ast

# docs[0] being the first result from the crawl run
with open(docs[0], 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    result = ast.literal_eval(f.read())
```

instead of `json.read( ... )`.

As I dont have the overview of the entire lib and how the created text files are used across the different pipelines, I am hesitant to use propose a solution. So I am raising this as a slightly odd behavior for now. Happy to provide a fix though given guidance from other developers.'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'For the first step, you can definitely use FARMRanker or SentenceTransformersRanker in the following way:
```
...
retriever = ElasticsearchRetriever(document_store=document_store)
ranker = SentenceTransformersRanker(model_name_or_path="cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2") # more models here: https://huggingface.co/cross-encoder
#alternative: ranker = FARMRanker(model_name_or_path="nboost/pt-tinybert-msmarco") # more models here: https://huggingface.co/nboost
p = Pipeline()
p.add_node(component=retriever, name="ESRetriever", inputs=["Query"])
p.add_node(component=ranker, name="Ranker", inputs=["ESRetriever"])
```
Note that the Ranker is used for Document Re-Ranking as described in the documentation: https://haystack.deepset.ai/docs/latest/rankermd#Ranker Before re-ranking, there is still a retriever, which could be an ElasticsearchRetriever as in the example here or it could be for example a DPR Retriever or Tf-idf Retriever.'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b'However, for your second use case you need a different approach. ```

p.add_node(component=retriever, name="ESRetriever", inputs=["Query"])
p.add_node(component=ranker, name="Ranker", inputs=["ESRetriever"])
```

Some technical detail: FARMRanker and SentenceTransformersRanker both rely on cross-encoder models. However, FARMRanker builds on models that have two outputs and SentenceTransformersRanker builds on models that have only one output. We are already thinking about how to simplify this difference and how to implement one general Ranker class that chooses between FARMRanker and SentenceTransformersRanker internally (automatically).'

Title: b'oryx1729'
Body:
b'> How can I call write_documents() on a pipeline?

With Pipelines, you can call the `run()` method with inputs to the Pipeline. Depending on the type of Pipeline(Query or Indexing), the corresponding methods get called on the nodes under the hood. For instance, in this case, for the `EmbeddingRetriever` node, `embed_passages()` will get called for an Indexing Pipeline, while `retrieve()` for a Query Pipeline. 

If it's an Indexing `Pipeline`, the document_store's `write_documents()` will be called when you do a `Pipeline.run()`.

----------------

For instance, with the following Pipeline, if you do a `Pipeline.run(file_paths=["path/to/sample.txt"])`, it will process the file to yield documents, create embeddings, and write to the document store.

```yaml
  - name: indexing
    type: Indexing
    nodes:
      - name: FileTypeClassifier
        inputs: [File]
      - name: TextFileConverter
        inputs: [FileTypeClassifier.output_1]
      - name: PDFFileConverter
        inputs: [FileTypeClassifier.output_2]
      - name: Preprocessor
        inputs: [PDFFileConverter, TextFileConverter]
      - name: EmbeddingRetriever  # the embeddings will created for the documents
        inputs: [Preprocessor]
      - name: FAISSDocumentStore # write_documents() will get called here
        inputs: [EmbeddingRetriever]
```

Does that make sense? '

b'The reason why the passage embedding differs for Haystack and Sentence Transformer in your example code is that slightly different texts are encoded. In your example, Haystack does not encode the text "appendix" but the text "appendix" AND an empty string as a placeholder for the title of the passage.

```
embedding_model = SentenceTransformer(retriever.embedding_model)
passage = """appendix"""
passage = [["", passage]]
emb = embedding_model.encode(passage)
```
With this code you get the same embedding and the same cosine similarity scores.

b'No, it's a bit different. Instead of "text" as input to the embed() method, a list ["title","text"] is the input to the embed() method. It's mentioned in the description of the embed() method here: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/17dcb8c23e2e79391965f84c80eff58522c65c52/haystack/retriever/dense.py#L643 SentenceTransformers then processes both elements of the list as sentences, including start and end token if I am not mistaken: https://github.com/UKPLab/sentence-transformers/blob/42c1d69a96a75ce6594da6335b535cac99ee91d3/sentence_transformers/SentenceTransformer.py#L156

  'attention_mask': tensor([
    [1, 1, 0],
    [1, 1, 1]])}
```

and 
`print(embedding_model.tokenize([["", """appendix"""]]))` gives:

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'Here is the tokenization step that handles a list of [title,text]: https://github.com/UKPLab/sentence-transformers/blob/d6c2b956ce946af3ddf75373d41944c07dc7f343/sentence_transformers/models/Transformer.py#L86
It distinguishes strings and list of two strings:
```
    def tokenize(self, texts: Union[List[str], List[Dict], List[Tuple[str, str]]]):
        """
        Tokenizes a text and maps tokens to token-ids
        """
        output = {}
        if isinstance(texts[0], str):
            to_tokenize = [texts]
        elif isinstance(texts[0], dict):
            to_tokenize = []
            output['text_keys'] = []
            for lookup in texts:
                text_key, text = next(iter(lookup.items()))
                to_tokenize.append(text)
                output['text_keys'].append(text_key)
            to_tokenize = [to_tokenize]
        else:
            batch1, batch2 = [], []
            for text_tuple in texts:
                batch1.append(text_tuple[0])
                batch2.append(text_tuple[1])
            to_tokenize = [batch1, batch2]
```'

Title: b'Data from Solr'
Body:
b"Hello,

first, thank you a lot for this repo. I have a quick question.
my data is indexed in Solr. is it possible to use it instead of Elastic search  ?

I can't find documentation in this repo regarding data preparation. Any guidance ? 

thank you a lot in advance.

Best"

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b"Hey @adjouama, 

We currently don't have Solr integrated. However, as Haystack is completely modular, it would definitely be possible to do that. 

What you would need to do: 

1. Implement a `SolrDocumentStore` 
You could take the [ElasticsearchDocumentStore](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/database/elasticsearch.py#L13) as an example and adjust it to Solr. 
This will be the major work, but you won't need all of the implemented functions there (e.g. query_by_embedding is not mandatory). The documentstore is needed for indexing docs, triggering queries and storing the mapping of fields from DB to haystack `Documents`

2. Implement a `SolrRetriever` (or use the in-memory `TfidfRetriever` for smaller prototyping)
The retriever could be rather light-weight, e.g. consider the basic  [ElasticsearchRetriever](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/retriever/elasticsearch.py#L11) which has only ~ 6 lines of code. 

The other major components (Reader, Finder ...) are independent of this and will work out-of-the-box. We also plan to have some advanced Retrievers soon that are independent of the datastore. 

Let us know if you want to tackle this in a PR. We are happy to support you along the way. 
"

Reader methods `eval()`, `eval_from_file()`, and `calibrate_confidence_scores()` have a mandatory parameter `device`. This should not be necessary as the device the Reader is on is already decided in its `init()`method.

b"**Problem**
I am handling multiple instances of Haystack, because I have multiple customers with their own knowledge base, and therefore custom needs.

Since the _pipelines PR_ #922, I am seeing a new possibility : having one file _rest_api/pipelines.yaml_ for each one of our customer, keeping the same code base among all of them. It will ease the maintenance, a lot.

At the moment, I create a file called _haystack/custom.py_ in which i write my python nodes  
```python
from typing import List
from haystack.schema import BaseComponent
from haystack.retriever.dense import EmbeddingRetriever
import numpy as np
from haystack import Document

class TitleEmbeddingRetriever(EmbeddingRetriever):
    def embed_passages(self, docs: List[Document]) -> List[np.ndarray]:
        texts = [d.meta['name'] for d in docs]
        return self.embed(texts)
```
and I import them in the _haystack/__init__.py_ like so 
```python
from haystack.custom import TitleEmbeddingRetriever
```

**Additional context**
For the setup, I am using the REST_API with Docker-compose

Title: b'Improve document stores unit test parametrization'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I noticed that, from developer's perspective, it is not trivial to invoke document/retriever/generator unit tests for a subset of document stores. Most of the document store related unit tests test certain functionality on **all** document stores which in turn require **all** document store setup on a local machine etc. Moreover, most of the unit tests explicitly hard-code all document [stores](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/test/test_retriever.py#L117) which then in turn require updates as new document stores are added. 

Developer has to either run all document stores on a local machine or explicitly change test parametrization in order to execute tests on a subset of stores. 

Wouldn't it be more convenient if we could specify, with a command line parameter, a document store to use in the collected unit tests? In case no explicit command line parameter has been specified then all document stores are registered, and registered in one place rather than explicitly hard-coded in the unit test parametrize marker across the entire unit test code base.

  
**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a command line parameter for document stores to use in unit tests. Remove explicitly hard-coded document stores from the unit test parametrize marker

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Workarounds typically range from temporarily removing hard-coded document stores from the unit test @parametrize marker
Spend substantial amount of time to get all the document stores running. 

**Additional context**

Although I haven't tried, it seems that this could be achieved with a special [pytest_generate_tests](https://docs.pytest.org/en/6.2.x/example/parametrize.html) hook. However, not all cases would be covered with this approach. Unit tests with parametrize marker matrix input such as this [one](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/test/test_generator.py#L416) probably wouldn't work. This could lead to further complexities which would defeat the whole purpose of the new approach. Either way, perhaps I am overlooking something, let's discuss what could be done to improve not only unit tests document stores parametrization but parametrization overall.

"

Title: b'tholor'
Body: b"@vblagoje Good point. I think this would definitely be helpful. \r\nI guess you saw that we have some markers on the test level that allow you to select a subset of tests you want to run (see https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack#heart-contributing and https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/test/conftest.py#L48). However, we don't have anything to select a subset on a more granular level of test params (e.g. doc stores). \r\nI think this has been becoming more and more relevant in the last months as the number of document stores grew quite a bit. Adding a command line param for document stores would be a good solution. "

Title: b'Reading Comprehension: Questions on model choice, context_window_size and preprocessing'
Body:
b'I have a Use case in which i have documents containing paragraphs of text and list of questions whose answers are in the paragraphs.
I started with tutorial 3, my questions are
1) which model should i use for better accuracy?I dont want to use elastic search.
2) I followed the tutorial 3 and the answers I got were pretty accurate but i could not understand what should i keep the context_window_size. As my Ideal situation would be to get the entire paragraph from where the answer is taken.
3) Do i need to convert my data into some specific formats? Rite now I use the doc convertor provided in the documentation.
4) Is it necessary to split the text into paragraphs? or what would be the ideal splitting method?



**Additional context**

'

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b"Hey @aqsa27 , 

Sorry for the late reply. Let me try to help you here.  

> which model should i use for better accuracy? I dont want to use elastic search.

This depends a bit on your use case. What language are you working with? Is it from a special domain (e.g. finance)? What is more important to you speed or accuracy? How many documents do you have?
Without knowing more about your use case, I'd in general recommend a roberta (`deepset/roberta-base-squad2`) or MiniLM (`deepset/minilm-uncased-squad2`) model. You can see a few benchmarks here that might help you: https://haystack.deepset.ai/bm/benchmarks 

> I followed the tutorial 3 and the answers I got were pretty accurate but i could not understand what should i keep the context_window_size. As my Ideal situation would be to get the entire paragraph from where the answer is taken.

You could increase `context_window_size` to a rather large value and after you got the answer you can manually cut it down to the paragraph containing your question. There was a similar issue recently that might help: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/1009. As this seems to be a recurring case, we might add a parameter in Haystack in the future that does this automatically behind the scenes.  

> Do i need to convert my data into some specific formats? Rite now I use the doc convertor provided in the documentation.

What is the filetype of your original documents? The converters are needed when you want to go from pdf->text or docx-> text etc. 

> Is it necessary to split the text into paragraphs? or what would be the ideal splitting method?

Yes, we recommend splitting long documents into shorter paragraphs. Especially when using a dense retriever like DPR as these model can only digest the first ~ 512 tokens of a text.  You can use the `PreProcessor` class to do this within Haystack. There you will find a couple of options how to split. In most cases, you want to split by a certain number of words (e.g. 200) and avoid splitting within a sentence. See this [Tutorial](https://haystack.deepset.ai/docs/latest/tutorial8md) for more information about it.  

Hope this helps! "

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Awesome, thanks for working on it @vblagoje!
A few thoughts on how to slice this work into meaningful stages / pull requests: 
1. As you already proposed, having a first example implementation for inference only is a good first step
2. Adding the option to train (from plain language models) or fine-tune (take retribert and continue on your smaller domain dataset). Even if ELI5 is the dominant LFQA dataset out there, people in the industry might have smaller, private domain dataset that they want to use for fine-tuning.  We know that similar domain datasets exist for DPR finetuning.
3. The models from Yacine Jernite seem like a great start. The next level would probably be C-REALM (Retriever) and RT (Generator) from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.06332.pdf. Just had a quick look some while ago but they seemed to outperform RAG+BART quite a bit. The sparse attention of RT allows for longer sequences which could be very interesting for the given generative task. 
(4. Adding generative models to our [Benchmarking](https://haystack.deepset.ai/bm/benchmarks))

I haven't found the time yet to check your branch (and Yacine's notebook) in detail, but in all the above steps let's make sure to use meaningful abstractions for the retriever and generator classes that fit well with the rest of Haystack. What do I mean by that? We already have an `EmbeddingRetriever` (single encoder) and a `DensePassageRetriever`(dual encoder). If there's a big overlap with `RetribertRetriever` let's rather integrate it there. If not, let's create a new "generic" retriever class that captures the essence of Retribert but would also work with other base models (e.g. Roberta). Same goes for the Generator (RAG is quite specific here at the moment, but maybe there's potential for generalization).  

Happy to review an early PR and give more detailed feedback!
'

b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

self.inferencer.model.save("tmp_model")

Title: b'Introduce QueryClassifier'
Body:
b'**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
With the new flexible Pipelines introduced in https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/596, we can build way more flexlible and complex search routes. 
One common challenge that we saw in deployments: We need to distinguish between real questions and keyword queries that come in. We only want to route questions to the Reader branch in order to maximize the accuracy of results and minimize computation efforts/costs.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**

b'> How would you separate a keyword query from a natural language one then?

I can have reserve keywords (keyword, question, generate, summarise, classifier, etc) which then understand by `QueryParser`. So UI will pass search string to parser and it then have (filter support as well like [Kibana](https://logz.io/learn/kibana-basics-searching-and-filtering-in-kibana/)). By default parser assume all queries as `keywords` queries.
- "keyword: <some text>" -> Parser will treat it as keyword query
- "question: <some text>" -> Parser will treat it as natural question query
- "keyword: <some text> AND summarise: all" -> Parser will run summarisation after keyword query
- "keyword: <some text> AND summarise: each" -> Parser will run summarisation for each docs retrieved by keyword query separately 
- "question: <some text> AND summarise: all" -> Parser will run summarisation after keyword query
- "question: <some text> AND summarise: each" -> Parser will run summarisation for each docs retrieved by keyword query separately
- "keyword: <some text> AND generate: all" -> Parser will run generator after keyword query
- "keyword: <some text> AND generate: each" -> Parser will run generator for each docs retrieved by keyword query separately
- "question: <some text> AND generate: all" -> Parser will run generator after question query
- "question: <some text> AND generate: each" -> Parser will run generator for each docs retrieved by question query separately
- "keyword: <some text> AND generate: all AND query_docs:10 AND generate_docs:2" -> Parser will run summarisation after keyword query retrieve up to 10 docs and generator will generate 2 docs.
- "classifier: <some text>" -> Parser will check with classifier to determine type of query and then execute it

Ultimately it will create one DSL (Lucene can be tweaked for this), which `QueryParser` will understand and parse it and then execute it. Treat Generator, Summariser, Reader, Classifier etc as different optional components of the Haystack and on production user/company can add/remove based on need via new Pipeline APIs (Similar to elasticsearch plugins/add-ons) at runtime.

Title: b'stefanondisponibile'
Body:
b'hello @lalitpagaria and thank for your support on the issue. I don't completely understand the use case of [your last comment](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/611#issuecomment-739928888), but I think what you're trying to say is [what you actually said](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/611#issuecomment-739155092): "_I was suggesting to use single search bar but with keywords support. Like searching in Kibana._" / "_How about user want to use reader / generator but typing queries in non natural question ways?_". This last one is quite interesting by the way, and an interesting feature for the classifier.

However, to understand why we feel the need of a `QueryClassifier` imagine the following situation:

Our index may look something like this:

```json
[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "text": "Haystack is an end-to-end framework for Question Answering & Neural search that enables you to do a lot of fancy things."
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "text": "Haystack is cool."
  }
]
```

Now, let's discuss the problem before rushing to the obvious solution. And of course, let's assume we _don't_ have a `QueryClassifier` yet. Let's start by pretending we don't even have _Haystack_ at all, just a `.json` in your filesystem.

Some user reaches our search bar and types in the following query:
> What can I do with Haystack?

Alright, we have [tranformers](https://huggingface.co/transformers/) or some model to extract the answer from the query. So we load it and [run the query against each of the contexts in our index](https://huggingface.co/distilbert-base-cased-distilled-squad?text=What+can+I+do+with+Haystack%3F&context=Haystack+is+an+end-to-end+framework+for+Question+Answering+%26+Neural+search+that+enables+you+to+do+a+lot+of+fancy+things.):

```json
[
{
    "id": 1,
    "context": "Haystack is an end-to-end framework for Question Answering & Neural search that enables you to do a lot of fancy things.",
    "question": "What can I do with Haystack?" ,
    "answer": "do a lot of fancy things",
    "accuracy": 0.548
  },
{
    "id": 2,
    "context": "Haystack is cool.",
    "question": "What can I do with Haystack?" ,
    "answer": "cool",
    "accuracy": 0.326
  }
]
```

So we're happy, we keep all the records with a satisfying accuracy (let's assume `50%` here), order them accordingly, and give back the best one to the user:

> What can I do with Haystack?  => do a lot of fancy things

---

However, the user types in another query:
> Haystack

Alright, let's run this weird query against our docs:

```json
[
{
    "id": 1,
    "context": "Haystack is an end-to-end framework for Question Answering & Neural search that enables you to do a lot of fancy things.",
    "question": "Haystack" ,
    "answer": "Question Answering & Neural search",
    "accuracy": 0.326
  },
{
    "id": 2,
    "context": "Haystack is cool.",
    "question": "What can I do with Haystack?" ,
    "answer": "cool",
    "accuracy": 0.319
  }
]
```

Well,  I don't know, what should I do with this? Having to judge, I feel that the document with `id: 2` would be more relevant here, because it's shorter and the "Haystack" token has a major impact on it (i.e., _to me_ the second document has a bigger _score_).

> Haystack => ????

---

So, we have 2 problems at least:

1. *We can't scale*: we get slower and slower each time we index a new document, because we have to pass all the documents to our model (i.e. my _Reader_).
2. **The user is not requesting something in a semantic fashion**, so we're spending useless computation (and time) trying to figure out how to extract an _answer_ from our _context_, using something that's not even a _question_. Odd, isn't it? 

## Elasticsearch to the rescue. 

We're having a coffee with our colleague, complaining about our scaling problem, and he comes up with a nice solution.

> Why not putting some search filter **on top** of you're current flow, so each time you will pass just a few docs to your Reader?

Elasticsearch sounds like the perfect solution for that! We throw away our json-database and index everything inside Elasticsearch. This let us also separate two concerns that were living in our model before: _searching_ vs _extracting_.

So the new plan is using a _Retriever_ to gather some documents related the user query (and rely just on that for our search) and then passing those results to a _Reader_ that will extract the proper answer from that subset of our index.

Cool! We solved problem 1, and our structure is more robust and lean now! 
Yet problem 2 is still quite an issue  I mean, yeah, we can do something at the end of our flow, like having a look at our results, and if all the Reader score are bad maybe just returning the document having the best Elasticsearch score, but again...odd 

So we take another coffee with our colleague, and he goes like:
> Well, in those cases, just skip the Reader.

So that's not a bad idea, pretty obvious, we could actually "*skip the Reader*", but our problem is identifying "_**those cases**_".

So @tholor opens his browser, goes to Github and tells:
> "Hey, we need a `QueryClassifier` to identify *those cases* in which the search style **could** (optionally) be influenced by the fact that the user is (or is not) expressing semantically. This may influence the search Pipeline in many ways, surely by performing dynamically the answer extraction done by the Reader."


## Some issues around **this** feature:

1. The classifier _itself_ **is** the core of this issue. (let's forget about Pipelines for a second)
2. The classifier *must* be fast and *not* computationally intensive. (that's probably the main problem to face)
3. The classifier *should* be multilingual.

I've been trying to create a dataset taking the "[Quora Question Pairs](https://gluebenchmark.com/tasks)" and using Spacy to craft a "keyword" version of each question. To give you an example from it:

```
What is Morse code?	1
Morse code	0
What is the best backend for my app?	1
best backend app	0
```

Not bad, as a start, but I still haven't come to any _lean_ solution. Moreover, unless having some tricks applied to the classifier, this wouldn't be multilingual.

## Back to Pipelines: Binary/Dynamic Node.
Whatever you may call it, even if we _had_ a classifier, there's another feature we would need: a Pipeline node to handle the result of the classifier  **callable** and use it to point the Pipeline in the right direction of the graph. I think we could already submit a PR for this, @Threepointone4 kinda proposed it already, so along its idea, as a sketch:

```python
class BinaryNode:
    def __init__(self, node_a: str, node_b: str, evaluate: Callable):
        self.node_a = node_a
        self.node_b = node_b
        self.evaluate = evaluate
        self.outgoing_edges = 2
        ...
    
    def run(self, **kwargs):
        a = self.evaluate(**kwargs) # evaluate function returns a Bool
        return kwargs.get("query"), self.node_a if a else self.node_b
```

This opens some ideas about having the "evaluate" function itself defining the next node id, but this approach would have some drawbacks to consider. However, thing is the evaluating function (or classifier) is injected, and that's it. If you want to skip the reader or whatever else based on the time of the day, from the [starwars api](https://swapi.dev/) or whatever function you desire, the user can handle that himself. That could also work as a middle-ground solution until a proper QueryClassifier is implemented. When it is, it will just inherit from the BinaryNode, as a specialized version of it.

---

What do you think?'

            else:

    pipe = Pipeline()
    pipe.add_node(component=QueryClassifier(), name="QueryClassifier", inputs=["Query"])
    pipe.add_node(component=es_retriever, name="ESRetriever", inputs=["QueryClassifier.output_1"])
    pipe.add_node(component=dpr_retriever, name="DPRRetriever", inputs=["QueryClassifier.output_2"])
    pipe.add_node(component=JoinDocuments(join_mode="concatenate"), name="JoinResults",
                  inputs=["ESRetriever", "DPRRetriever"])
    pipe.add_node(component=reader, name="QAReader", inputs=["JoinResults"])
    res = p.run(question="What did Einstein work on?", top_k_retriever=1)
    print(res)
```

Title: b'RAG tutorial 7, how to detect wrong answer?'
Body:
b'**Question**
I just run the latest Tutorial 7 - Generative QA via "Retrieval-Augmented Generation": on [Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/tutorials/Tutorial7_RAG_Generator.ipynb).

It looks promising.

I just realised though that from the examples, the model would still return a wrong answer if the question is not covered in our docuement store. 

For example, we get:
Generated answer is ' india' for the question = 'panda is a national animal of which country'

We know that the answer should be China, not India. It looks to me as a "reverse allucination" of the model. There is nothing about the panda animal in the document store.

How can we detect that the questions are not covered by our document store? Do we have any probabilities we can use as a threshold, similar to what is provided by the extractive QA model when we get the answers? 
Shall we use the doc_scores as an indication, like any doc_scores that is below 80? 

Is there planning to add a "No answer" as a valid answer?

Thanks
'

Title: b'lalitpagaria'
Body:
b'I might be wrong due to limited knowledge, @tholor please correct me.

> How can we detect that the questions are not covered by our document store? Do we have any probabilities we can use as a threshold, similar to what is provided by the extractive QA model when we get the answers?
> Shall we use the doc_scores as an indication, like any doc_scores that is below 80?

You can use retriever returned documents for this purpose. Generator will always try to generate answer from retriever provided documents. Hence you can use doc_scores returned by retriever and filter if it is below certain threshold before feeding it to generator.

> Is there planning to add a "No answer" as a valid answer?

I think for this also same would be valid. If retriever does not return any docs then generator will not produce any answer.


As this is Retriever-Augmented Generator hence Retriever plays big role here. Fine tuning of question and generator encoder will produce good result as stated in original paper. But I feel by tweaking Retriever retrieved documents also one can achieve good result. 

Again I might be wrong and I answered based on my understanding of RAG when I was integrating it in the Haystack.  '

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @demarant ,

Very relevant question! I think it would be quite a helpful feature for the practical usage of RAG. However, I don't see a quick solution for this. I believe the original paper / implementation does not cover a "no answer" option. 

@lalitpagaria From my perspective, using the retriever scores is not really a good proxy here. The scores from DPR are rather reflecting a "higher-level" match of doc and query and will probably be to "blurry" for determining a "no answer". Secondly, RAG can still give correct answers even though the answer is not contained in the retrieved docs (e.g. when the answer is "remembered" from previous training). 

I could see two broad directions that might be worth exploring: 

1) Using the likelihood of the generated sequence (e.g. from beam search) or use a measure like perplexity

2) Training a separate, lightweight prediction head that determines the confidence level of the generated sequence

My gut feeling that 2) would give better calibrated scores and allows setting better thresholds to return no answer. 
We will work on model confidence (mostly for reader models) in Q1/Q2 next year. We can try to incorporate RAG there as well. If you want to explore this topic yourself in the meantime, we will try to give some light-weight support of course.'

Title: b'[Proposal] EmbeddingStore in Haystack'
Body:
b"Currently haystack have notion of DocumentStore (SQL, FAISS, Milvus, In-memory and ES).

These document stores can be classified in three categories -
- Pure document store (SQL and In-memory): Which store text and meta data. Querying is based on full text search.
- Pure embedding store (FAISS and Milvus): Which store text, meta data and embedding. Querying is based on vector search.
- Hybrid store (ES): Which store text, meta data and embedding (if used as embedding store). Querying is based on vector search as well as full text search or BM25.

Except ES store, all other store embedding in separately from document storage. So idea is to introduce notion of EmbeddingStore which will - 
- Sub class of BaseDocumentStore
- Have document_store as required parameter
- Embedding generation (Idea to keep embedding generation logic closer to Embedding store). User can customize generation logic based on their need.
- Document store operation will generate embedding, store embedding to it's store and write documents to document_store
- Searching operation will generate embedding of given query, query it's store to find vector_ids and then query document_store
- All operations like delete and update will flow from it's own storage and then to document_store

There will be three DocumentStores sub classes based on current implementation -
- SQL
- In-Memory
- ES

There will be three EmbeddingStores sub classes based on current available features -
- FAISS (Can support ES, SQL and in-memory document stores)
- Milvus (Can support ES, SQL and in-memory document stores)
- Sparse (Only support ES)

In future if haystack support weaviate, then it will be part of EmbeddingStore sub class.


Following pros and cons I can think of above proposal.

Pros -
- Separation of responsibilities between doc store and embedding store
- Embedding generation logic closer to the the storage
- User able to customise search logic easily
- User can use same document_store in separate pipeline and embedding store in another
- Easy to integrate other embedding stores
- ES also can be used with FIASS or Milvus

Cons -
- Direct update/delete on document_store will not reflect in embedding_store. Anyway now also able to do same by interacting directly to exact store like SQL. So we would need to introduce logic in doc store that if document data contains vector_id then print error or warning
- Confusion among user about purpose and use


I just shared my thought which I had since long time, and open for discussion about this proposal :)"

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @lalitpagaria , 

This is a very thoughtful suggestion and actually a topic that actually also came up in some discussions in our team in the last months. I thought about it quite a lot in the last days and discussed it with @oryx1729 . 

Let me try to summarize our key thoughts here: 

Pros: 
- Cleaner separation in the code
- Easier combination of new docstores and embeddingstores (e.g. allowing mongoDB + milvus)

Cons: 
- Significantly bigger test surface if we want to support all combinations
- If we don't support all combinations, it will be hard to document / explain what is possible and what not
- Optimization and benchmarking becomes more tricky - e.g. when we need to optimize FAISS for usage with SQL **and** Elasticsearch 
- Harder for the user to pick the "right" combination
- We believe the future is rather about hybrid stores (e.g. Elasticsearch + ANN plugin like in the open distro, weaviate ...) and we think for these hybrid stores the separation into docstores and embedding stores is rather confusing than helpful
- We haven't seen demand from the community for custom combinations like FAISS+elasticsearch yet. If this changes, and we see important use cases enabled by this direction, this would be an important game changer for this discussion.

All in all, we believe the value today is not really worth the costs (cons from above + implementation work). That's why we would not like to go down this road right now. Does this make sense for you? 

'

Title: b'lalitpagaria'
Body: b"@tholor Yes agree with you as it is big ticket item also involve educating community about new naming.\r\nSo let's close it for now, we can revisit this in future based on need. WDYT?"

Title: b'tholor'
Body: b"Yes, let's close it for now and if we see more evidence for need from the community we can reconsider it :)"

Title: b'Simplify usage of confidence scores & add documentation'
Body:
b'With # we introduced an option to get more reliable confidence scores for predictions from a QA model / reader. 

So far the usage in Haystack seems not well documented and calibrating scores is not easily accessible. 
Calibration would probably look something like this: 

```
    evaluator_dev = Evaluator(
        data_loader=data_silo.get_data_loader("dev"),
        tasks=data_silo.processor.tasks,
        device=device
    )
    result_dev = evaluator_dev.eval(model, return_preds_and_labels=True, calibrate_conf_scores=True)

```

Or you set it manually to:
```
model.prediction_heads[0].temperature_for_confidence
```

Proposed changes:
1. Let's simplify the calibration by introducing a new "high-level" method in FARMReader (e.g. `calibrate_confidence_scores()`)
2. Let's update documentation so that more users are aware of this functionality (doc strings, but also adding an example either somewhere in the "usage section" or in one of the existing tutorials)
'

Title: b'brandenchan'
Body:
b"Hi @LivingDeadCloud , thanks for the question. To give a rough overview, we can classify questions into a few different categories:
- `extractive` (the model is expected to return a span of text that answers the question)
- `no_answer` (the model is expected to say that no answer to the question can be found)
- `yes / no` (the model is expected to answer yes or no to a question)

Most QA models are trained on the SQuAD dataset. SQuAD 1.0 has only `extractive` questions. SQuAD 2.0 has both `extractive` and `no_answer` questions. There is a dataset called [Natural Questions](https://ai.google.com/research/NaturalQuestions) which also features `yes / no` answers on top of the other two. 

Our transfer learning framework FARM has a [basic tutorial](https://github.com/deepset-ai/FARM/blob/master/examples/natural_questions.py) on how to train such a model. This would probably be a good starting point for what you're after! I do need to point out however that we are currently reworking a lot of our preprocessing steps which means that NQ may be somewhat unstable. It's already been pointed out [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/FARM/issues/739). You may need to revert to an earlier FARM version in order to get it all to run.

Let us know how you get on with this. Happy to guide you through later steps and help with any problems that come up!"

Title: b'Simplify evaluation for filtered search cases (e.g. product search)'
Body:
b'A search query in Haystack's retriever-reader pipeline can run "globally" against all docs or only on a filtered subset. 

However, when we run eval we usually do it globally, i.e. running a set of questions without filters, comparing predictions with gold answers and returning metrics. 
When you want to run eval for something like product search, where your pairs of question and gold answers are closely tight to a product, this eval is not ideal and manual adjustments are needed. 

Let's simplify this. One rough idea would be along the lines of adding metadata to our label objects and use this for filtering the queries at eval time. 

Probably also related to #https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/1030 where we want to aggregate single labels to multi labels in a more meaningful way.'

Title: b'Double Check Milvus Benchmark Results'
Body:
b'When the speed benchmarks are run using `haystack/test/benchmarks/run.py`, the results of DPR with FAISS and Milvus seem to diverge quite significantly. 

When initializing the HNSW models, we have tried to align the parameters so they are comparable.

```
FAISS HNSW
n_links = 64
efSearch = 20
efConstruction = 80

Milvus HNSW
index_param = {"M": 64, "efConstruction": 80}
search_param = {"ef": 20}
```


The number below show queries per second given a certain document store, when loaded with a certain number of documents.

 | FAISS Flat | FAISS HNSW | Milvus Flat | Milvus HNSW
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
1000 | 40.41 | 44.32 | 40.48 | 40.39
10000 | 28.03 | 42.12 | 38.13 | 38.15
100000 | 6.62 | 40.68 | 28.30 | 28.08
500000 | 1.54 | 39.43 | 15.30 | 24.50


While Milvus Flat seems significantly faster than FAISS Flat, Milvus HNSW does not match the near constant speed that FAISS HNSW has. It is currently unclear to us what the expected speed profile of each Document Store should be like. For reference, here are the mAP scores for the same configurations.

 | FAISS Flat | FAISS HNSW | Milvus Flat | Milvus HNSW
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
1000 | 92.95 | 92.95 | 92.95 | 92.95
10000 | 89.87 | 89.50 | 89.87 | 89.87
100000 | 86.55 | 84.33 | 86.55 | 86.55
500000 | 80.86 | 75.73 | 80.86 | 74.86

Here it shows that Milvus HNSW matches the Flat performance exactly at 1k, 10k and 100k. Only at 500k does the performance diverge.

We should figure out what the expected performance of each DocumentStore is and configure each so that they are directly comparable.

A [question](https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus/discussions/4939) has been raised in Milvus Github discussions'

b'This is placeholder ticket to discuss ideas about improving SQL stores bulk insert performance.
If we see various document stores [benchmarks](https://haystack.deepset.ai/bm/benchmarks), SQL based store have very low indexing speed. Let's discuss how to achieve it.

Few idea which I have are -
1. Use SQLAlchemy Core insert/update instead of ORM. Refer [link](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11769366/why-is-sqlalchemy-insert-with-sqlite-25-times-slower-than-using-sqlite3-directly) for more benchmark.
2. Incorporate few ideas from this [article](https://towardsdatascience.com/3-data-backed-ways-to-significantly-speed-up-your-mysql-bulk-inserts-28e20b42d51e) specially regular `commit` and lazy indexing.
3. For faiss and milvus store, write embedding to FAISS and doc to SQL in parallel. In order to achieve this first we need to generate vector_ids ourself and use to write both embedding and doc in parallel. For Flat index we would need to add IDMap as well refer [link](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/wiki/The-index-factory#prefixes) and for milvus refer [link](https://milvus.io/docs/v1.1.0/product_faq.md#should-i-specify-entity-ids-when-importing-vectors-or-have-milvus-generate-them-for-me).
4. [Just hunch so not sure] Insert meta after document insertion step and do it in background. As these store does not support filtering so first inserting document to make document store available for query would be good tread off while a background process continue inserting meta data.
5. Try alternative of UUID and ways to use integer primary keys. Refer [link](https://www.percona.com/blog/2019/11/22/uuids-are-popular-but-bad-for-performance-lets-discuss/) for more details.

**"Show me the benchmarks": Any implementation/PR should have supporting benchmarks **'

Title: b'Reader evaluation merges questions with the same text'
Body:
b'**Describe the bug**
Some QA datasets are review-based (e.g. [AmazonQA](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.04364) and [SubjQA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.14283)), where the question-answer pairs concern the reviews about a _single_ product. What can happen in these datasets is that the question _text_ can be the same for _different_ products, e.g. in SubjQA the question "What do you think about headphone?" is asked about two different products.  

This duplicity of question text produces inflated EM/F1 scores when using `FARMReader.eval` for evaluation because the question text is used as a key for aggregation [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/32050fdce3cc6d55ed744e2475b8c2dcee2edd4b/haystack/reader/farm.py#L498), so the number of potential answers to match with increases. 

For reasons I don't fully understand, a similar effect is seen for `FARMReader.eval_on_file`, e.g. evaluating `deepset/minilm-uncased-squad2` on the test set of the `electronics` domain of SubjQA I find:

```
{'EM': 0.25139664804469275,
 'f1': 0.32950102625485156,
 'top_n_accuracy': 0.7597765363128491}
```
whereas the scores shown in the publication are closer to EM = 0.06 and F1 = 0.23 (Figs. 5 & 7). 


**Error message**
None (silent bug)

**Expected behavior**
* Merge questions by their unique ID instead of their text. 
* Be able to evaluate `FARMReader` on review-based datasets.

**Additional context**
Evaluating the Retriever-Reader pipeline for review-based datasets is not currently supported "out-of-the-box" by #904  because one needs to first filter the Retriever for a product ID, calculate the EM/F1 scores per product, and then aggregate to get the overall scores for the pipeline. 

I am not sure whether the use case is common enough to warrant a change to the API, but allowing users to evaluate e.g. the `ExtractiveQAPipeline` on a subset of the data (via a filter) would be welcome  

**To Reproduce**
See this Colab notebook: https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1K00ut8_E4GuLS-xk4f_JRJdyRwGNATsO?usp=sharing

**System:**
 - OS: Whatever Colab runs :)
 - GPU/CPU: GPU
 - Haystack version (commit or version number): 0.7.0
 - DocumentStore: Elasticsearch
 - Reader: FARMReader 
 - Retriever: Elasticsearch (BM25)
'

Title: b'What is the difference between the formula for recall for retriever and the formula for top n accuracy for reader?'
Body:
b"**Question**
What is the difference between the formula for recall for retriever and the formula for top n accuracy for reader?

**Additional context**
It seems that the underlying formula for both is the same. For each question we check if a correct answer (or document containing the answer) is in the top k, we mark false or true correspondingly. Then we compute the percentage of questions for which we have the value true. If there isn't any difference, I think perhaps the better name for this metric is top k accuracy? 

@psorianom @Rob192 FYI  
"

Title: b'Timoeller'
Body:
b'Hey @nyxpho good question, both metrics are somewhat similar though there is a difference in granularity. Recall is for retrievers retrieving documents, top n accuracy is for readers producing short, precise answers.

**Recall for retriever** is 1 if anywhere in the document the correct answer is located (= correct document retrieved)
**Top n accuracy** is 1 if the granular QA model prediction (a few words, numbers, etc) has any overlap with the correct answer (= correct answer produced)

'

Title: b'nyxpho'
Body: b'Thank you for the answer, @Timoeller ! And when we have more than one document (for retriever)/answer (for reader), we say that for that question we have 1 if any of the documents retrieved contains the answer, or if any of the answers have an overlap with the correct answer? I was confused, as especially the recall metric seems to be exactly the same as top k accuracy as defined for classification in scikit learn.'

Title: b'Timoeller'
Body:
b'Exactly : )

For recall@10 you look if any of the first 10 retrieved documents is correct.
For Top-3-Accuracy you look at the first (most likely) 3 QA model predictions and if they overlap with the answer label.'

Title: b'nyxpho'
Body: b'Thank you for the clarification! Together with @Rob192 , @psorianom, @AbdenourCh  we were considering adding more metrics and doing a pull requests.  Would that be something interesting for you? \r\nIn particular we want to add for the retriever mean reciprocal rank, mean P@k, mean R@k and mean F1@k. \r\nFor the reader, I think it can be interesting also to consider the position in which the correct answer appears (or part of the correct answer) - which is currently not captured if I understand correctly - is it the first answer, the second and so on. So it might make sense to have the mean reciprocal rank, but where we check the position of the first answer which has partial overlap with the correct answer - or if we want to be more strict, which is an exact match. '

Title: b'Timoeller'
Body:
b'Hey sure, contributions are always welcome!
There is already an issue with very good ideas about additional retrieval metrics: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/925

About additional Reader metrics, I think if you create something completely new you will have to educate and introduce it a lot. Currently we are thinking a lot about softer metrics than EM, f1 or even TopkAcc. We would be interested in something that works on a semantic level like https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.09675.pdf but for comparing answers.

Title: b'Weaviate as a Knowledge Graph'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Leverage Weaviate as a Knowledge Graph.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Haystack supports knowledge graph using GraphDB. Don't know enough about the future direction for KG in haystack, however this could be a useful addition.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Weaviate brings in semantic learning with its vector based approach. It uses class hierarchy to build relationships between entities. This could be a powerful when compared to traditional graphs.

**Additional context**
Once Weaviate is integrated as a document store, it can be extended as a knowledge graph."

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body:
b'Hi @venuraja79 Thank you for brining this up.  Currently, haystack's knowledge graph functionality is limited to GraphDB, knowledge stored in the form of triples (subject, predicate, object), and SPARQL queries that can either be created manually or automatically translated from natural language questions.
I had a [brief](https://www.semi.technology/developers/weaviate/current/more-resources/faq.html) [look](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50063202/what-is-the-difference-between-graphql-and-sparql/50068361) at Weaviate and it seems to me that this is very different: we would not use SPARQL but GraphQL to query Weaviate.
Another related challenge that I see is that the data in Weaviate requires a schema as in this [example](https://www.semi.technology/developers/weaviate/current/tutorials/how-to-create-a-schema.html). You are right that using class hierarchies to build/"semantically understand" relationships between entities would be more powerful than traditional graphs, e.g., our GraphDB triple store. However, that's also the reason why it could not be combined with haystack's current graph features. I think that the power of these triple stores is that we can automatically fill them with knowledge by extracting triples from text without manually creating a schema. With Weaviate we would rely on manually creating a schema, which would make sense for a large corpus of documents with the same structure but not so much for unstructured texts, do you agree?
Do you have any particular use case in mind? Something that did not work well with other document stores in haystack? I am curious to understand your idea and motivation better!'

Title: b'venuraja79'
Body: b"Thank you @julian-risch for your thoughts on this. I see that Weaviate's schema requirement as a limitation in this case.\r\nI raised this because #957 Haystack will support weaviate as a document store in future and may be able to leverage it as a graph also. No other use cases in mind currently. Thank you!"

Title: b'julian-risch'

Let's wait for the pull request and see what functionality it provides: https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/pull/1064 It's definitely a cool idea to query the new WeaviateDocumentStore with GraphQL. For now, I'd say we wait and see whether we come across a use case that would benefit from having a Weaviate-based knowledge graph in haystack. If it's okay with you, I would close this issue for now but please feel free to reopen it, if there is more to discuss. Maybe learnings from the pull request will help to discuss advantages and disadvantages in the near future. Thanks again for bringing this topic to our attention! Much appreciated!"

Title: b'Improve handling of duplicate documents during write_documents()'
Body:
b"**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In #1000 we introduced a hashing mechanism that creates the file id depending on document content (default: the text).

The current behaviour:  

If you call  `write_documents()` with a batch of documents and one of them is already existing in the document_store (determined by the ID), the request is failing:

Memory store - ValueError
ES based store - Throw BulkIndexError
SQL based store - Throw IntegrityError exception because of UNIQUE constraint



**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add an argument `handle_duplicates` to `write_documents()` that allows users to change the behavior in case of duplicates:
 
- Ignore duplicate (with warning) - Default option
- Overwrite if exist
- Fail if duplicate

In all cases write_documents should return inserted document ids (same in case of rest API). So the user knows what was written and what was skipped.

Ideally, we also make the thrown exceptions more consistent across document stores. "

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @F95GIT , 

Sure, that's possible. It should work pretty similarly to the "multiple retriever examples" in the docs.
Let me try to give you some pointers: 

1) Route Query (Run only one branch)
```
    class QueryClassifier():
        outgoing_edges = 2

        def run(self, **kwargs):
            # you can put here some rule or fast classification model
            if "?" in kwargs["query"]:
                return (kwargs, "output_1")
            else:
                return (kwargs, "output_2")

    pipe = Pipeline()
    pipe.add_node(component=QueryClassifier(), name="QueryClassifier", inputs=["Query"])
    pipe.add_node(component=dpr_retriever, name="DPRRetriever", inputs=["QueryClassifier.output_1"])
    pipe.add_node(component=reader, name="QAReader", inputs=["DPRRetriever"])
    pipe.add_node(component=embedding_retriever, name="FAQRetriever", inputs=["QueryClassifier.output_2"])
    res = p.run(query="What did Einstein work on?", top_k_retriever=1)
```

2) Combine results (Run both branches)
Ideally we should be able to define some pipeline like this: 
```
p = Pipeline()
#extractive branch
p.add_node(component=dpr_retriever, name="DPRRetriever", inputs=["Query"])
p.add_node(component=reader, name="QAReader", inputs=["DPRRetriever"])
#faq branch
p.add_node(component=embedding_retriever, name="EmbeddingRetriever", inputs=["Query"])
#TODO add conversion node "Docs2Answers"
p.add_node(component=JoinAnswers(join_mode="concatenate"), name="JoinResults", inputs=["EmbeddingRetriever", "QAReader"])
res = p.run(query="What did Einstein work on?", top_k_retriever=1)
```
However, I just realized, that the FAQPipeline has one extra step needed to convert the retrieved documents into proper "answers" (see code [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/32050fdce3cc6d55ed744e2475b8c2dcee2edd4b/haystack/pipeline.py#L469)). This is needed, as both branches in the pipeline need to pass lists of `Answer` to the `JoinAnswers`  node. Hi, if I want to build an FAQ retrieval system in the same fashion as you demonstrated in Tutorial 4. I initialized a FAISS document store without specifying any SQL DB. So, I have a few questions:

Title: b'lalitpagaria'
Body:
b"
> 1. Do I need to use a SQL DB at all?

Yes

> 2. Do columns need to have certain names in the SQL DB?

Document store will need three tables: `document`, `meta` and `label` with schema mentioned in https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/document_store/sql.py
So if SQL DB already have it then document store will not create it otherwise it will create automatically.

> 3. Shall the SQL DB have defined a column for storing the embedding, or would I store the embeddings in another object?

FAISS document store do not store embedding in SQL DB. It kept in FAISS index usually in memory (refer https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss)

> 4. Where can I save the index in a production environment so that I don't have to re-index the DB every time I add a new entry in the DB?

You can use [`save()`](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/document_store/faiss.py#L328) and [`load()`](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/haystack/document_store/faiss.py#L338) to save and retrieve embedding stored in FAISS index respectively. 
Other data reside with SQL DB which is already persistent. 

> 
> **Additional context**
> I tried to search some code examples in the documentation about connecting a SQL DB in the FAISS document store, but I couldn't find much.

See if this https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/tutorials/Tutorial6_Better_Retrieval_via_DPR.ipynb help you."

Title: b'tanaysoni'
Body:
b'Hi @AMChierici, 

> what would you suggest for the SQL db structure if I have different sets of documents to search? Is the only solution to create a separate DB for each knowledge base?

Do you want to make queries across multiple knowledge bases? If the queries are always made to a single knowledge base, then you can use the `index` parameter when writing to the `SQLDocumentStore`. Each knowledge base must be assigned a different `index`. With the changes from #812, now a new FAISS instance will be created for each `index`(knowledge base).

If you want to have the option for making queries across multiple knowledge bases, the `ElasticsearchDocumentStore` could be a better fit. You can set the name of the knowledge base as a meta field in documents that can later be used when querying.

>  I want to update only the last one I inserted in the db.

With #812, now you can set `update_existing_embeddings` parameter to False when calling `update_embeddings()`.  '

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @mlnlpenthusiast ,

Welcome to the Haystack community :) . Happy to support: 

> Issue 1: The process take very long time . More than a hour for creating embedding and prediction

This seems indeed extremely slow and unusual. Can you share some more details please: 
- Do you split the docs into smaller chunks before adding them to the `document_store` (see [documentation](https://haystack.deepset.ai/docs/latest/preprocessingmd#PreProcessor))?   
- What environment do you run this on? CPU / GPU? OS?
- What version of Haystack and FARM are you running?
- Can you share any code so that we can reproduce it? 

> Issue 2: Prediction takes long as well and creates multiple processes

I would recommend not using the large model `bert-large-uncased-whole-word-masking-finetuned-squad`, but rather a [RoBERTa](https://huggingface.co/deepset/roberta-base-squad2) or [MiniLM](https://huggingface.co/deepset/minilm-uncased-squad2) variant. They are more than 2x faster while having a similar range of accuracy in most domains (see our [benchmarks](https://haystack.deepset.ai/bm/benchmarks)).

> This step also takes several minutes to a hour depending on number of documents.

Just for loading the components :scream: ?  Or are you again calling `update_embeddings()`? Would be helpful to understand what exact step takes so long here (e.g. model loading vs. DocumentStore loading)


> I also noticed that during prediction, there are number of streamlit processes running (20-30)

We use multiprocessing for the preprocessing in FARMReader. You can disable it via setting `FARMReader(num_processes=0))` ([documentation](https://haystack.deepset.ai/docs/latest/apireadermd#Class-FARMReader)) or in the REST API via the ENV  `MAX_PROCESSES` (see [here](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/master/rest_api/config.py#L10)) 
In addition, it might depend on how you run the REST API. Are you running via gunicorn using multiple workers?
'

Title: b'Timoeller'
Body:
b'Hey thanks for posting more tests.

## Prerequisite
As haystack-pipeline you used a `TransformersReader` and your custom pipeline is the `DlModelDocumentAndQuestion`?

## Possible Solution
So I looked at your method in modelRun() and it doesnt really aggregate the answer in the way that Transformers or FARM does. You use:
```
  answer_tokens = all_tokens[torch.argmax(start_scores) :torch.argmax(end_scores)+1]
```
Huggingface Transformers as well as FARM compute the best joint score of both start and end scores. For this FARM constructs a 2D matrix of start and end scores and selects the best combination.
I guess This could be the difference in mem consumption, especially when you use longformer on very long documents, the square matrix of start and end scores becomes very large.'

Title: b'julian-risch'
Body: b'Hi @Threepointone4 I would recommend to use a longer text sequence as context and not only a short text that supports the answer. First, "qas" is a list and could contain multiple questions that can be answered given the context. Therefore, the context would also need to "support" answers for multiple questions and not only a single answer for a single question. A second reason is that if you would like to use the data for training or evaluation, a shorter context might make the question answering task to easy for the model. As a result, the model might not learn enough from you training data and your evaluation on your dataset will look good but as soon as you use longer texts (at inference time), performance will drop significantly.\r\nIf you are interested, you could have a look at the original SQuAD 2.0 dataset here: https://rajpurkar.github.io/SQuAD-explorer/explore/v2.0/dev/Normans.html In this example, the context is rather long and contains the answers to multiple questions. Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @Prabhav55221 , 

Sure, that is possible. 

If I understand your use case correctly, there are three things that you want to save: 

1) Reader model (Albert XXL)

Just call `reader.save(Path("some-file-path"))`. You can later load this local model by simply calling `FARMReader('some-file-path')`

2) DPR model
Similar to above: `retriever.save('some path')`

3) Embeddings for your docs  

The embeddings are stored together with your docs in your DocumenStore after you called `update_embeddings()`. So persisting them depends on your choice of the DocumentStore. Are you using Elasticsearch here? If yes, your embeddings will be persisted in your elasticsearch instance. You can also make sure to only update "missing" embeddings by calling `update_embeddings(update_existing_embeddings=False')` '

Title: b'tholor'
Body: b'Regarding the "empty" answers: This is the way the model represents a "No answers found". This can be helpful in scenarios where you want to avoid returning an answer in every case - even when the model is very uncertain. You can configure the sensitivity for this, i.e. how often the no answer option is returned, via the param `no_ans_boost` in the FARMReader or completely disable it via `return_no_answers`. '

The REST API relies on Elasticsearch as the underlying [document store](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack#components). Do you already have Elasticsearch running locally on your machine? If not, a good place to get started with Haystack is the [tutorial 1](https://github.com/BNkosi/haystack/blob/master/tutorials/Tutorial1_Basic_QA_Pipeline.py). Title: b'brandenchan'
Body:
b'Hi @sophgit, cool to see you're already using the new evaluation nodes!

So I do expect a difference in Retriever eval stats when run using `Retriever.eval()` vs a `EvalRetriever` node but actually I would have expected `Retriever.eval()` to do worse. The reason is that `Retriever.eval()` is doing a **Closed Domain** retrieval evaluation, meaning that a successful retrieval is based on whether the right document is retrieved (this is judged using the document's ID). The `EvalRetriever` node is actually an **Open Domain** retrieval. A document is considered correctly retrieved as long as the answer string is contained within the retrieved document, and we don't check its ID. 

**Open Domain** retrieval is easier than **Closed Domain** so I actually would have expected the opposite results to what you posted. Down the line, we will want to implement **Closed Domain** in the Eval nodes. 

For now, we should definitely look into this problem to see what is going wrong. Currently it seems like you are using a different dataset to what is in the tutorial, which makes this a little bit tricky. But to start, maybe you could help us out by looking a little more closely at the Retriever's predictions in each case.

For the Retriever only case, could you try adding the `return_preds=True` argument?
i.e. `res = retriever.eval(return_preds=True)`
`res` is now a dictionary and `res["predictions"]` returns the predictions of the retriever.

For the Evaluation Nodes case, add `debug=True` when initializing the `EvalRetriever`
i.e. `eval_retriever = EvalRetriever(debug=True)`
After running the evaluation, `eval_retriever.log` will return all the retriever's predictions.

If you are able to compare the results from each and see which samples differ, that could be really informative for us! '

Title: b'tholor'
Body:
b'Hey @MathiasKrill , 

Happy to tackle your questions one by one: 

> Is this big time diffrence expected? I bypassed this problem by splitting pdf's into single pages what speeded up
the search in the past by far. This helped with 80-pages documents in the past for example. - Is there any other trick?

This seems too long. In general you have three levers to increase speed: 
**a) Model size**
 -> Try a smaller model. You are using an electra-large model here. electra-base or even better miniLm or distilbert would be faster. See our benchmarks for speed differences. For German, the options are still a bit limited, but see my comment below for some hope on the horizon. We just published `deepset/gelectra-base-germanquad` ;) 
**b) Document length** 
The more text you feed to the reader model, the slower it gets. You can either reduce `top_k_retriever` (less documents passed to the reader) or change the document splitting options (shorter documents passed to the reader). See our [docs](https://haystack.deepset.ai/docs/latest/optimizationmd) for details about this. In your case, you could for example pass `split_by="word"`and `split_length= 200` in the file_upload request to diverge from the default values here. 
**c) GPU**
For production, I would always recommend running on a GPU (I suppose you use a CPU here?). You can gain easily > 30x speedups.

---------------------------

> Filename in the answer is now a uui "document_id" - how to get the filename?

One option is to add it as meta data while uploading the file to the rest API (similar to your "author" and "year"). Currently only our utility function `convert_files_to_dicts()` does this automatically behind the scenes for you. This function is however only accessible from pure python code (not in pipelines in rest API). (CC @tanaysoni: we should change that)

----------------------------------

> Is there a meanwhile better german model than "Sahajtomar/GELECTRAQA" ?

It's not publicly announced yet, but you can already have a sneak peek at our[ new german models](https://huggingface.co/models?search=germanquad) trained on a custom, hand annotated dataset gathered over the last months. The paper, dataset, and announcement will follow soon :) 

Hope this helps! '

Title: b'Update Embeddings in FAISS'
Body: b'In the `FAISSDocumentStore`, the `update_embeddings()` has a parameter `update_existing_embeddings` to decide if existing embeddings get overwritten. Since the current implementation of FAISS do not allow updating existing embeddings, we should ensure that the FAISS index must get reset when `update_existing_embeddings` is set to `True`.\r\n\r\nAdditionally, ensure that `filters` must only select documents that do not have an embedding. Otherwise, it could result in the FAISS Index having more embeddings than the number of documents.'
